Input: What are the wrong depictions of the US in Hollywood movies? When I think of a Hollywood movie that is far removed from any possible spectrum of realism, this movie always comes to my mind. You can tell by just watching the poster that this is going to be another formulaic family movie; the white background which signifies that this movie will have no content, dialogue or subplot other than this generic couple and their darned dog, the smiling figures staring at you almost sinisterly, the tepid humour of a puppy leading the couple by leash. “A dog leading its masters by leash?…….. that's so clever and ironic!” Sarcasms and cynicisms aside, here are the reasons why this movie is not just a wrong depiction of US life but an offense to ordinary people who tighten their belt and blue collar while slaving it on the 9 to 5. 1. Raising a dog = good practice for raising children, according to this movie. The above image perfectly captures how stupid that notion is. No one would watch a photo like this and and say that this is evidence of good parental skills. Besides feeding and caring there is nothing remotely similar to raising dogs as compared to children. This is a notion you tend to see solely in Hollywood movies where raising children can be condescended to the same level as keeping a litter of puppies. Raising good children, especially for poorer parents, is practically a lifelong sacrifice and the ultimate moral contract. Giving up your youth, freedom and finances and being willing to shield your child from incoming physical harm or even death is not the same as a bowl of Kibbles n Bits and a scratch on the tummy. 2. Every middle class American lives in a mansion on a sprawling well-kept spread of land. Owen Wilson and Jennifer Aniston's characters are ordinary reporters with two kids. She becomes a stay at home mom which makes him the breadwinner. His highest paying position is at The Philadelphia Inquirer which, according to online research, currently has an average annual salary of $60,000. This would mean that his monthly salary would've been around $5000 give or take. This 16 acre five bedroom Pennsylvania farmhouse had a selling price of $1.25 million in 2011. Using a mortgage calculator based on local interest rates at the time his payment for the house would’ve been roughly $5800 per month based on a 30 year loan repayment. So in other words, for the family to have realistically lived such a lifestyle, Jennifer Aniston's character had to have employed some means of soliciting tax-free money at night. 3. Let's all shed tears……. A dog has died of old age. This was the moment that was the straw that broke the camel's back. We ejected the DVD in sheer annoyance and frustration at this point. The dog died……a natural death. Cue sad music and flashbacks. How entitled can your country be if the natural death of a dog can elicit tears from an audience? A pet dog in Trinidad is lucky to live past 8 years, even in the best of care. My own backyard where I grew up contains the remains of over a dozen unfortunate cats and canines who died prematurely due to illness, speeding cars and just plain bad luck. We had not a single pet that died of natural causes i.e. old age. If we did, we would have celebrated its life and the fact that it led a full life. This supposed tearjerking scene was just another alienating Hollywoodism that highlights how out of touch the film industry is. What an awful movie full of delusional perceptions of the average American life. Don't watch it.

Have you ever witnessed an office prank that cost someone their job? I may be cheating a bit but I can't help to answer such a burning question. I performed a prank that could've cost me my job. In my late teens I worked in a warehouse doing manual labor which mostly included picking up boxes of products, placing them on a trolley and bringing them to the front to be delivered. It could sometimes be rather monotonous especially when the huge orders came in and you spent all day rolling about the massive double warehouse in your creaky trolley that always had one bad wheel. Jason (or J as he preferred to be called) was our supervisor. He was a muscular guy with a deadpan face and shiny bald head. He was the butt of many of our jokes because he spoke in this forced, psudo-sexy whisper and constantly licked his lips while giving his daily inspirational morning speeches (we would call him LL Cool J in secret). He didn't have much of a sense of humour. He barely ever smiled and no one saw him laugh, although one of my friends claimed to have seen him laughing at an episode of Rugrats while behind his office computer. Anyways. As I mentioned the job could be monotonous. One evening I saw that one of the older female workers, Erica, had written on the bulletin board. 'I love my fellow workers.’ This irritated me because it was not a bulletin and it had an air of Soviet Communism about it. I wanted to change it to 'I love my fellow COMRADES' and draw a hammer and sickle but I knew that most of my coworkers wouldn't get the joke and it would be ignored. In the end I decided to change it to 'I love my fellow SLAVES.’ That would catch their attention and provide a good laugh and then it would be erased and teach Erica to stop using the bulletin board to write her insipid, brown-nosed statements. Unbeknownst to me J, who was of African descent, was in the process of watching all the episodes of Roots on DVD. He was emotionally charged about African history and slavery in particular. It didn't even occur to me that he was wearing a lot of African themed clothing also. The next morning I arrived just in time for the morning prayer and J's speech. The atmosphere was like a funeral as I entered the warehouse and saw everyone staring at me. J, in a low growl, asked me if I was the one who wrote the slave comment on the board. I replied yes. J licked his lips and made a long, impassioned plea about slavery and black pride. Every time I tried to explain to him that I didn't mean it in a context of race he would say, 'Shut up Jumbo (my nickname).’ He then ended by saying in his low psudo-sexy LL Cool J voice, 'Don't you ever………..ever, ever………let me see you write anything racist on this board again.’ Had I not been of African descent myself I'm certain I would've been put on extended probation, let go or at least spoken to by HR. My friends enjoyed the whole ordeal and it made good scuttlebutt for a few days. I never touched the bulletin board again but being the best impersonator of J, I was sought after by my friends and coworkers to re-enact J's racism speech. I would do a perfect impersonation with exaggerated licking lips and have them howling with laughter. Unfortunately I was called into Js office some time later. I was in trouble. Someone snitched to J that I was mocking how he spoke. I was certain now I would get the boot. Instead I saw J with a big smile on his face watching on his phone a video of me impersonating him. 'Jumbo,' he said and then licked his lips, 'Let me see you talk like me.’ I looked at him and repeated what he just said, licked lips and all. To my surprise he simply smiled and gave a soft 'he he he’ laugh and told me to go back to work and stop fooling around. He did have a sense of humour after all. Myself with some friends at the warehouse. J wasn't present unfortunately.

Which TV shows were popular when you were younger that would flop today? Why? Oh man. There are so many shows from the 90s that would flop hard had they been released (as they were) today. These two shows ruled daytime television for a long time in the mid 90s. I think one of the reasons for the success of the two interrelated shows is the fact that they were different and there was nothing else on. These weren't the days of Netflix, streaming, 4K/HD, watch at your own pace, high production value but limited seasons/episodes, hundreds of options to choose from high speed internet TV. These were the days of ‘Damn I missed my show’ cable television, paper TV guides, one new show every few months, low budget production with endless episodes and seasons etc. These were the days of ‘take what you can get’ on TV. HERCULES: THE LEGENDARY JOURNEYS Hercules is this chill, alpha-jock type guy who roams around New Zealand (wearing the same Super V-neck goatskin vest and tight leather pants every day) meeting nice quirky villagers of whom he saves from various villains ranging from petty con-men to full blown freakish monsters. At his side is a short, blond, surfer-dude like Iolaus who is the comic relief character. This is the premise for practically every episode. The show is supposedly set in ancient Greece yet don't be surprised to find English knights, Chinese peasants, Japanese ninjas, Nordic Vikings, Mongolian warlords, Egyptian Pharaohs or any cool and exciting historical anachronism discovered randomly during Hercules’ wanderings. The always well-shaved Kevin Sorbo would never break a sweat or mess up his lovely long hair in fights. Everything always worked out well in the end for Hercules, Iolaus and the villagers and if things got truly icky then you know it would take a second or third episode for the villain to be destroyed or for Iolaus/a love interest/a child to recover from near death. XENA: WARRIOR PRINCESS It’s pretty much the same thing except the leads are women. Xena (previously a minor Hercules villain on the show) atones for her past by going around saving helpless villagers with the aid of her short, blond quirky bard Gabrielle and the village idiot Joxer. Unlike Hercules, Xena had more personality and a rather interesting ‘Ay ya ya ya ya’ war cry accompanied with more of a focus on action scenes rather than Hercules’ constant spew of Dad jokes. The show became far more popular than its predecessor and ran from 1995 - 2001 whereas Hercules began in 1995 as well and ended 1999. Comparing these two shows with the crop of fantasy shows that are available now is definitely a chalk and cheese comparison. Take a look at the following screenshots. Now take a look at various people doing Hercules and Xena cosplay: You can barely tell the difference! Historically inaccurate clothing, easily accessible and cheap to film ‘forest’ backgrounds, pampered hairstyles, anachronisms galore, Hercules: The Legendary Journeys and Xena: Warrior Princess were nothing more than glorified cosplay. If either show were released today, as they were, they would be a source for ridicule and memes. However if I can give one positive comment for the show I would have to say that it doesn’t try to secretly force any message down my throat. Xena is a woman who kicks ass. She is not a feminist and definitely not a lesbian as that lame rumour suggests. Hercules doesn’t spout any subtle parables promoting socialism or taxing the wealthy. There is no powerful and evil villain that looks and acts like Trump (or Bob Dole to be more precise with the time). The show is silly and stupid and doesn’t promote any type of political activism. So I’d definitely watch Xena or Hercules over Rings of Power and She-Hulk any time, any day.

What was a red flag that made you stop talking to a person immediately? My brother had a relative staying over at his apartment and she brought along a friend. They both had just turned 18 and had recently run off from home (Red Flag #1) and were crashing at my brother's place basically sleeping all day and partying all night to their teenaged wont. I struck up a conversation with the friend (let's just call her Alice for simplicity's sake) and found her quite intelligent and charming despite her lifestyle. Went with Alice to hang out one night and we ended up in a club. We began dancing but I was quite surprised how physically close she positioned herself while we danced as we had only just met a week ago (Red Flag #2). I then asked her about how it was staying with my brother and she began a slew of insults as towards my brother's manners and housekeeping standards (Red Flag #3) despite the fact that she didn't help with his bills or rent. We exchanged numbers and I dropped her off home. She laid on her charm quite thick the entire journey and spoke of how great of a guy I was and that she couldn't wait for us to chat again. We exchanged numbers and the following morning I called her to see how she was doing. In a groggy voice she said ‘Who is this?’ I told her my name and to my surprise she said in a irritated tone, ‘Who? How did you get my number?’ (Red Flag #4) I reminded her that she gave me her number willingly the night before. She tried to laugh it off as being hung over. I reminded her that she only had one drink last night (Red Flag #5). There was an awkward silence and she tried to coo about how great of a guy I was but I cut her short and said that I was getting another call. Three years later Alice got pregnant for her boyfriend's married boss.

Which supporting actress was much more memorable than the star of a movie? Toni Collette gave one of the greatest performances ever rendered on film in the soon to be cult classic Hereditary (2018) but another actress outshined her by a fraction of a fraction. Ann Dowd gave a most chillingly deceptive performance of Joan, a warm and empathetic older lady who befriends Collette's character Annie as she struggles with tragedy, resentment and depression. The beauty of Ann's performance is her complex nuances. She transforms from a lovable, nurturing Aunt May type character that was so understated yet genuinely compassionate to a different being one would've never predicted her to be near the ending. The most common description I've heard about her character for those who've enjoyed the film is how 'real’ Joan seemed. Ann Dowd is one of the most underrated actresses of the 21st century. No one can play matriarchal type figures like her and even the most hardened scoundrel would find themselves letting down their guards and engaging a sense of love and trust in the warmth she emanates. Therefore it's startling when that different side of her comes out during the final 20 minutes of the film. I'm not giving spoilers because YOU NEED TO GO SEE HEREDITARY IF YOU HAVENT SEEN IT YET.

What Scorsese film would have been better if directed by Spielberg and vice versa? Interesting question. In regards to Spielberg doing a Scorsese film, I know I may be in a minority but I never had much love for Scorsese's Gangs of New York (2002). I've never been able to sit through the entire film. In my honest opinion, just because the epoch the film is based on is an ugly period in history, it doesn’t mean that the film has to be inherently ugly. In the comparable and far superior Once Upon A Time in America (1984), Sergio Leone captures the pockets of childhood innocence and warm camaraderie in a truly poetic manner despite the inherent ugliness of the period documented. In Gangs of New York everywhere looked like a filthy trash heap. All the main characters were assholes. Everyone was somehow dressed in the most rattiest rags they could find. I think Scorsese was a little heavy handed in demonstrating the chaotic grittiness of the period. With the exception of Daniel Day Lewis the entire cast gave mediocre performances. The colours and camera work of the cinematography was glaring and unsettling and the whole revenge arc story didnt seem to have much of a point in the context it was used. In a nutshell the film was just a pointless, ugly film that just happened to have a measure of historical accuracy. Spielberg is the King of demonstrating the humanity that can be found in the absolute darkest periods of history. He does this without undermining historical accuracy or succumbing to fluffy melodrama. Of course the chief examples being Schindler's List and Saving Private Ryan. I think if Spielberg was given the job to direct Gangs of New York, the final product would've been a superior film with fleshed out, relatable characters, a better plot and overall a much more engaging experience for the senses. In regards to Scorsese doing a Spielberg film, I think the there is one film that was right up Scorsese’s alley that I think Spielberg’s did a disservice. Scorsese's eye for realism and portraying characters in their raw, unlikable form would've created a better product. No. It's not Munich (2005) It's Catch Me if You Can. The film was a the feelgood blockbuster movie of 2002. Frank Abagnale Jr was the antihero everyone couldn’t help but love, especially when portrayed by hearthtrob Leonardo DiCaprio. I enjoyed the movie when it premiered but it has aged poorly as of recently. Abagnale Jr was not just a scammer, it has been revealed that he is also a pathological liar. Much of the events described in his book are either grossly exaggerated or completely untrue. When you watch the film now you are treated to a self-indulgent, ego-stroking feast of fakery. I think Scorsese would've been a bit more skeptical towards the author's story and do the proper research into Abagnale Jr's life. The story would've been less attractive and a lot more cynical with moments of downright nastiness (very much in the vein of Raging Bull and The Wolf of Wall Street) but it might have been a compelling portrait of a fractured individual who thought more of himself than he actually was. It definitely wouldn't have the embarrassment that Catch Me if You Can suffers from today. So in conclusion, Spielberg and Scorsese should’ve simply traded director seats in the year 2002.

Why does the Caribbean island of Dominica get so few tourists? This may be pretty assumptive but Dominica is like an archaic little town on a little island, surrounded by mountains, surrounded by banana trees and surrounded by real, 100% indigenous Carib tribe Amerindians (Native Americans). Indigenous (Carib) teenaged girls selling souvenirs. (I was told they were superstitious against having their pictures taken, but managed to sneak this one behind them.) The first thing one would notice once they arrive at the capital Roseau is that they are transported back into the early 19th century. All the buildings of colonial days are there and still intact. One can see the architectural styles of the Spanish, French, English and even Irish in the building facades. There are some quite interesting architectural innovations to discover when you go to more rural locations. The people that I met were very friendly and laid back. I may get some flak for this but to me the Dominican accent can be best described as a Nigerian trying to sound French or Haitian trying to speak English. Go to the market at Roseau early on a Sunday morning and you will hear the Dominican brogue in all its glory. The group I went with unanimously found their accent and sing song very charming albeit amusing. The locals in turn found my accent strange and asked if I came from India. If you look at this basic map you would notice that Dominica is populated mostly at the coasts. If England is known for its fields Dominica should definitely be known for its mountains. The stocky mountains there stretch as far as the eye can see. It gives one a surreal feeling when driving towards higher altitudes. The hotel we stayed in was called La Flamboyant. When I heard the name I just figured it was just another generic, pseudo-exotic hotel name. However when we got there, the sensation of nails on a chalkboard was felt in my eyes. Yes. Somebody thought it was a good idea to paint a very dreary, blocky building in the most garish and loud colours of the kaleidoscope. If the question is why Dominica lacks tourists, maybe it's because they saw La Flamboyant while looking for hotels online. Funny Story As a very amateur fisherman, I spent a day fishing with a primitive caster and using beef liver as bait. The local fisherman laughed at me and subtly complained in their barely discernable patois that I was stinking up the place and attracting flies with my bloody beef liver. The problem was I didn't come with enough EC dollars to buy proper bait and beef liver was cheapest meat I could buy that would hold well on a hook. After an hour of no success I felt my line pull and the fishermen watched in amazement as I pulled up the most hideous sea creature I ever witnessed in my life. I am so sorry I didn't have the nerve to take a proper video to capture this creature in all its sheer horror. The fishermen around me ran off in fear as the creature looked like it would chase after them on its legs. I myself was severely tempted to throw it back in the water with caster hook and line. Hell, even throw my remaining beef liver behind it to appease its wrath. I flung it back in the water and severed the line with my knife. The creature, now uglier sporting an emo-style lip piercing, swam away in a very unsettling, human like manner. I learned later that this was called a Batfish. When the fishermen returned, I showed them the photos and they chastised me for not getting a bucket and keeping it. They said they would’ve used it as a tourist attraction. Hence, reason #2 Dominica has scarce tourists: I didn't get a bucket to keep the Batfish. On a sidenote, Dominica specializes in two resources: Bananas and souvenirs. Every nook and cranny you will see either a banana tree or someone selling souvenirs under a tent/umbrella. Try to buy from the ones who do not have conveniently located stalls as we noticed that amongst the several dozens of souvenir stalls in Roseau, only a handful actually get significant sales. Also, be aware that most of the souvenirs are not handcrafted by local artisans as they tend to claim. Nearly all of them seem to be imported from China. (The Caribs are masters of pretending to be the artisans of their wares). They put a big Dominica sticker to cover the 'Made in China’ engraving. So to answer the question seriously, why Dominica lacks tourism. The answer is simple. They aren't Westernized enough to attract the typical tourist. Don't expect to see a KFC next to a McDonald's or a big sprawling Ibiza style nightclub next to a Holiday Inn. They are an ecotourism style country and attract tourists who appreciate the purity and serenity of a land lost in time.

What should I absolutely not do when visiting your country? TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO Avoid hiring 'local tour guides.’ Stick to official touring groups from your hotel or large hiking groups. You’ve come to Trinidad on a vacation but you don't want to be so 'touristy.’ You don't want to sign up for the generic cross country tour the hotel is offering. You don't want to be crammed in a bus with a bunch of khaki short wearing, middle aged couples who want to stop the bus every 10 minutes saying. 'Hey driver, look there's a natural spring there. I want to fill my water bottle.’ Or 'Ooh driver stop the bus. I want to get a picture of those local Trinidadian cows.’ And you definitely don't want to go on the same well beaten hiking track where ten buses like yours are parked so more tourists like yourself could commence on a 5 minute hike, past dozens of souvenir stalls, to see a dormant mud volcano which, if you're lucky, might belch out a nauseating scent of rotten eggs. It sounds awful but believe me the other option is far worse. You'd meet someone who'd tell you, 'I know a guy who does private tours. He'll take you to the real hidden sites that the tour groups don't go and he's very knowledgeable of history and professional. You don't have to stick with the dull tourist tours.’ You want to make the extra effort and discover the hidden Trinidad (or Tobago) and this guy sounds like the real deal. Here are the problems with that offer: Discovering a makeshift stone axe . My Scottish cousins realized this too late when they hired some guy who was a friend of a friend of friend who did private tours. He was taking them to Turure Water Steps which was indeed a beautiful place with four amazing waterfalls, each bigger than the last. When I heard he was charging $1000 TT (roughly 150 US) to take them there I protested and told them that they were being ripped off. Anyone could take them there for free. They argued that he was a professional and had deep knowledge of the history of places. I went along with them for the trip. Some hours later, returning home, they agreed that they were ripped off. In summary the lesson learned here is that there are several people like that so-called tour guide who wants to rip off hapless tourists. Either you stick with your hotel tour or if you want to go off the beaten track, join a professional hiking/tour group or go with a large group of friendly, trustworthy locals. Doing otherwise could have you ripped off or even worse. Edit 31.08.21 Had no idea this little tidbit of info would've garnered so many upvotes. Thank you all for the support. What is the most badass thing your parent has ever done? Martin was a guy who lived a few houses away from us. Outside of his fence was a coconut tree that grew on an empty lot of land. When the tree finally bore coconuts, myself, my brother and some of the boys of the neighborhood went and attempted to climb and get some. Martin, the middle aged perpetual bachelor of the street, came out in his underwear (he was always parading around his yard in his underwear) and cursed at us to leave ‘his tree’ alone. We went home downtrodden. When my mother asked us what the problem was and we explained she suddenly took on a serious countenance. She said the tree did not belong to him. She then tells us to follow her. She went to each of the boys homes, spoke to all the mothers and before we knew it there was a gang of all us boys and our mothers marching to the coconut tree. Our mothers commanded each of us to climb and pick a coconut each. They made sure to be loud to get the attention of the neighborhood. ‘Go ahead,’ my mother said loudly ‘Nobody owns this tree.’ Martin came out to see the ruckus and immediately he had four mothers on his case. They gave him an earful about the coconut tree and cussing out us boys. My mother even tosses in a zinger saying that no one likes to see him in his jockeys, that he doesn't impress any of the ladies living here and if she sees him one more time undressed she would report him to the police. Martin slunk back indoors. After a few laughs our mothers carried us back home. I never thought my mother had it in her to organize an angry mob so quickly and over something so ridiculous.

Whom did you feel bad for in high school? Balram. There was a boy who came from the depths of poverty named Balram. He was sinewy and had coarse skin and features that made him look like he jumped out of the pages of our history books as an indentured laborer from colonial times. Everything about him was out of sync with the rest of the class. This was the late 90s and baggy pants were the thing, Balram wore his khaki trousers wrapped tight around his skinny legs. Perms from excessive hair gel (my specialty at the time), corn-rows, Caesar styled and spiky hair was the rage amongst teenage boys back then. Balram wore something that looked straight out of a an old Amitabh Bachchan movie from the 70s. Balram's school uniforms always looked faded and threadbare. Never once did anyone see him wearing new items of clothing. This led to many of the kids in class poking fun at the possibility that Balram's family got used clothes for him. Balram didn't have cable. It was possible he didn't have a TV. Balram didn't care for the music everyone else listened to. He didn't go to the arcade and play video games. He didn't get excited hearing about Stone Cold Steve Austin. He was odd in that he only enjoyed games that demonstrated his eerie strength and his skills in survival. This included holding breath competitions, arm wrestling, 'mercy’ and 'bokee' (hitting an opponents fist by flicking a finger against it until someone gives up in pain). He didn't have much of a sense of humour. He would sit in class like an old Native American chief, peering knowingly at the world through his squinted, Charles Bronson-esque eyes while everyone else made jokes and acted like morons who needed attention. My friends and I would hang out with him but for some reason he never was an official member of our group. He preferred to roam alone. Once, I was tricked by some boys into pretending to want to beat him up, all for kicks. Before I could say 'Hey' Balram lifted me into the air by the shoulders and against the wall until I yielded. It was an impressive display of brute strength that I could never forget. In moments of boredom Balram was usually an easy target for jokes and insults. Some of the girls were particularly mean to him. One would say to that she would never be with a boy like him who looks dirty and always smells like old curry. The boys would always joke around that he came from 'the bush’ and came to school swinging on vines like Tarzan. One of the boys even managed to create a comic depicting Balram's life in the bush, fighting snakes and tigers on a daily basis etc. Balram learned to laugh with everyone and not let it get to him. In Form 3 Balram vanished. Always a recluse he never communicated to anyone what were his plans/intentions. Some months later he visited the school wearing a new uniform and with a friend at his side. He got transferred to a school closer to home where more rural kids like him were around. He looked much happier and was far more social than he was before. That day, most of the class ignored him but my friends and I held a reception to commemorate the good times we had with him. He said his new school was the best; teachers were hardly there and the kids did what they wanted. He showed me a tattoo that he got on his arm of a dragon. Even though the tattoo looked ridiculously amateurish and his clothes were still faded and threadbare and his hair still outdated my friends and I sang his praises and gave him his day. He really was a great guy. He had no fear of trying to fit in and had an infinite amount of patience for those around him. I wouldn't be surprised to find out that he made a huge success out if his life as an adult. But alas that day was the last time I saw him/heard anything about him.

What is a show or movie which was super hyped up but ended up being terrible? The Underground (2006) Who doesn't love the Wayans? It seemed like they could do nothing wrong throughout the 80s, 90s and 00s. Keenen Ivory created In Living Color and directed the cult classic I'm Gonna Git You Sucka (1988) as well as the first two Scary Movies and White Chicks (2004). At one point in time he was the highest earning black film director in history. Shawn and Marlon had a large following with The Wayans Brothers television sitcom and a variety of acting credits in the Scary Movie films and In Living Color. Damon on the other hand……..Damon tries. He had a short unmemorable stint in Saturday Night Live where he played characters that would be deemed offensive by today's standards. He starred in a couple of duds throughout the 90s such as Blankman and Major Payne. He had a varying success with a few sitcoms under his belt but in 2006 he delivered the biggest turkey of his career with the Showtime sketch comedy show The Underground. Hyping it as 'In Living Color on steroids' the show was a truly tasteless and desperately unfunny attempt to zone in on the post-Chappelle Show audience. Some of the sketches include an ex-convict seducing and having sex with a very old woman, a talking vagina, and Peter Pan wanting to play with starving Somalians. Abandoning the witty and insightful parody of his brother Keenen, Damon opts for trashy and tasteless. Despite his sad attempts to gain attention by supposed shocking and edgy humour, no one raised an eyebrow and the show was cancelled without a murmur.

What do you think of the album Titanic Rising by Weyes Blood? I think it's one of the best albums of the 21st century thus far. Titanic Rising has singlehandedly restored my faith in the music industry's ability to still churn out works of art. I've literally spent the entire month of October trying to get ‘Andromeda’ out of my head (in a good way). Titanic Rising is a well-crafted song cycle album consisting of 10 songs that explores topics ranging from heartache to the decline of modern civilization. Her songwriting is poetic and the combination of her smooth, elegaic voice with that of her operatic back up singer creates a warm tone throughout the album. Natalie Mering aka Weyes Blood looks and sounds like she teleported right out of the Golden Age of singer-songwriters of the 70s but with a style of her own. One can't fail to notice the influence of artists such as Joni Mitchell, Moby Grape, George Harrison and even more contemporary artists like Enya and Aimee Mann in her songs. Highlights for me include A Lot's Gonna Change, Andromeda, Wild Time and Picture Me Better which is a sweet country tinged prayer that closes the album to a classically rendered reprise of A Lot's Gonna Changed called Nearer to Thee. I was highly impressed listening to this album from the very first listen (which is rare for me). I truly love this album and I wish more people would see the talent of this truly under appreciated young lady. My rating: 8.5 out of 10.

What is the most ungrateful way someone reacted when opening up a birthday gift? I’m cheating a bit but all my examples are Christmas gifts…..and yes, this would be another ‘ungrateful mother’ answer. Christmas 2001 My aunt gave my brother and I some money to purchase a gift for our mother. My aunt’s relationship with her brother’s ex (my mother) was quite ‘lacking’ to put it diplomatically but to spread the love my aunt insisted that we take the money and buy something nice for her. I was 15 and my brother was 17. We were admittedly not the most thoughtful boys in the world but we put our minds together and decided that we would get something Catholic based as our mother was highly religious. We saw a handcrafted angel that had a decadent, antique look. We both agreed that our mother would love it. It cost almost the entire sum of money we were given. With the remainder we bought a lunch and shared it. When she unwrapped it on Christmas Day she simply stared at it with disapproval. ‘How much this cost?’ We told her the amount. ‘So much money for this?! Where you got the money to buy this?’ We told her how we got the money. ‘Where’s the change?’ We told her we spent the change on buying lunch. Her mouth puckered and she gave the look someone gives when smelling a foul odour. ‘Next time don't buy anything just bring the money for me,’ she said and that was that. Christmas 2009 I’m 23, recently got a new job with a decent salary. My father, whose history of mental illness had him out of our lives for the majority of my childhood has found a solid footing in life as a taxi driver. He has been saving his money and helping my mother financially for the last few years as a sort of reciprocation for his burdens of the past. Though my mother had long moved on and started a new family, my father felt it his duty to be in her life and help her in whatever way he could. My mother,, however, refused to forgive him for the past. I thought he paid his dues twofold, as the majority of the money he earned was directed towards her. My love and appreciation of him was growing but my mother somehow didn’t seem to like that. For Christmas I bought him a small pair of car speakers for his taxi. For my mother I bought a necklace and a purse. My mother’s gift cost far more than my father’s but my father’s gift came in a larger box whilst my mother’s two items fit neatly in a small box. When I presented them with their gifts I could detect the look of disapproval on my mother’s face as she saw that my father’s gift was larger. My father, in his usual excitable manner, showed great joy. My mother decided to go into her bedroom to open her present, away from everyone else. Whilst we were all making merry in the living room; my father, his best friend Henry, my brother, myself and our two half-sisters could hear some mutterings coming out of my mother’s bedroom. Suddenly the mutterings became more audible. My mother was doing what we Trinis call ‘throwing words’ i.e. speaking ill of something/someone to yourself with the intention of that person hearing you. ‘Cheap…cheap and ungrateful,’ we heard her say, ‘I don’t know why they don’t get out of my place.’ I went into the bedroom and as I entered she flung the purse and necklace on the floor towards me. ‘Ummm, I don’t like this,’ she said tartly, ‘I don’t wear cheap things.’ I couldn’t believe my eyes and ears. I protested that her gift cost twice more than my father’s. ‘You raising your voice at me?’ she yelled and she then demanded that we all leave the house, myself, my brother, my father, his friend Henry. She kicked us out her house Christmas Day because she believed I bought her something cheap and wanted to spite her in front of my father. This would be the last Christmas the whole family spent as one. Christmas 2021 I’m 35 and my relationship with my mother has been strained to say the least. She hardly calls to find out about her grand-daughter Adrianna and when she does, she refers to her as ‘your daughter.’ I stumble upon my mother at the bus station and we make an attempt at some kind of reconciliation. I ask if she’d like anything for Christmas and she said she would like an iron (heater). I thought that was a reasonable request as it was a cheap item and I was lacking in funds, but she then decides to ask for a ironing board as well. I told her I may not be able to afford both but I’d try. I wait for her to ask me what she should get for her grand-daughter but I receive no query. Coming close to Christmas Day I encountered several unforeseen expenses so I sent a WhatsApp message to her that I can only afford the iron. She receives the message but doesn’t respond. I call her on Christmas to tell her I wanted to send my father to drop off the present as I didn’t have a vehicle. She replies that she doesn’t want him by her place. After a long time pleading she finally acquiesces. My father takes the gift up to her house and after an hour I get a voice message from her: ‘You didn’t get the ironing board?’

What experience changed your perception on something? Vachel was weird. He was a boy who attended my class at primary school. I dont have a photo of him but he had a strong resemblance to the boy above. I attended a somewhat prestigious school for boys and all of us boys found Vachel eerie. We wondered if he was an alien. Why? Vachel never got a single answer wrong in quizzes. Ever. Vachel always scored 100% in the science based subjects. Had it not been for the subjective creative writing essay, he would've had a flawless portfolio. He had a legendary reputation throughout the school and his name was always cited whenever teachers spoke of academic success. As would be expected, he wasn't well liked by many of the boys in class. Because he was somewhat dandy-ish and spoke in a flat, emotionless, baritone voice, the boys in class would secretly refer to him as ultra-nerd, faggot, Spock and all kinds of derogatory labels. He was aware of this but was not the confrontational type of person. He was also seen as an eccentric loner. This was '97. The year of Titanic, who was the hottest Spice Girl, Street Fighter vs Mortal Kombat etc. Vachel would participate in none of these 'ordinary boy’ discussions. We all figured him to be an oddball, only-child, living with wealthy, aged parents in a crumbling estate and his hobbies were listening to opera while playing chess or reenacting Shakespeare to an imaginary audience. Well that was how the cartoons portrayed genius level boys. As it so happened, I was to stay at a relative's house for a week. After school, while about to travel to that location I saw that Vachel was heading the same way and learned that he lived not too far from my relative. We boarded the bus and sat together and for the first time I had a conversation with him. Expecting the conversation to be awkward, I was quite surprised how good of a conversationalist he was. He was quite interested in hearing about my relatives and family. I felt comfortable and basically gave him my whole life story during that time. I didn't even bother to ask him about his family but that didn't bother him. We stopped off at the town of San Juan and he told me he wanted to show me what he liked to do in his spare time. I was a little hesitant, thinking he would carry me in a lab and experiment on my brain but instead he carried me to a book store. I wondered what was the big deal. Neither of us had money and if I did I definitely wouldn't spend it on a book as I had loads home. He took me to a section of the bookstore that had some novelizations of movies. He showed a Ghostbusters 2 novelization, a Return of the Jedi novelization and then he asked me to close my eyes as he had a secret to show me. I did so and when he told me to open my eyes he held a Batman and Robin novelization in front of my face. He was excited because the movie had only premiered a few months ago. I never saw such joy in his face. He then started speaking softly as though he was describing a crime he had committed. He whispered that what he does is that he comes into the bookstore daily. He reads a few pages of these movie-books and would leave before a worker catches him. With pride he said that he had ‘seen’ all the popular movies without paying the price of a single movie ticket, by simply reading a few pages a day of these novelizations. He then hid the Batman book behind some older novels and said that someday, when he has saved the money, he will come back and buy this very book, so he can ‘watch the movie' at his leisure. I was thoroughly confused. The little rascal in me wanted to laugh at him and his 'secret.’ I wanted to ask him, 'Why don't you just watch the movie? Most of these show on cable every day’ when something suddenly caught my eye. In his excitement his shirt became untucked from his pants and I saw that his shirt was much too small for him. Then I realized that his pants had an inkblot on the left leg through which I recalled he always had that same inkblot, every day. This meant that he had but one pair of pants. Then I recognized that his shoes were oversized, almost clownish, they had to be hand-me-downs. It then struck me. Vachel was poor. As in really really poor. This coming from someone from a family of lesser means. As I listened to him going off about how he feels sorry for Mr. Freeze and his dead wife, I felt like crying and giving him a consoling hug. While us boys in class rattled on about shows and movies we saw on cable, trips to the cinema and video games we played on our personal gaming consoles, Vachel was home with none of those luxuries, forced to entertain himself with his school books. His ‘genius’ simply came from the fact that he had nothing else to occupy his time but read whatever books he possessed. He was in fact, a normal boy just like the rest of us. We left the book store and took a taxi together, heading homewards, up a hill. My suspicion was confirmed when he stopped off at a humble wooden house that looked ancient, almost abandoned, inside a dirt track. I saw his plump mother scrubbing at some clothes in a bucket under a tap. There was no sign of electricity available at the house. Vachel went and proudly pointed at me, his new friend, to his mother who cheerily waved. I awkwardly waved back as the taxi reversed out of the track and drove off. It was the first time I got a taste of how alienating and unfair baseless assumptions can be, especially for those who fall under them. Edit 02.02.22 I was a nice child at times. At times I could be naughty. Click here to see this fascinating prank I almost pulled off on my teacher.

Has there ever been one single scene that ruined a movie for you? 10 Cloverfield Lane (2016) has quite possible the worst film ending of the 21st century thus far. In the film Mary Elizabeth Winstead’s character Michelle is kidnapped by John Goodman’s seemingly insane Howard. She, along with friendly but a low IQ young man called Emmett, are kept in Howard’s underground bunker as he believes that the world is under attack by either the Russians or aliens, everyone is dead and the air outside is poisoned. As she becomes fearful of Howard’s ever increasing paranoia and aggression she attempts to escape. What she witnesses outside in her first attempt makes her question if what he has been telling her is actually true. The movie is coated in deep suspense accentuated with great performances by the cast, particularly Goodman who undergoes a sinister change of persona without coming across over the top at any point in the film. As a viewer I felt the state of constant confusion and increasing fear that the protagonist felt. Is this man insane? How could what he’s saying be true? Maybe I’m going insane as well? The final 15 minutes of the film answers all these questions. It answers these questions as if an average High School student was given the task to write the screenplay’s ending. It is the dumbest most far fetched denouement to what could’ve been a great film. I won’t spoil it for you but the film starts of as a gripping thriller but then suddenly decides at the end to become some kind of action sci-fi flick in the vein of Aliens (1986). It’s almost like if the end of Silence of the Lambs had Jodie Foster’s character being ambushed by Hannibal Lecter in her home, surprises him with her kung fu moves, knocking him out and then hauling his ass back to prison. It’s that dumb. Watch it for yourself and see.

What things do people say that make you roll your eyes? A guy from my neighbourhood came to my house some time ago asking for help. He had gotten a flat tire and wanted to borrow my spare for the following day as he needed to check out a job in the morning. From the moment we started speaking to the moment we parted, our conversation was a series of eye rolling on my part. Me: So how come you don't have a spare? Him: I just bought an amp and some speakers. Money’s finished. My car probably has the best music setup in the whole street. Me: (At his house) But look you have another car here. Why don't you use this car? Him: That car isn't working. Me: Then why don't you use one of the tires. It's the same size. Him: That's not my car that's my wife's. Wife (comes out to say hello, seemingly drunk): I have a car for sale. If you only see the engine on this car. Proceeds to open the hood on the car previously mentioned. Me: But is this car working? Wife: Who says it's not working? (glares at husband). Me: (Looking at the engine) Why are there sunflower seeds on top the carburetor? Wife: That damn parrot! It acts as if this car is his house. Husband: I'm actually a mechanic myself. Me: (Tempted to say ‘But you can't fix your wife's car?’) Mmhmm. Husband: I have practically every tool there are for cars. Me: (Tempted to say ‘But you don't have a spare tire.’) Mmhmm Husband: If ever you need work done on your car be sure to check me. Me: Will do. Husband: Can I borrow your tire wrench? I can't find mine. Husband: I can do masonry, plumbing, electrical, roofing. Wife: He's very talented. I never have to call anybody to get work done. I have an entire contracting company living in my house. Husband: Take my number. (He proceeds to search for a call card in his wallet but the area is in darkness.) Honey shine a light on my wallet for a second. Me: Why don't you put up some lights in the front yard? Husband: (Says nothing) Wife: (Scowling) The man just asked you a question. Husband: Well your spare didn't fit but thanks for the help anyway. Me: No problem. Husband: Can you do me one more favour? Me: (groaning) What? Husband: (Whispering so his wife, who went back in the house, doesn't hear). Can you lend me $20? I’ll need it for gas in the morning. Me: Sure (hands him a $20) Husband: (whispering even softer) You want a beer? Me: Yeah why not. Husband: If I go with you she'll know that I'm going for alcohol. You don't mind going to the grocery and getting it for us. (Hands me back my $20) Me: (Puts $20 back in wallet). Sure thing man. I then went home. I wonder how long he waited until it dawned on him that I was not coming back with his beers.

What is the hardest you've ever worked at in your entire life? A branch of Mario's Pizza had only recently opened in my home town just last year. They were looking for motorcycle delivery riders and though I promised myself to never do motorcycle delivery for them again (it's actually very risky, and you always get soaked in rain) I really needed the money. I reapplied and during the orientation I got a head's up from old friends that one of the most hated branch managers Ms. K, was to be the appointed manager of my branch. The scuttlebutt was that she was a brown-nosed elitist, looking to do anything that it takes to get an area manager position i.e. she was the current area manager's pet. I heard awful stories that some of the best, most dedicated workers either resigned or were transferred to an unfortunate location after having disputes with Ms. K. This made me groan inwardly because I had various encounters with branch managers like that. All they do is to try to makes sales targets to satisfy their superior and be rewarded cash bonuses. They would literally lie, steal and kill to make these sales targets. The customer means nothing to them unless he/she is some big shot. The staff beneath them are nothing more than names on a roster sheet. Once I slipped and fell violently on a poorly mopped floor and such a manager ran out her office, not to help me up, but to demonstrate to everyone that I was wearing the wrong type of shoes hence the restaurant had no legal responsibility for my incident. I sighed but convinced myself with the idea that Ms. K couldn't be all that bad. The opening weekend of the branch was made into a spectacle. There were live artists, our mascot (a stereotypical moustachioed Italian but with a huge head), a bouncy castle, a buy one get one free offer and prizes being handed out to random customers. I arrived for the evening shift. When I arrived there were so much people I had to squeeze through the crowd just to enter the building. This was right after the COVID lockdown of 2020 and though the store was supposed to have a maximum of 20 people indoors at any given time, I counted about 50 indoors and over 100 outside fighting to get in. It was like being thrown into a battlefield. There was no introduction to anyone. No one had anticipated that the restaurant would’ve been flooded with customers to such an extent. I came all smiling and social but everyone wore frowns and all the customers looked furious. 'Hey delivery man,' a man called out angrily, 'Check on order 607 for me…….2 hours now I waiting.’ Suddenly a barrage of people started to hail me out to check on their orders, the men scowling angrily, the women giving me sad, puppy-dog faces. I had to run away from them all. The poor cashier had to stand there and take verbal abuse while angry customers shoved receipts into her face. 'If this order not ready I want my money back.’ 'I want to talk to the manager.’ 'Excuse me! Can I get your name? This service is terrible.’ The poor cashier was just a dwarfish 22yr old single mother who only recently got the job. I wanted to help her but I knew it would be to no avail as I saw that there was a mountain of deliveries on the warmer. Firstly I had to hand my assumption letter to the manager. I spoke to a supervisor who was frantically trying to answer calls that were ringing off the hook. I could barely hear her because the live music was so loud that it was a shouting match between us. 'CHECK INSIDE THE OFFICE.’ 'WHAT?’ 'THE OFFICE' She pointed to a little room ahead where the door was closed. I watched as several workers moved to and fro in a daze getting dough and toppings out of the chiller. There was a stock pile of finished pizzas of unknown destination that lay on the cutting table practically cold. Two workers were frantically sorting through a pile of crumpled bills trying to determine which pizza belonged to whom. Apparently the store invested in some cheaper bill management software that was glitchy and froze when overworked so a lot of old orders resurrected on the screen and pushed out the new orders hence the chaos of customers not getting their orders. I tried to assist in sorting out the orders and finding the right pizzas when I felt a hand on my shoulder. It was another delivery rider I was acquainted with. 'You just reached?’ he asked concernedly. 'No. About an hour now.’ I replied. 'Go talk to the manager.’ he said with a hint of caution. He then said as though reading my mind, 'Boy is madness up in this restaurant.’ He then proceeded to laugh his manical laugh which he did whenever he was under pressure or had something on his mind. I knocked on the manager's door and heard a voice say to come in. Inside I saw a lady in her 30s who I assumed to be the branch manager. Next to her was a lady in her 40s/early 50s who I assumed was her boss, the area manager. They were both watching baby photos on the area manager's phone. The manager Ms.K looked quite attractive with light brown eyes, a svelte figure and huge boobs. I told myself that she couldn't be all that bad. Then she spoke. 'You're an hour late……and this is your first day.’ Her voice was cold and pedantic. She and the area manager then stared at me critically. Ms. K. then adjusted her mask to reveal a rather ugly mouth. The charm was dispelled immediately. I explained to them that I was on time and I was just trying to help because there was a lot of chaos outside. 'Chaos?’ the area manager cried as though offended, 'What chaos is he talking about?’ 'I don't know what he's talking about,' Ms. K replied, 'Staff outside not following orders and want to bawl chaos every 5 seconds.’ She gave me a book to sign in my time. A landline phone that was next to them was ringing off the hook the entire time. It was a customer line. They both proceeded to exit the room and bawl 'Answer the phone! Answer the phone!’ to the frantic staff. I felt uneasy being amongst them and went to do some deliveries. Every customer I reached to had a severe tongue lashing ready for me. 'Tell me why I should pay for this. Three hours now I waiting.’ I had to put on my most pathetic and mournful face and give my most eloquent excuses just to get paid without hassle by almost every customer. ''I'll never order from you all again. What's your name?’ I must've heard that statement 50 times in just an hour. Meanwhile, inside the restaurant, things just never seemed to quell, only intensify. The phone kept ringing incessantly and 9 out of 10 times it was an angry customer yelling obscenities about waiting 5 hours for his/her order. 'Answer the phone. Answer the phone.’ yelled the manager and her master from inside the office. Suddenly the air conditioner malfunctioned. Now we had to contend with the chaos and blistering heat of a massive pizza oven in a closed in building. A fight broke out amongst two customers. Security was dragged into it. A customer used that opportunity to threaten to jump across the counter if he didn't get his order now. Thankfully police came to disperse some of the crowd and warn the restaurant about not following COVID protocols. 'Answer the phone. Answer the phone.’ yelled the managers. I looked at one of the supervisors who was glued to the phone from the minute she arrived. She was an old acquaintance and I liked her. Sadly she was overweight and suffered from high blood pressure. She was trying to answer the phone to the best of her abilities and take orders\deal with irate customers. She had two pages full of orders she scribbled that were to be entered on the database. Everytime she tried to enter them the phone kept ringing, preventing her from doing so. In the end she decided to ignore the calls to focus on entering the orders. The area manager was passing by and observed this. 'Sharon,' the area manager said stoically, 'Why aren't you answering the phone? Do we have to have a chat in the office?’ I felt an overwhelming rage hearing that comment that wasn't even directed to me. I watched Sharon as she gave a look similar to swallowing a frog, wiped the sweat off her face and replied calmly, 'Ms. A, I have almost two pages full of orders still to enter into the system from since an hour ago. I'm trying.’ The area manager looked confused and then glanced at Sharon's list. 'Somebody else answer the phone,’ she yelled, 'Somebody answer the phone!’ She then looked at her watch. 'Oh I have to pick up my daughter,' she said to Ms. K. They exchanged some pleasantries and the area manager left to return in a few hours. Ms. K. returned to her office and closed the door. The chaos continued as the heat intensified. At one point I felt I was going to have a mental breakdown. There was absolutely no order or plan and everyone basically just tried to stay afloat in their little corner amidst a towering pile of tossed aside pizzas; wrong and cancelled orders. Out front was an army of angry customers who looked ready to riot kept shouting to get some kind of attention. The phone kept ringing and ringing and ringing. The two workers who were sorting out orders condescended to just handing out random pizzas and hoping for the best. Whenever I answered the phone and an angry delivery customer demanded for his/her order placed 5 hours ago, I was forced to lie and say that the order was on its way, despite the fact that it was never entered on the database. I was relieved to go on deliveries, anything to take me out of that madhouse. After returning from a severely disgruntled customer of whom I had to give an exceptional performance of sorrow and misery, begging her to pay for the order, I returned to the restaurant, parked the motorcycle and was thinking to abandon the job. I was seriously considering just leaving without a word. I did not want to face more chaos and madness and 'Answer the phone’ anymore. However I realized that that would make me a coward. I entered the restaurant and to my relief, as the sun set, the crowd died down and things were starting to get manageable. I started helping customers source their orders when I observed Ms. K. arrive in her car and exited the vehicle holding a large cake. I assumed that this was a token of appreciation for the staff and the hellish day that they had. I thought that was quite nice of her. She took the cake into her office. A few minutes later the area manager returned and went into the office. Ms. K then announced for all the supervisors to come into the office and whilst the rest of staff toiled in the unbearable heat we could hear strains of 'Happy Birthday to you’ emanating from the room. The cake was not for us. It was the area manager's birthday. The area manager took the cake and thanked Ms. K. Without a word to the rest of staff she left with her cake in one whole piece while the rest of us stood there in disbelief and disgust. Thus ended the opening day of the restaurant. The next day, Sunday, I got word that three employees had quit, including Sharon the supervisor who had almost a decade of service with the company. I told myself that the storm was over and today would be much more pleasant. Boy was I wrong.

What one thing do you wish you had known about life when you were in your 20s? This question is for those who are older than 20 who would like to share their mistakes and insights with a younger person than themselves. I wish I didn’t get caught up in the typical young adult craze of getting a car. When I got my first full time job as a warehouse attendant at age 19, practically every male co-worker around this age would go philosophically deep in the discussion of buying their first car. A car meant everything to us simple minded fools. It signified freedom. It allowed for us to be able to go out wherever we wanted and come back home whenever we wanted. It meant getting premium birds (girls). It meant easier access to sex. It meant getting wasted on beers while bar-hopping and chilling out by the riverside or the beach with our closest pals. It meant blasting our favourite hit songs of the time while cruising through our neighbourhoods and getting attention. There was a certain mystique about getting a car at age 20 and to this day there still is. Now at 35, I can safely say that for the majority of 20 year olds, that mystique is in fact bull***t. There are only two criteria I believe that allows for getting a car at 20 to not be financial suicide. If you are fortunate to belong to either category, upon getting your first car Heaven’s Gate opens up and you have years of wild adventures at your helm that will allow for fond memories. If you don’t belong to either category, Heaven’s Gate opens up for an extremely short while but then suddenly the floor caves in on you and fall into the pits of finance hell that will allow for a bald spot on your head by age 23. Whether new or used, investing in a car at a young age is a recipe for disaster for the average Trinidadian 20 year old. When you’re fresh out of school and you decide to get a car to experience your man-child utopia, you might as well change the name of your bank account to your car’s license plate number. Practically all of your salary belongs to that car. If it’s new or foreign used (as we have in Trinidad) your ass is owned by whichever bank that gave you the loan for your car. You may cry ‘freedom at last’ to your parents but the bank has an even bigger leash around your neck and they don’t love you like mommy and daddy does. When you bite the bullet and save some money to buy a cheap, used car, you may pat yourself on the back for such grit and determination but you are most likely in a worse off position than your friend who has to pay a loan as your ass is owned by the mechanic. It’s almost pathetic to see the typical twenty something year old Trini looking frantic at the side of the road after his car broke down; no money to pay for a wrecking service, desperate for any kind of assistance, his lady-friend abandoning him in shame. Yet I see such a scenario every Friday evening, especially when I pass by the mall. Friends and peers would make the excuse, ‘Once you choose a good car and have a really good mechanic you could buy a used car.’ I fell for this terrible piece of advice and at age 24 bought with cash my first car. It was used and recommended by a trusted mechanic friend. It was one of these: It was a disaster. I had a breakdown the very second day of driving it. I spent more time waiting for the mechanic to fix it than actually driving it. The steering wheel actually came off while driving one fine evening. Going on a date while driving this beauty was more suspenseful than a Hitchcock movie; will it break down on me and roll down the hill? Oh no, what’s that weird noise? When I had to get repairs/service done, sourcing parts for my discontinued model would send me on an Indiana Jones like expedition where I would find myself in some remote scrap-yard miles away from home, climbing up a ghastly stack of aged and abandoned vehicles looking for a model like mine. If I was lucky enough to find my model, the scrap yard owner would gauge how desperate I looked and charged to suit. Forget starting a small business, forget marrying your sweetheart, ignore stock market opportunities, partnerships or simply taking a summer trip to Cancun. My beaten up Ford Laser was my business partner, my lover, my future, my everything. Forget taking out girls to movies and the beach, I might as well carry out my mechanic and try to sweetheart him into cheaper rates. The final straw came when I took out my last bit of money from my account and was siphoning some from my credit card, an epiphany ocurred: At the time, my mechanic informed me that he was unavailable but his son would take over duties for the time being. As I waited at the garage for the son to arrive, I saw a boy, a few years younger than me, ride towards me with his bicycle and park it at the garage. Wondering if the kid was lost or confused, I told him that this was a garage for cars, not bikes. He laughed and said that he was the mechanic. I queried why he didn't have a car, being a mechanic and all. He gave me a knowing glance and said, ‘Can’t afford one.’ ‘But there are so many cheap used cars for sale!?’ I said quite fascinated, ‘And you know how to fix ‘em!?’ He simply smiled and said nothing. He asked me to raise my bonnet. I then realized he probably saw me as a fool. He had already given his answer. Just because he could fix them himself doesn’t mean that they would stop being a bloody expense, a pain in the ass and a sacrifice of all other youthful goals and endeavours. It was time to face the facts, buying a used car, for someone like me, was like buying a dying horse. After the repair I put the car for sale at a great loss and washed my hands of it. Something magical happened after. Like glimmering grass on a summer morning, I could see my money starting to grow. Life suddenly became enjoyable again. Whenever I see a twenty year old posing proudly next to his aged, first car, I shake my head and laugh to myself. The amount of money he is going to spend behind that vehicle could clothe and feed a child. Go ahead and call it your baby.

Which incident offended you badly? While attending university I was enrolled in a Human Resource Management course. There was this guy who was also a student but he was doing research for a separate Occupational Safety/Labour Law course or something of that nature. During the break period he would hand us questionnaires for us to kindly respond to for his research. The questions he asked were basic Labour related questions in regards to where we worked, if we understood the meaning of workplace safety, witnessed preventable workplace accidents etc. Of course there were the typical age, gender, ethnicity type questions at the beginning of the questionnaire. When he approached me to answer one he said the usual disclaimer of 'the information will be strictly confidential and used only for research purposes' and yadee yadee ya. However when I finished the questionnaire and handed it to him I was shocked to see him open my questionnaire and begin reading it. I took slight offense to that. Him reading, right in front of me, my personal questionnaire that was supposed to be confidential information used for data collection was very unprofessional. I told myself maybe he's just making sure I didn't leave out a question. He then looked at me and said something that I would never expect a university level student to say 'You really consider yourself mixed race?’ I automatically responded 'Yeah’ and we both stared at each other awkwardly. I tried to figure out what he meant by that. I wasn't African. I wasn't Indian. I wasn't European and I wasnt Other. I was a mixture of all the above. He himself was mixed race. He was of Portuguese-Indian descent with freckles and a pony tail. He saw that I was getting offended so he tried to say something that he believed wouldve defused the situation. Instead what he said after was far more heinous. 'It's just that I'm getting too much respondents ticking ‘Mixed Race.’ I'm trying to show through my research that it's mainly black people who are victims of unfair labour laws and workplace conditions.’ I stared at him. He basically nonchalantly admitted to me his desire to skewer, corrupt and sensationalise his own research along racial lines. The way he casually said it gave me the impression that this was the norm for his department. He gave a brief, nervous laugh and walked away. Thinking to himself that I was the weird one. I learned something unintentionally from my university studies that day.

Why is Eric Clapton such a highly rated guitarist when he's very average? Average you say? Clapton is in my personal top five of greatest guitarists. I'd even rank him higher than Hendrix and just a smidgen below Duane Allman. I dont know anything technical about guitars, I can't play and I definitely can't determine prowess. However I've listened to hundreds of guitar oriented albums and only a handful of guitarists stick out in terms of consistency of quality. Clapton is definitely one of them. For someone to listen to Disraeli Gears and call the stunning solos on that album average would be the rantings of a madman or the simply just a common troll. From his work with The Yardbirds, John Mayall & the Bluesbreakers, Cream, Blind Faith, Derek and the Dominos and his solo work (my least favourite, but heck he wrote Tears in Heaven) he has proven to be more than just average. I think the best performance depicting Clapton's talent is his guitar duel with The Band's Robbie Robertson for the The Last Waltz concert. Here one can see two immensely talented guitarists politely trying to upstage one another in a mastery of improvisation. The fans who wrote 'Clapton Is God’ on a London wall were not paid to do so. They did it because something about his guitar work touched them deeply inside that they felt him to be on a higher realm than ordinary people. Definitely doesn't fit the description of someone with average talent.

What is the cruelest way to find out someone doesn’t like you? SHOWING OFF As a teenager I was sometimes a bit of a dirtbag. One day after school I was hanging out with the boys and we were trading girl conquest stories, most of them fake of course. I bragged to them that there was this pretty girl named Nicole who was obsessed with me. I showed them a picture of her and they fawned over it. I then laughed and told them that I had higher standards and they could have her if they wanted. To add more relish to the dirtbag weiner that I was I pulled out my flip phone for a prank. I called her and put the call on speaker. They listened as she kept saying 'Hello, hello?’ I then replied, 'I can't hear you…….bad signal……..go somewhere different.’ I could hear her moving about.I had to hold my laughter in. Nicole: 'Elijah? Are you hearing me now?’ Me: 'Kinda. You need to talk louder.’ Nicole: 'YOU HEARING ME?’ Me: 'Ahh…..You're shouting in my ears. A little softer.’ Nicole: 'I'm sorry. Is everything ok?’ I hung up the phone. Most of the boys were impressed and found it funny but one boy stared at me angrily but didn't say a word. My phone then started ringing. Nicole was calling me back. 'You see,' I said to the boys while showing them she was calling back, 'She's obsessed.’ I pressed END CALL. Why was I such a dirtbag? The girl whom I was infatuated with didn’t show the same kind of sentiments for me, no matter how hard I tried. Maybe I used Nicole as a vessel to unleash the anger and hurt that I had pent up over my unrequited puppy love? Maybe I was just an insensitive bastard? Regardless Karma came like a you-know-what more than a decade later when I saw Nicole enter my workplace looking ravishing. I engaged her in conversation and she seemed friendly enough. We both were single at the moment. I told myself that the incident was so long ago, so most likely she forgave me and got over it. I ventured to ask her out for lunch. Without sparing a second’s thought she replied, ‘Sorry, I’m busy.’ I ventured to ask for her number. She pretended she didn’t hear me and started wrapping up the conversation. She then politely took her leave. I felt like a massive fool. Serves me right I guess.

What is an example of someone who underestimated the wrong individual? In my first year of secondary (high) school, taunting and chest-beating was a norm amongst the more silly and immature boys like myself. Balram was an Indian boy who came from rural poverty. He wore worn clothes, kept an outdated hairstyle and mostly kept to himself to avoid the others making fun of him (which they constantly did). They would call him bush-coolie, Mowgli, Balram of the Jungle and various other insulting names. Balram would sit and deflect their insults with the stoic calmness of a Navajo chief. He was an acquaintance of mine but we were not close. However a group of boys looking to make a ruckus started taunting me that I was so weak, even bush boy Balram could beat me up, I quickly took to the offence. I rushed up to Balram who anticipated that I would fall for the bait and before I could say 'Bal’ he pinned me against the wall with two sinewy hands against my shoulders and told me to behave myself. Everyone was astonished at Balram's strength. After struggling to escape his grip for a several seconds he saw I was worn out and released me. That day forward I never messed with Balram and even became his good friend. The class still teased him, but this time they made sure they were at a safe distance when doing so.

I'm a school custodian and when people ask me what's my job I'm ashamed to tell them. What's the best way I could say what I do without saying I'm a custodian? Embrace the fact that you are a janitor. Yes. I said it. A janitor. You work for a living. You work hard. You are valuable salt of the Earth. People feel comfortable around you and feel more at ease to talk to you because you hold no airs about yourself. People admire you because you do a job that most people don't want and when you do it with pride you are an inspiration. I'm sure if you tell the staff around you your plans to get a degree or invest in a small business you will get an overwhelming amount of support. Everyone loves to see the little guy make small steps. No one likes to hear the big rich CEO gushing about a planned merger or a thriving stock portfolio. No. People love to hear about the janitor who saved his money and started his own cleaning company. You also have the benefit of always knowing who are your real friends. Lawyers, doctors and politicians don't have that benefit. Everyone is running to kiss their ass and use them. Nobody is running to kiss Larry the janitor’s ass and use him. You know that people who don't respect you or your work, no matter how well you perform it, are people to stay away from. You don't have to have your back against the wall to see your enemies. Be proud of who you are. You work hard. Not many people do that. And if anyone asks what you do for a living say with pride that you are a school janitor. Their reaction will say a lot about them Written by a former delivery ‘boy.’

What’s your favorite movie based on true events? The Founder (2016) This is a movie I habitually return to watching. It's an inspiring movie but it's not a ‘feelgood’ movie per se. The movie tells the story of how a run of the mill salesman named Ray Kroc outmanoeuvred and outperformed the McDonald brothers and became owner of the McDonald's franchise/empire. I say it's not feelgood because, based on the film, Kroc was not by any account a ‘nice’ man when it came to business. He was a conniving opportunist but at the same time he was also unrelentingly persistent. His partners, the altruistic McDonald brothers derived a brilliant concept and product but had little interest in franchising and/or wealth. It is because of Kroc's persistence and willingness to take great risks that McDonald's is the success that it is today. If there is one concept the movie begs you to take away from it, regardless of your view of Ray Kroc, it is the value of persistence. Without giving away too much of the plot, this is what is inspiring about Kroc's efforts. There are so many profound scenes and quotes in this movie that it find it hard for anyone to not appreciate it for the sole merit that it generates a lot of thought, regardless of whether you don't like it or find Ray Kroc reprehensible. I think Michael Keaton gave his greatest performance and I was thoroughly disappointed that he was not nominated for an Academy Award. His persistence speech at the end of the film, I consider to be a classic in business motivation, trumping that of Jordan Belfort’s ‘sell me this pen’ in The Wolf of Wall Street and Alec Baldwin's ‘Always be closing’ scene in Glengarry Glen Ross. I beg to debate this opinion.

Can you give an example of a TV program you watched as a kid and thought it was cool or sophisticated, but seeing it as an adult you think it is dumb or appalling? Tales From the Darkside. Dum dum da da………..Dum dum da da My brother and I would stay up late at nights watching Sci-Fi (now SyFy) just to hear that chilling intro. It was absolutely terrifying to hear those eerily innocent yet menacing keyboard notes accompanied with this ominous voiceover and the placid shot of trees, rivers and rural farmhouses suddenly melt into a distorted final image and caption. (Nothing beats the horror aesthetic of late 80s/early 90s television and film.) We would play a game to see who could sit and watch the intro in its entirety without running into the bedroom or hiding behind the couch. Neither of us succeeded. But it was thrilling nonetheless. I wish the show itself was thrilling though. The ‘tales,’ quality-wise, ranged from uninteresting to appallingly corny. Take a look at some screenshots and be the judge.

The network that shook the world with Beavis and Butthead and Jackass, is now proudly giving us a middle aged man dressed and behaving like a 13 yr old whose daddy was never home, a pretty blonde, human laugh-track who would find a grain of boiled rice uproariously funny and a token, black guy who's job it is to supervise their swag attempts. This wouldn't have bothered me as much had it not been for the fact that the show is a complete rip off of Tosh.0. Why do the rich become richer and the poor poorer? Consider the above drawing. The mountain represents varying degrees of wealth. Poverty, represented by the area at the red P is the most steep area at the slope. Any wrong move, any poor investment, bad financial decision, heck even non action itself would lead to the climber slipping off the slope and down to rock bottom. People born into poverty have to climb that steep slope. There are no second chances. Once you fall you are either dead, crippled or lucky enough to just simply lose the motivation to try climbing again. Stability represented by the blue S is the area where the mountain becomes less steep. You can relax a bit. It is no longer a fight for survival. Most people aspire for stability; a decent job, a nice house and car and loving family. If you make a bad move you are on such stable grounds that you can simply pick yourself back up but too many mistakes and you slip right back into poverty. Wealth represented by the green W is the area where, with just a little additional effort during Stability, you can make it near the top of the mountain. Though you can slip and fall back into poverty it's very unlikely. Any further effort and you will land yourself at the top of the mountain, the super wealthy, the select few at the very top. Here's why the poor get poorer and the rich get richer: The slope representing poverty is steep and long whilst the slope from stability into wealth is steep but not nearly as long. What does this mean? It's harder and takes much longer for poor people to get out of poverty than it is for well-off people to get more rich.
