What is the biggest lie society has taught you to believe? The 'strategy’ that worked for your parents will work for you. In Trinidad we have two different generations with two different mindsets. For ease of understanding I will label them: Any colonial Trinidadian will tell you that the older generation was far different from the modern non colonial, many will argue that, in terms of morals, norms and values, the Colonial mindset was better. The Colonials were greatly influenced by British standards. The path to one's success was deemed to be how closely he/she can emulate an upper class English person. Great emphasis was placed on education, speech (or the ability to speak the Queen's tongue without the influence of corruptive local dialect) and there was manic obsession of gaining recognition by ruling agents of our English masters through social acceptance (a combination of race and etiquette played a big role), scholarship, sport (mainly cricket) and if all else fails, kissing your parents goodbye and hopping aboard the HMT Windrush to the seek opportunity in the land of the Queen. Colonial parents were obsessed with their children's grades. Education was seen as the only means of upward mobility for those who had no other means of gaining English recognition. All of life seemed to be based around this rigid structure of class. The non-Colonials had little to no influence from the British. Those born after 1962 were privy to witness a near chaotic transition to self Government. Speaking proper English and demonstrating a level 'class’ now bore little to no impact on social mobility. Education and good grades provided some measure of success in life but was far less impactful than under British rule. Success was a combination of personal capitalistic drive and being 'in the know’ of certain opportunities the Government provided or exploits to be exploited. The US rather than the UK was now the chief model of success. Most of the laws the British provided were still in place but everyone from the the beggar on the street to the highest titled Government official approached them in 'read between the lines’ or 'you're only guilty if you're caught manner.’ The system is less rigid, less Draconian from the past, allowing, for better measures of opportunity for all levels of society but at the same time it operates within an opportunitistic, 'do as the Romans do,’ style bordering on controlled anarchy. As a boy I was drilled into believing that the path to success is getting good grades, speaking good English, maintaining a proper image, obeying the law and respecting elders. Now if I were to impart such wisdom to an average boy of this generation I would be scoffed at, not just by the boy, but also by his parents.

What’s the biggest thing people take for granted in your country? Land Development and Planning. Trinidad and Tobago scores a D when it comes to how we treat our land, how we value our land and how we exploit all resources involved with land. Just looking out my window I can spot several major infringements of land use, town and country regulations and the law in general. This is an apartment complex recently built opposite me. It should not be there. Why? Because as indicated by the arrows it is built under major power lines and next to one of the transmission towers. The photograph doesn’t demonstrate it but it is also on land lower than the road, making it vulnerable to flooding (of which the area is infamous for). The owner also didn’t see the need to finish a proper road and drain, rather just have some slippery gravel and aggregate and a dirt ditch alongside it. Not to mention a tiny makeshift unsecured bin, hardly noticeable in the right corner, susceptible to animals and for garbage falling into the drain. This is someone looking to profit off of land through renting apartments. In fact several locations in this area has seen an increase in these poorly planned apartment complexes built on lands that are not developed and/or restricted towards such use e.g on or near water courses, under power lines, earmarked for future roads etc. (As per above photos it is the norm for apartments and sometimes even entire private/state developments to be made and sold/rented/leased with little to no proper land development involved.) I’m no Town and Country Planning expert but with my limited knowledge I see infringements everywhere I go. People do what they want and the Government throws a blind eye and vice versa. We have many sprawling communities that develop in short time with little concern to what they see as minor issues such as drainage, waste and garbage disposal, efficient road networks, efficient water distribution etc. These guerilla communities make a domino effect in such that communities further down the line suffer from the bottlenecks and problems brought forward by a complete disregard of central planning. It is not uncommon to see garbage piled on the side of the road because people have sprawling and meandering hamlets with tiny narrow roads that twist and turn on a drunken path to nowhere, unable to allow for services such as garbage collection and other utility trucks to enter. Most people in the country do not get a steady supply of water in the country because of the lack of regulations and the increased demand for water when several people illegally build communities in locations that have already met its quota for residences to have a proper daily supply. The domino effect is ugly. People who have long maintained their land and property are now surrounded by these hastily built shantytowns. With them come an increase in traffic, crime, disregard to basic civil laws and a likewise reduction in the services that most communities enjoy. It also cuts off the potential for further development. No one wants to open a bowling alley, a Holiday Inn or a drive through cinema in a location that reminds them of the Wild West. Unregulated and illegal settling allows for an increase in the amount of illegal quarrying and polluting which creates a disruption of natural watercourses. This combined with large settlements, built without any prior land development and town and country standards, making flooding more disastrous than ever before in history. I know every country in the world suffers with varying degrees the issues brought forward by poor planning and regulation. However I would safely say that whereas in developed countries it is an issue found in small pockets of the country, typically in sparsely populated rural areas. In Trinidad and Tobago it is widespread and found practically everywhere, urban and rural. The problem here is a complete disregard of addressing the issue. In the past this was an issue that was an understandable reaction to poverty. It stemmed mostly from the inability of the Government to provide the housing needs for those who couldn’t afford property. Now it’s become simply a bad habit fostered from rich to poor, contractor to state official, peasant farmer to CEO; everyone is just making themselves comfortable doing what they please and in the end everyone is paying for it.

Is it superficial that I lost interest in a guy because he proudly said that he hasn't read any book in his life? Here's the point of view of a somewhat bookish male. First of all I would say that you've started wrong by considering something he claims about himself. A man (a many women in general) will say all kinds of things to give some kind of impression. In his case he is bragging that he doesn't like books/reading. He probably comes from a rugged environment where reading books is looked down upon as dandyish, antisocial and/or overly sensitive. I come from such an environment. Trinidad is a literate country but for males the stereotypical clumsy, scatterbrained geek who hides behind books because he is afraid to tackle worldly experiences is a prominent stigma. Even if you speak meticulously with proper English words that contain more than two syllables you are regarded with suspicion. Many females are raised to avoid these type of men. Him being proud not reading books is, to me, an ego driven declaration of machismo. You shouldn't let that be a deciding factor though. When younger I always sought after intellectual type girls with whom I could discuss the arts, philosophy, politics, classic literature etc. Sadly relationships never seemed too work out with for a myriad of reasons the chief problem being a severe lack of emotional intelligence. Now that I'm older, the last quality I look for in a woman in how much books she has read in life. Literacy and intelligence are two completely different types of wisdom and I would argue that the latter is far more important than the former. Just because he doesn't read doesn't mean he is any less wise, thoughtful, caring and responsible than the average guy. I've met too many literate women who are a financial and emotional trainwreck to allow for the notion that book reading is a make or break factor in a relationship. Just my two cents.

If you could choose only one font which one would it be and why? Without a doubt Gill Sans. Something about these World War II era fonts stirs up romantic and escapist feelings within my subconscious. From these ugly times came this beautiful, almost flawless font. I’m no anglophile but the British (specifically Eric Gill employed at the prestigious Monotone company) knew a thing or two about subtlety, graceful curvature and ‘breathing space’ when it came to eye-catching typefaces. Symmetry is the essence of being and Gill Sans makes every effort to be symmetrical yet bold and demanding. It is referred to as a ‘humanist’ font, in that it is easily legible in text and display to the extent that lines do not overlap or meld into each other. Intricate focus is put on the roundness of its letters, most notably, having a perfect circle for the ‘O’ Gill Sans, to me, conjures up images of RAF fighter planes heading eastwards in formation, Orwell interviewing coal miners at their last breath due to tuberculosis, children in rags catching colored butterflies amidst the rubble of buildings blown to pieces in Dresden and the decay of British Raj. Terrible times indeed but captured in various newspapers, flyers and magazines with this pleasant font which made many nations feel hope for better times to come.

Are there parents who regret having mixed-race children? My paternal grandfather Anthony Roy Hughes was a white Grenadian and his wife Mona (paternal grandmother) was a mixed raced Grenadian. Together they had six children and enjoyed an upper middle class existence after they both migrated to Trinidad, him working for Shell Oil and her working as a French school teacher. They bought a large house together in a picturesque neighborhood called Cascade. Things were definitely not as happy as it appears in the above photos. Grandfather was abusive with untreated manic depression/bipolar symtoms. It was said by my family that he never truly loved my grandmother. His original goal was to find a white wife (as was the norm during colonial times) and she was the closest thing he could get towards that goal. It was also said that he gave preferable treatment to his more Caucasoid children and was particularly unloving to the others who weren't (my father [center of the above photo] being a prime target due to his being the darkest of the lot). In just a few years within the marriage he lost his job at Shell Oil as being seen as unfit. Despite being given a severance payout he depended on his wife's teaching salary to provide for him and the children. Jobless and prone to depressive episodes he would make every attempt to find merriment outside of his home and when he did come home his frustrations over his incapacities and failures were taken out on his wife and children. My aunt would tell me that they would hear him singing drunken songs as he came up the hill towards the house and according to what song he sang, they would know whether he was ready to give everyone a whupping or if he would go shut himself in his bedroom for several hours. They prayed that it would be the latter. He depended on his wife's salary and her kind nature to hold the family together, pay the bills and take care of the house. Meanwhile he repaid her kindness by being more physically and emotionally abusive. Grandma was stricken with motor neuron disease in her early 40s and wasted away wheelchair bound for the last years of her life, passing away at the relatively young age of 48. All this tragedy and abuse contributed to their children suffering from various neuroses and mental illnesses. Only two managed to have some measure of success in their personal lives while the rest succumbed to directionless lives of struggle and financial and mental hardships, the youngest committing suicide at age 40 and two recently passing away alone and in squalor. But rather than delve into personal history (and there's a lot), let me answer the original question. Are there parents who regret having mixed-raced children? It is possible that my grandfather regretted his mixed raced children and harbored deep prejudices. It is also possible that he loved his mixed race children but his untreated mental illness brought out the worst in him. The answer in regards to my grandfather is probably. He showed no remorse when his wife died, relieved himself of any further fatherly duties and made no attempt to establish communication with his children. He sold the house and remarried (his long sought after white bride) a few years after his first wife's death. He died a lonely divorcée in 1994. Would he have made a greater effort to be a better father if he had found his white bride and had a flock of children, all the same complexion as him? No one knows.

What is the most pointless crime you've witnessed? I worked for a short stint as an usher in a multiplex cinema franchise. One of the perks of working in the cinema was that you get to watch as much movies as you want for free on your day off. You could also bring one partner with you. One of our newer teenaged employees didn't fully understand the perk and believed it to be 'one movie, one guest.’ My friends and I recognized this to be his understanding because he would always come with his little brother and after watching his one movie, we would spot him in the corner of our eyes making a lame attempt to sneak into another room with his little baby brother in tow. It was such a cute sight to behold that I informed the rest of the staff about his little crime and many of us would come out to see him snooping about after his movie, pretending to hold conversation with concessions staff or feigning interest in the posters and then the minute our back was turned would run into another showing. He was just so terrible at the 'crime’ that it was almost heartwarming to witness our two freeloaders scurrying about like mice whenever we pretended to turn our backs. It's only when the manager confronted him as to why he acted so strange did the pieces finally fall into place for him. We all rubbed it in how much we enjoyed his lame attempts at petty crime.

What are some dirty tactics used by fast food restaurants? I worked delivery for a popular local pizzeria in Trinidad for some years and left somewhat dishonorably discharged after having arguments with management over a growing reliance on a dirty, illegal tactic that they employed with no discretion. I can best describe it by means of a short skit. Customer: Hi. Good day. Do you have any specials today? Newly Employed Cashier: Good day. Our Monday special is two large pizzas for only $100. Customer: That's great. That's like two for the price of one. I'll have it. Newly Employed Cashier: Yes. We have a different specials everyday. You can check them online or simply ask us. Customer: I appreciate. Great service. The Manager is in the background keenly observing the proceedings. After the customer leaves she approaches the cashier. Manager: Did you just sell that man two pizzas for $100? Newly Employed Cashier: Uh...yeah...the special? Manager: So you sold just the two pizza special? What about the donuts and cookies that we’ll have to discard this evening? What about the salad? I need you to sell all of these before the end of the day. Newly Employed Cashier: I'm trying but most people just want the two pizzas for $100 special. Manager: This branch doesn’t have a two pizzas for $100 special. Our special is two pizzas, four donuts, four cookies and a salad for $160. Newly Employed Cashier: But that's not what we have advertised. What if….. Manager: What if we have this discussion about this in Head Office tomorrow? A new customer walks in with his wife and two children and approaches the cashier. Customer 2: Hi. I heard you guys have some kind of special for two pizzas? The cashier glances at the Manager staring at her. Newly Employed Cashier: Yes. Two pizzas, four donuts, four cookies and a salad for $160. Customer 2: Okay. I really don't want all that other stuff. I could've sworn I saw online it was just two pizzas for the price of one….? He stares intently at the cashier and hoping for her to give him the offer he wanted. His wife then urges him to take the offer as the kids are getting restless. The customer grudgingly accepts. The customer behind him is well dressed in a suit and is discussing a legal matter with a client on his cell phone. Customer 3: Hi. I'll have the two pizza special. One pepperoni, the other veggie. Newly Employed Cashier: The special today is two pizzas with four donuts… She feels a nudge on her arm. The Manager is motioning for her to shut up. The Manager enters the order just as the customer asked. The customer takes his bill and moves away. Manager: I'm going to spend the rest of the day giving you additional training in sales. You need to know how to sell and who to sell.

What is the shadiest industry you've worked in? In 2009 right after the whole world was reeling from the AIG insurance scandal, I decided now was a good time to quit my job and and follow the lucrative career of an insurance salesman. What happened was Jason, an old school friend, told me that while attending University, he was selling life insurance policies at his leisure. He told me he made enough money (commissions) in just a couple of months that he was able purchase a car. He also rubbed in the fact that he could afford to purchase decent clothes and go out for a night-life whenever he felt like it. I would be lying if I said I didn’t envy him. The ripple effects of the 2008 recession took a while to impact Trinidad and suddenly our insurance firms were affected, most notably CLICO which had to be bailed out by the Government. ‘You sure selling insurance is a good idea now? With CLICO and all?’ I asked him. ‘Yeah,’ he said. I was convinced. I immediately quit my job and applied to work in the same insurance company and branch that Jason was employed in. Literally, the very same day I started training was the day Jason quit. As I walked in the door he had already collected his belongings and was walking out. ‘Hey bro what’s up?’ I said concernedly, ‘You leaving?’ ‘Just for a little while,’ he replied, ‘I just have a few credits until I graduate. I need to focus on my studies.’ He then left. I was confused. Didn’t he tell me insurance selling was very flexible in regards to his University studies? I tried not to let that bother me and ignore the looming sense of dread that I made a huge mistake quitting my permanent job to go sell insurance on commission in the midst of a global recession and countless insurance scandals. The seasoned insurance salespeople were all warm and friendly. Half of them queried as to whether I had life insurance. A few of them tried (semi-jokingly) to sell me life insurance right then and there. The branch was named after the lead insurance salesman i.e. branch manager, Cecil. He did the training sessions. He was a short, squat middle-aged man with a comical demeanor who loved to include fart jokes in everything he said. He excited us trainees by telling us that if we sold enough policies we could live off the commissions like him. He said he made enough commissions that he didn’t need to sell policies anymore. That all his clients’ premiums (insurance payments) were paying him enough to live comfortably and he was here for fun. I wondered how that was possible. Wasn’t the commissions a one-off thing? It’s not like the insurance salesman gets money every time the insured person pays his premium. ‘Yes!’ the branch manager responded excitedly, ‘You get paid every time your client pays his insurance. A small percentage of each payment goes to us.That’s why I tell my clients when they buy a policy from me, I’m now part of their family……because their payments literally make me part of their family. When daddy goes and pay his premium and buys a new pair of shoes for sonnyboy, Uncle Cecil gets money to buy a new pair of shoes also.’ All the sales agents began to laugh at this. I was then taught the basic tools of selling life insurance policies. And much more. After the training all the newbies were teamed up with a senior agent and left to go find prospects. My coach, Stephen, told me that all insurance agents have their niches. Cecil was good with churchy type families, Lara, the sole female agent was good with police officers and defense force type men and he himself was good with salt of the earth type men i.e. taxi drivers, construction workers, tradesmen etc with security guards being his specialty. He said because his niche weren’t very reliable in regards to being consistent in paying their premiums, that he was one of the lowest performing agents. Stephen’s technique was basically to visit rolling-stone type men who were delinquent with child-support and bully them into ‘at least taking out a policy for the sake of your children.’ After a week I finally got a policy sold. I had the paperwork to file for my first client. Stephen told me to put it in the pile with the others. He directed me to a vacant office where I saw boxes upon boxes of insurances policies pending to be filed and entered into the database. ‘Who’s going to file all those?’ I asked. ‘The girl left the job two months ago,’ he replied, ‘When we get a new girl she has her work cut out for her.’ ‘So my client’s policy…’ I said concernedly, ‘All of these policies aren’t filed yet?’ ‘No,’ he replied. ‘What if something happens to my client like right now? What if she gets in a freak accident today? Her name isn’t even on the database...’ Stephen paused for a minute and then said, ‘There are some things you just shouldn’t worry about in this organization.’ Needless to say my stint in that particular insurance organization ended a few days later.

What’s a typical “masculine” thing you do not want/like to do? There are many ‘masculine’ things I don't like or not appreciate as much as other men due to ineptitude. Libations We call this 'a toast to the fallen soldiers’ in Trinidad. This is a macho habit of pouring some of your premium liquor on the floor after you just opened a new bottle in reverence of friends and acquaintances who passed away. I think it's stupid. What if your 'fallen soldiers’ didn't drink? What if alcohol caused their death in the first place? It's not as common here as it used to be but whenever you’re with a group of friends there's always that one salty hermit who proposes that you throw some of your Johnny Walker Blue or Glenlivet 18 yr on the floor in toast of 'his fallen warriors.’ It's funny how the guys who ask for these type toasts are the one who never bring a bottle themselves. A Round of Drinks for Everyone Or 'buying a rounds’ as we call it in Trinidad. When you go to a bar with your friends everyone takes a turn in buying a round of drinks (usually beers) for all members in the group. I'm not cheap it's just that this is one of the worst demonstrations of economic inefficiency and inequity in the world. Firstly, you start of with a small group, usually about five of you. The first guy to buy a round gets off the hook with just having to buy about five beers. Then, before you know it, a friend of a friend comes in, then someone's uncle, then some guy someone knows from way back when, then the cheap, sneaky brown-nose at work and before you know it, you have to buy a round for your friends and all these people you don't know (and in some cases, don’t like). Many of these un-invitees ‘just happen to be passing through’ and never fulfill their duty to buy a round themselves. They drink their free beer and flee, taking advantage of the intoxicated group. It's ridiculous. Another reason buying rounds is a waste is cold beer gets lukewarm in a short space of time. Many times I would be drinking a beer and forced to discard the lukewarm ones because the other beers are coming in so fast. The round of drinks culture needs a modern day revamping. Under the hood chit-chat I'm no mechanic. But even if I were mechanically inclined I'm always dumbfounded to see men gather round staring at their car engines and discussing what modifications they had done, the hell they went through building a bracket to install such and such new engine, V8 versus Rotary, CA18det vs SR20de, NOS vs Turbo, carburetor vs fuel injected etc etc. The amount of time some guys spend on discussing the transformation of their piece o junk Sunnys, Lancers and Familias (their ‘beast’ as they like to call them) is astonishing for me. Even non-gearheads who just got their first vehicle get carried away with under the hood chit-chat even though they have no idea what their peers are talking about. Unless I’m getting good car maintenance/repair advice, under the hood chit-chat bores me. Team/Player/Club Fanaticism (Football) ‘Watch the rest of the World Cup? Are you crazy? Brazil just got massacred. Luiz and Neymar are still (sob) in tears. Go away!’ ‘How the hell can you support both Real Madrid and Barcelona? Bandwagonist!’ ‘I bet you $500 Messi has a bigger penis than Ronaldo.’ ‘Pele is God. Balotelli is Jesus.’ ‘Zidane has the IQ of a caveman. Keep Deschamps.’ And so on. Football fanatics take pride in making such ridiculous statements like a badge of honour. The more outlandish and provocative your statement regarding whatever popular team, player or club, the more psychopathic your obsession is the more warmly fellow football fanatics would accept you as one of theirs. It’s a good idea to befriend them though. Football fanatics are exceedingly loyal and generous to their fellow fanboys. ‘Look at my big bad dog.’ It’s always been a mystery to me why some of my fellow men have an almost cult like worship of possessing the biggest, baddest dog in the neighborhood. Some men are more proud and dedicated to their mean pitbulls, rottweilers, mastiffs and dobermans than they are of their own children. Putting up that ‘Beware of Dog’ sign is almost an orgasmic experience for them. They gather together in groups to discuss unique ways of maltreating these dogs (training they call it) to make them as mean as possible. They almost always do this stupid prank where they approach you with their dog on a leash and tell you that it’s ok to pet it. When you attempt to, their dogs snaps viciously towards your hand and the owners raise their heads in laughter and pride. Many of them end up getting mauled by their own mistreated dogs. And finally My most detested ‘macho’ thing of all time…. ‘Bro’ talk For centuries, being well-spoken, cultured and organized in thoughts and words is seen as weird, effeminate, pompous and pretentious to so-called macho men. In Trinidad, the larger the group of men, the more dumbed down the conversation. Emoting is a no-no. Using words that have more than three syllables is a no-no. Soliloquizing is a big no-no. ‘Macho’ men always repeat ‘you understand, you understand’ but nobody really understands what they’re saying. No need to sound snobby myself but listening to self-appointed macho men talk about deeper issues on the radio is a cringe worthy affair: CRIME ‘We have to fix this community. You understand? We have to look in the mirror and know that ‘crime’ ends with ‘me.’ You understand? It’s like [insert another cliched parable/quote]. You understand? The youths…..You know? Think about the youths.’ Or try telling a macho man about your compounding personal problems/crisis: ‘That’s how it is……..it not easy………you understand?’ Or discussing the Machiavellian undertones in the Prime Minister’s new campaign speech. ‘Wha’ da f**k you smoke?’ If there is one thing I definitely wish to see change in the macho ideals is an ideal towards articulation of thoughts and efficient communication. You understand?

Who was the rudest person you’ve ever encountered? And what was your response? Some years ago I was working the late shift at my part time job doing pizza delivery. I was taking phone calls when a smug, off-putting voice was suddenly heard on the other end of the line. 'Are you hearing me? This is Michael Griffith. G-r-i-f-f-i-t-h.’ There was a second of silence as I registered that that the person didn't even bother to say 'Good Evening.’ I acknowledged that I could hear him and subtly mentioned that I could spell. I then proceeded to ask him for more information. 'I have been a regular customer to this restaurant for over 15 years. I like my pizzas done a special way. Are you listening……what is your name?’ 'Elijah sir.’ 'I want a veggie pizza. Listen to how I want it……Are you hearing me?……..I want the dough baked with the pizza sauce and cheese, nothing else added………are you writing this down?…….Then I want the raw veggies added after the pizza has been cooked. DO NOT COOK MY VEGGIES. I REPEAT. DO NOT COOK THE VEGGIES ON MY PIZZA.’ I tried my best to separate this man's condescending tone and my feelings towards him and mentally process exactly what it was he requested. We always got customers who felt entitled to have their pizza done in some special way. Either they wanted their pizza baked separate from all other pizzas or their dough must be of a certain grade or the pineapples must be cut from fresh fruit and not from our canned stock. Most of the time we ignored them and just gave them what they (and everyone else) were paying for. Most of the time they just wanted to feel bourgeois. This guy however was adamant that I make his pizza with raw veggies. What this guy didn't seem to realize was that these veggies were never freshly cut veggies. These were precut veggies sitting overnight in a plastic tub in a chiller, probably swarming with bacterial matter. Cooking these veggies in the oven was his only defense against E-coli. If he were to get sick from eating his beloved raw veggie pizza, he could hold us accountable and sue and I would be the one to get the blame. I diplomatically expressed to him that we couldn't make his pizza in such a manner, that it was a risk to his health and against the company's policy. In anger he asked for my name a second time. 'Listen to me young man. I am arriving in 15 minutes and if I do not see my veggie pizza prepared the way I want it, I am going to deal with you.’ He then hung up the phone. I explained what just happened to the cashier and she agreed with me that the guy was an idiot and that we couldn't give him a raw veggie pizza. I processed the pizza order as a regular veggie pizza and continued taking calls. Fifteen minutes later I'm in the back, about to head out on a delivery when I heard a smug but familiar voice bellowing out at front counter, 'WHERE'S THAT STUPID BOY NIGEL?’ I looked in front to see Mr. E-coli in the flesh. He looked exactly like how I imagined he would look; large, big-bellied and bespectacled. He was middle aged and greying, with a thick bottom lip that projected outwards in perpetual disgust at the world in front of him. I kid you not he looked like the human version of the obnoxious character Bubble Bass from SpongeBob. Immediately my entire physique and mental structure took to the offense. I literally wanted to clobber this idiot. However, I marched to the front counter to confront him and use all my powers of vocabulary to diplomatically explain to him that he was an idiot and that he was not getting a raw veggie pizza from this branch. As if to make himself as repulsive as ever, with him was a preteen girl (either his niece or daughter) with whom he tried to exaggerate how tough he was, by yelling and berating, mostly female minimum wage paid fast food workers. 'Listen to me,' he shouted at the cashier, 'Remove this pizza and get me what I ordered. I want to see that boy who took my order.’ He then spread a creepy smile over his face, turned to the little girl and cooed, 'You’re gonna taste the real way to eat pizza.’ The poor little girl looked like she wished she could disappear at the moment. Everything about the guy was just so off-putting in an incongruent sense. He was like a living, breathing 'Can you find all the things wrong in this picture’ cartoon brought to life. 'I'm the one who took your order sir,’ I said with seething rage as he glanced me, ‘And you can't get a raw veggie pizza.’ I saw him turn red. This was no longer about the pizza. This was about him proving himself to that little girl. 'You telling me what I can or can't get?’ he bellowed, 'You want me to knock you out?’ I stood there waiting for the tub of lard to attack when the manager flew out her office and came between us. In her best prepared monologue she explained she was sorry for his inconvenience. The manager told me to go to the back. In anger I listened as she explained the danger of consuming such a pizza but acquiesced to his demand. After I cooled down some minutes later I grabbed a delivery and en route to my motorcycle out front I spotted him shovelling away his bacteria ridden pizza in his mouth and commanding the little girl to do the same. He gave me a nervous sideglance as I passed, then continued goading her to finish her slice. I asked God to protect that little girl from getting sick and pleaded that He not allow more idiots like that man to multiply on this Earth.

Who are the most uncomfortable movie characters depicting the UK that you’ve ever seen? Gotta go with three films and I'm listing the characters based on the level of discomfort (low to high). *** Spoilers ahead *** Movie: Saturday Night and Sunday Morning (1960) Character(s): Arthur Location: Nottingham The late, great Albert Finney gives a magnificent performance as Arthur, a rebellious, young, working class man who has somewhat of a fetish for stirring up trouble and going beyond the limit. The title refers to the fact that Arthur begins his trouble immediately after his work ends on Saturday. He dedicates his Saturday nights to going out pubs and drinking himself beyond consciousness, stirring up trouble in the streets, fighting etc. His Sundays are spent engaging in a sexual affair with the equally defiant wife of his mild-mannered co-worker. He eventually gets her pregnant while hiding his deeds from his own morally virtuous girlfriend. In the final scene Arthur confesses his actions to his girlfriend who forgives him and gets him to agree to marry her and settle down. Arthur agrees but angrily throws a stone at a nearby building. His girlfriend asks 'What did you do that for?’ He replies, 'Just felt like it I suppose.’ I don't live in the UK but I know and have befriended many Arthurs throughout my life here in Trinidad. Arthurs can never find inner peace and unknowingly to themselves, foster a subconscious hatred towards structure, routine and normalcy. They believe that a stone must be thrown into the rolling cogs every so often otherwise life would just be uneventful and monotonous. At their best Arthurs can be just angry, resentful troublemakers but at their worst they can be psychopathic narcissists who cause harm and destruction to all those who engage with them. Arthur in this film was a downright bastard in this kitchen-sink classic and anyone not interested in him as a character study would simply find him mildly repugnant. Movie: Kill List (2011) Character(s): Jay Location: Sheffield Kill List is something of a psychological/supernatural horror inspired by the fiction of HP Lovecraft. However there's nothing fictional about the character Jay. He's a menacing, angry and uncouth ex-soldier turned contract killer, quite possibly suffering from PTSD from a botched mission. He has a son and a wife who urges him to take a normal job as they are in financial distress but Jay prefers to wait for that one big contract job that would provide for him for years to come. His 'luck’ arrives as a friend of his wife hires him to eliminate various unnamed people in a mysterious Kill List. Jay and his friend are given locations of the targets The Priest, The Librarian and The MP. Each kill becomes more mysterious than the last with both of the first two victims softly thanking Jay before being killed. The 2nd kill unearths video evidence of an underground society involved in the most, depraved and disturbing acts imaginable causing Jay to become even more unsettled. Jay's final kill leads him to a mansion where a some sort of pagan cult is taking place with several figures hidden in white robes are having a ceremony. Believing these to be the people involved in the depraved videos he starts shooting them, killing some and manages to kill the leader. However he is captured and forced to a knife-fight with a robed hunchback figure. Viciously stabbing the hunchback all over its body, it is revealed afterwards to be his wife with their son strapped to her back. His final kill was his own family. I believe Kill List to be a portrayal of a man with psychosis and schizophrenia brought on by severe PTSD. Neil Maskell gives a phenomenal performance as Jay. His consistently scowling face and venemous tone make him such an unsettling character that I fear ever running into such a person on a lonely side street at night. I may be wrong but I interpret a lot of the happenings to be solely in Jay's imagination. Jay saw his own killings as something as a grand mission against evil so as to erase guilt from a botched mission in Kyiv where he, quite possibly, had to do heinous acts to survive. Kill List, to me, is a heightened portrayal of a mentally unstable man. Movie: Eden Lake (2008) Character(s): The parents Location: London Condemned by critics for stereotyping and exaggerating the 'Broken Britain’ underclass this film is relentless in its portrayal of savagery. Jenny and Steve are a couple vacationing and decide a visit a lake near a working class community. Steve is highly critical of the behaviour of the children of the area and the parents' role in their poor upbringing. Even though the lake is condemned to become a quarry Steve and Jenny sneak in for a final visit but become targets of a gang of local delinquent 'Chavs’ driven by a maniacal leader Brett. After constantly being harassed by the youths, a fight ensues in which Brett's dog is killed. Enraged he eventually raises the stakes by capturing Steve and having members of the group stab him to death while being filmed. Jenny is then captured and with botched attempts to kill her as well, Brett murders two of his own gang members while the rest look on silently. In the ensuing chase two other members of the gang are killed. Bleeding to near death and dirty, Jenny manages to run to a nearby house where a house party involving several middle aged locals are taking place. There is copious drug, alcohol and sex among the members and even though it is certain that these people are not her cup of tea she seeks help from one of the more sympathetic women. However she soon realises that many of them are parents of the gang and when one of the women get a police call informing of her murdered son, the parents suspect her and suddenly transform into 'we look after our own’ monsters. As far fetched as Brett and the gang is portrayed, I believe a good job was done portraying the parents. There are so many communities of families out there who have vague morals in regards to greater society but a strict code of secrecy and loyalty for themselves. Despite many of the horrific scenes in the movie, nothing was more uncomfortable and disturbing than this final scene. There is no major onscreen violence during the last five minutes but just looking at Jenny hiding in the bathroom as she hears the voices of the parents of these monsters (learning of their dead kids) screaming in trauma and yelling in rage as she acknowledges the fact that they will soon kill her makes it the most uncomfortable scene I've ever witnessed in a film set in the UK.

What screams "I'm rich, but I have no class"? Some years ago I was at a supermarket looking to pick up a drink. Strangely enough the clothes I wore was similar to the uniform that the workers wore. After I cashed I stood looking at some snacks near a cashier. A lady who looked well-to-do had finished cashing for a heaping trolley of goods and was making ‘Psst, Psst’ noises in my direction. I looked at her. She motioned with her head that her trolley was ready to be carted out. ‘It’s the white X-Trail on the right,’ she said nonchalantly. She apparently thought I was a worker-boy and wanted me to carry her stuff out for her and help her load it into her vehicle. I eyed the cashier who gave me faint, knowing smile. I decided to play along. I took her trolley and rolled off with it. The lady walked a few paces behind me staring at me with more solemnity than a prison guard. It was as if she didn't want to be near me and at the same time wanted to make sure I didn't steal any of her stuff To complete the disguise of a lowly grocery-boy I attempted to make friendly small talk. ‘Looks like it's gonna have some serious rain later.’ She didn't answer. She just kept staring at me and keeping a few feet behind me. The probability that she was just a mean, old rich twat was getting higher and higher. I decided to administer one more test. All of a sudden I stopped the cart, looked at my watch and said, ‘Hey it's time for my lunch date. Later.’ I then walked a few paces away from her and her trolley and pretended to make a phone call. ‘Excuse me!’ she said with venom on her tongue. ‘Hey I'm on the phone,’ I said with gusto at her and gestured a finger to my mouth. I tried my best not to burst out in laughter. One of the workers who kept guard near the entrance door saw all this. He himself tried not to laugh. She went up to him. ‘What’s that boy's name?’ ‘I dunno’ the man replied, stifling a chuckle. ‘Is he stupid or something?’ she spat, ‘Tell him to come back and get my stuff.’ It was so beautiful to watch. I couldn't have responded better than how that guy did. ‘I think you may have to tell him yourself. He doesn't work here.’ There was a silence and a moment of comprehension then bitter acceptance. With a haughty face she proceeded to silently carry her trolley by herself pretending as though nothing happened. To add salt to the wound as she passed me I yelled, ‘Hey, you need any help with that?’ She passed me without a word or a glance.

Which is the most misunderstood film of all time? It shocks me to this day that people think Breakfast at Tiffany’s (1961) is a charming, feelgood rom-com. Even though the screenplay was sugar coated to heck, the source material is actually a character study of grooming, abuse and promiscuity and its impact on a young rural woman deliriously pretending to be something she isn’t. No one talks about the Truman Capote book because reading it is a sobering experience that takes away a lot of the shimmer from the hugely popular movie. Holly Golightly is a really messed up, poverty stricken girl from Texas with the birth name of Lula Mae. She ran away from home to an older man through which she was groomed and became his wife at the age of 14. She then ran away from him to New York under a false identity. Through manipulation, fraud and mafia related espionage she maintains a high end Brownstone apartment above her means. She courts several wealthy suitors by throwing lavish parties and intends to marry the richest of the lot. In the film and the book she shows symptoms of borderline personality and disassociative identity disorder. When things don't go her way financially she goes further into her fantasy of being a high society socialite by simply walking around in her best clothes and pretending to shop/hang out at Tiffany's or other famous luxury stores and locations . Audrey Hepburn is cute and charming. Holly Golightly is not. She is a warped individual that is prone to fits of anger, delusion and self destruction. She is pretentious and borderline narcissistic with the only ease of conscious being her flimsy belief that she will help her abject brother at some point in time. This delusion does not work out well for her. If the film had ended the way the novella ended it would have been a tragic, small town, wide eyed kid comes to New York in search of the American dream drama very much in the vein of the not so feelgood Midnight Cowboy (1969). The final scene with Holly and Paul finding her cat (named Cat) in the alley in the pouring rain is supposedly where the moral of the story comes in. It is the part of the film that transforms it from a softened character study into a full blown romantic comedy. It gives a moral that love can heal all as both Paul and Holly acknowledge their faults, subtly agree to change their ways and direct their love to one another. I have ambiguous feelings towards the ending but it is admittedly cute. However, I think any licensed psychologist would agree that Holly Golightly from the film Breakfast at Tiffany's is a movie that is a somber study of the neuroses and disorders a young female runaway from a broken home has to endure disguised as a sophisticated rom-com. Edit: Several commenters have been stating that they don't see why I refer to this as a misunderstood movie, that it deviated from the novel but as a film it is not misunderstood. Yes it is a misunderstood movie. Many people believe it is a simple love story about two good looking, fashionable young people falling in love in New York to the tune of Moon River. Generations of people believed that Holly Golightly was classy, an inspiration and an icon in lifestyle and fashion. Many girls of the era grew up wanting to be just like Holly Golightly without thoroughly understanding that she was a deeply flawed character with deep seated personality disorders. If this is not a misunderstood movie then the word misunderstood is ‘misunderstood.’

What screams "I'm low class"? A girl, no older than 20 comes into Papa John's a busy Friday evening. I'm helping out at the cash register. It's near the end of the month (pay day for most people) and this is when we get our bulk of orders. The phone is ringing off the hook. I'm really just a delivery guy but the store is short staffed so I help cash. The girl, her cellphone tucked at her groin area in her trousers comes up to me at the register. Totally ignoring the fact that I'm taking an order on the phone she proceeds to talk about what she wants. I paused from the phone call to tell her, ‘One minute please miss I'm on the phone with a customer.’ I look as her eyebrows slant further downwards in anger and she puts her arms on her hips, staring at me in a show of impatience. When I finished with the call I apologized and asked what would she like. ‘Gimme one of the chicken pizzas.’ The phone started ringing again. I sighed inwardly. All the time she spent staring at me in anger she didn't even make up her mind as to what she wanted. ‘Which one of the chicken pizzas?’ I don't know if by asking a simple question like that she found some measure of offense but she replied in a belligerent tone, ‘How am I supposed to know what chicken pizzas you have?’ The phone continued ringing. I sighed again. I pointed to the display above her head and told her I have to take the call, choose a pizza by the time. Instead she frowns at me while I take another phone order, she refusing to look at the menu board herself. When I was done she glared at me and said, ‘Chicken and pine….the largest size you have.’ ‘That would be an extra large’ I said. ‘I know!’ she spat. She then proceeds to take out of her purse a brown envelope which contained the salary she just received from whatever job she worked. She proudly counts her 100s in front of me and gave me $200 without waiting for me to tell her the price of her order. I gave her her change and receipt and told her the waiting time (15–20 mins). She proceeded to stare at me whilst I take other orders, helped cut pizzas from off the oven and organized my deliveries at the same time. With her seeing me doing all these things at once I thought she would have generated some sympathy for me seeing that I wasn't really the cashier but just a delivery guy helping out the situation. While heading towards the exit with my deliveries I passed near her and she beckons me. I thought it was to apologize for her attitude. Instead she tells me something that makes my blood boil instantly. ‘Ummm. How much longer for my order?’ She just placed her order 5 minutes ago! I gritted me teeth and replied, ‘It’s not in the oven yet. 10 to 15 minutes.’ She rolled her eyes and looked away. I then realize what her game was. She didn't really care about the pizza. Her fetish was to feel some sort of superiority over someone else and the only place she could achieve that was in a fast food restaurant. We get customers like that regularly, especially around month's end (pay day). They get some kind of sick thrill out of pissing people off and flaunting what (little) money they have. So to answer the question above, nothing screams 'I’m low class’ more than people who buy fast food for the sake of showing off/putting on airs.

What television shows started strong only to become unwatchable later? Skins (2007 - 2013) The show was highly popular with millennials as it strove to give a realistic depiction of teenaged adults of that generation. The show, with its graphic portrayal of promiscuous sex and drug use among the majority of its main cast made it controversial at the time. Themes such as anorexia, poverty, depression, trauma, dysfunctional parenting etc were also touched on without succumbing to preaching or caricature. In essence the show was a comedy that subtly touched on some of the drama that went on in the personal lives of each of its characters. Generation 1 Without a doubt the first generation of Skins (Series 1 -2) is the true representation of the show. The first two seasons chronicles the lives of the above 9 teenagers. I enjoyed how no one was treated as the star of the show. Everyone had their positive traits as well as deep seated flaws but no one is given more screen time over the other or made into a token. The show focused on the youths as a group rather than as an hierarchy. The lifestyle may have been a tad exaggerated in its insistence that every character supposedly engaged in promiscuous sex and/or drug use. Besides that the show was an honest representation of teenaged millennials, written by an actual millennial, Jamie Brittain, who was 22 at the premier of the first season. The show launched the careers of actors Nicholas Hoult and Dev Patel who portrayed Tony and Anwar respectively. Generation 2 The second generation of Skins (Series 3–4) saw some changes. The comedic tone was increased as well as the amount of sex. The third season started off with an air of superficiality compared to the first generation but had a few well written moments and thoughtful episodes, particularly that of the trials and tribulations of teenaged Congolese immigrant Thomas. However the cast seemed all over the place and without developed characterization except that of cheap stereotypes (bully, geek, skater boy, drama queen, femme fatale etc.) Unlike Generation 1, this generation seemed to have an hierarchy among the cast as everything seemed to revolve around the characters Effy and Cook, who were, unsurprisingly, the most promiscuous and morally unscrupulous of the lot. Nearing the end of series 3 the show's writing started to wear thin. Shocks, drama and comedy were shoehorned in at every chance available. The show and its characters started losing their sense of direction and some of the themes that made them compelling characters in the beginning were abandoned in favour of sex and silliness. Some episodes were so ludicrous it became an effort to keep my eyes on the screen. The show seemed like a poor man’s imitation of itself. (So he's stealing a boat now…?) By series 4 it became painful to watch and I gave up. I have no intention to watch the third generation nor the American MTV remake. However the first generation of Skins remains a classic in my mind and a damned brilliant character study. It's hard for any writer to keep such a momentum going so you got to give the creators of the show credit for trying, even if they tried too hard in the end.

What's the most obnoxious instance of America-centric behavior you've ever witnessed? During my first week at Papa John’s (Trinidad) the phone rang and I took the call. An American accent could be heard on the other end of the line. Caller: I’ll have the Friday special Me: Sorry ma’am but the specials are from Sundays - Wednesdays. Caller: This is Papa John’s right? Me: Yes. Caller: Papa John’s has Friday specials where I’m from. What’s the special for today? Me: Sorry but the specials are only from Sundays - Wednesdays. Caller: I’m goin’ write a review about the Papa John’s in Trinidad. I’ve traveled the world. I’ve never encountered any Papa John’s that doesn’t have a daily special. I want to talk to the manager. I call Ricardo, the manager, and he takes the phone. I’m expecting him to repeat what I said but instead he says ‘yes’ every few seconds and on the screen I see him enter two extra large pizzas, a large garlic bread sticks, a large cheese bread sticks and a 2L soda. He’s entering all these items, not as any discounted ‘special,’ but at retail value, so the bill is fairly sizable. He then covers the receiving end of the phone with his palm and tells me, ‘Go check and see if there’s any brownies left. I went in the chiller and saw two brownies remaining. I showed him two fingers and watch as he enters them both on the lady’s bill. He repeats the order to the caller. ‘So the total will be $502………no miss that is in Trinidad dollars. Yes miss that is a good deal you are getting…….OK…….Yes we take Mastercard………20 minutes…………thank you.’ He hung up the phone and looked at me smiling. ‘How did you manage to sell her all that stuff?’ I said, ‘She wanted a special.’ ‘I did give her a special,’ he says with a mischievous smile, ‘Ricardo’s special.’ He then proceeds to laugh flamboyantly and heads back to his office while saying, ‘Whenever you hear an American accent on the phone just call me…….I have a $10,000 sales target to make today.’

What guitarists do you think have the most emotionally moving solos? I love this question because it's entirely subjective and for someone who has zero technical guitar knowledge and even less skills, I can answer it. It's rare that I sense a feeling of emotion in a guitar solo. Most solos to me just sound like cool improvisations that take you away from the rigidity of the melody and repetition of verse-chorus, verse-chorus. There are only a handful of songs that I've actually felt the emotion behind the playing. It's like the guitarist is talking to you with his guitar and you sense the emotions behind the words. Such are the best examples I can think of: Carlos Santana — Samba Pa Ti. This is possible the best example I can think of in regards to emotional solos. The entire song is basically an extended guitar solo. Wrought with the feelings of longing, regret and desire this song is one of the artist's most impressive contribution. I can hear a man at his wit's end wailing to lost love from the very first few notes. Buck Dharma — Don't Fear The Reaper Nothing is more terrifying than the ominous solo in this pre-heavy metal classic. I get visions of demonic creatures rising from beneath when this manic, blistering guitar starts going off after a creepy rhythm guitar intro. Buck Dharma wrote the song after envisioning death for himself and it shows in his playing. Jimi Hendrix — Little Wing Funny how this original composition grew from obscurity to one of his most covered songs. 'Fly on, Little Wing' Hendrix indeed takes us to soaring heights with this solo full of wonder, hope and optimism. I consider the solo an extension of the themes explored in another Hendrix classic The Wind Cries Mary. Play both solos one after the the other and you'll see what I mean. John Frusciante — Scar Tissue In the land of weeping guitars Scar Tissue reigns King. The greatest achievement of the Red Hot Chili Peppers in regards to their sombre, non funky output. Frusciante's guitar sounds like a broken down and dying animal. Figures that it is shown to be literally broken in the music video. Jonny Greenwood — Paranoid Android + There There Couldn't choose between the two Radiohead classics but they both explore the emotions of fear, paranoia and anxiety. Paranoid Android's solo is fractured yet blistering. It is cold and unconventional yet wrought with feelings, like an android having a physical and emotional breakdown. There There’s rhythm and solo combined instills a deeply fearful feeling of slowly incurring the wrath of some powerful unseen entity. And lastly Duane Allman — Melissa The slide guitar to end all slide guitar. A grandeur solo like no other is encapsulates themes of freedom, love and innocence. Duane's guitar makes its presence from the very beginning and soars to the heavens in its solo. Given the fact that Duane Allman died not long after creating this marvellous piece of work does one sense an almost spiritual connection with Duane's playing on this a masterpiece.

What movies can you watch all the time and never get tired of watching? Without a doubt Dirty Rotten Scoundrels (1988) is the movie I’d take with me to a desert island. I don't think the movie gets a fraction of the praise it deserves. I think it's the highlight of the careers of both its leads Steve Martin and Michael Caine. I must've seen the movie over 20 times and still it is a delight to sit and watch for its entirety. What makes it endearing as compared to great movies that you only watch once is that it doesn't take itself too seriously. There is no moral or lesson to be learned here. Two dirtbags, one a petty hustler, the other a gentlemanly con artist, make their living by manipulating wealthy, slow witted women. They make a bet as to who would be first to con a simple but good natured soap heiress who just arrived in the village at the French Riviera. What makes this film so rewatchable is that, yes it is silly movie, but it is also a very well written, well executed and thoroughly refined silly movie. The location and cinematography is absolutely gorgeous. The score and soundtrack is a fitting blend of waltzy French classical and sophisti-pop. Mostly filmed on location at scenic locations along the French Riviera, the film is one of the most gorgeous movies I've ever seen. From the beginning Villefranche-Sur-Mer train station to the breathtaking Beaulieu-sur-mer to the lookout at Villa Hier at the end, the film is a feast for the eyes. Not to mention the performances. Both Caine and Martin give stellar performances from a remarkably clever script but Martin steals the show and makes the character Freddy Benson his own in a highly physical role the likes of which only Martin can accomplish. Props also to Glenne Headly who plays mutual target of the leads, demonstrating an innocent charm that wins over the hearts of the conmen and the audience. The film takes a not so pleasant topic and turns it into a rather good natured, comedy film. If it were remade today it would be chocked full of the gratuitous profanity, nudity and sex that is the hallmark of modern day ‘comedy.’ There's not a single F-bomb, nor a sex scene, nor a gratuitous flashing of breasts etc. Frank Oz uses no cheap gimmicks to entertain an audience and as such the film can be enjoyed by the entire family. Watching Dirty Rotten Scoundrels is such a pleasure that watching it feels like a little vacation rather than a movie. I watch it every year as a sort of ritual and I am yet to find another movie that is such a timeless delight.

Which moments, either good or bad, do you still remember from your childhood? As an 8 year old my school was a quaint little building with a population of a little over 100 kids; kids of lesser means like myself. The school was raising funds by sending us out to collect money through raffle sheets. The price of a chance on the raffle was a quarter. The 1st prize was an Oster blender. I found it pathetic and embarassing back then. People would give usally give us a dollar when asked, not because they wanted the blender but because they felt sorry for us; a lower tier school at the side of a river full of kids of lesser means. Instead of going about asking people for a chance in the raffle I slowly filled my sheet using my own allowance. However when I submitted the money and the completed sheet my teacher simply took it and gave me another raffle sheet to get filled out. ‘But I already filled out my raffle sheet!’ I protested. ‘One raffle sheet for an entire month Elijah?’ she replied tartly, ‘Kenrick filled out over 20 sheets already. He did 5 in the last two days.’ She was wrong. Kenrick probably filled out over 40 sheets. Us boys knew, from his sudden increase in wealth, that he was pocketing a lot of the raffle money as his own. I wanted to say this but I knew I had no evidence and even if I did I doubt she would've cared. I took the sheet but mentally refused to go about after school, tugging on strangers’ clothes putting on a sad face, begging for a chance in my raffle like Kenrick. I also refused to use more of my personal allowance to fill the raffle sheet. At the end of the week the principal wanted to see me in his office. My classmates were shocked. Only serious offenders, ripe for suspension, were called into the principal’s office. I was known to be a good boy throughout. In the office the principal chastised me for not getting my second raffle filled out and how I brought in the least amount of raffles of all the students in school. (A lie, my best friend didn't submit any.) He also threatened that if I didn't get 5 raffle sheets filled out by next week I'll be kicked out of the school. Yes. He literally said those words. I left office trying to hold my tears and when I was home my mother queried as to why I was so sullen. I explained to her what had happened. To my utter surprise she started to laugh. I asked her why she found it funny, that soon we would have to be looking for a new school. She told me to relax and that tomorrow she was going to make a phone call to my school. At the end of school the following day my teacher quietly asked me to return the raffle sheet. At assembly the following morning it was announced that raffle sheets would be suspended until further notice. In fact for the rest of my time in that school they never reinstated raffle sheets again. Whatever my mother said to the principal on the phone was effective. Most of the students were happy for the news, except Kenrick of course. Thankfully raffle sheet fundraising have become a thing of the past in most of our local schools. I'd like to think that my mother had a part to play in schools being banned from encouraging children to solicit money from strangers.

The Good, the Bad & the Ugly is an amazing movie but I never understood the scene involving Tuco and his monk brother. As much as it was an emotional scene, it did not advance the movie plot at all. Did Leone ever explain why he added the scene? Yeah. Quite true. But then again, remember, throughout the movie, how often Tuco does this: Everytime he kills or someone is killed through his double crossing, he makes a sign of the Cross. Clearly he has a conflicted relationship with God. It paves the way for the reveal that he comes from a very religious background i.e. the scene with his disapproving monk brother. Admittedly, that scene sticks out like a sore thumb. I guess it was to give an emotional depth to Tuco`s character. It was meant to show that Tuco had a sympathetic, human side to him. Blondie had an emotional side as evident by the short scene where he shared his cigarette with the young, dying soldier. That scene was perfection. However Tuco`s emotional scene didn't play out so well. It tried a tad too hard. Tuco was well characterized and even without this scene one could sense that though he was bad, he wasn't evil. Tuco kept odd standards of decency, unlike Angel Eyes who was a psychopath. Before the monk scene, the movie had established a macho aesthetic of manly indifference. These guys were looking for gold, not for emotional closure. Then this overwrought scene comes in and goes on too long and is a bit unlike Tuco`s persona. He was too hardened from years of crime and debauchery to care about the opinion of his monk brother who he considered a fool or even his recently deceased father who he obviously didn't have a good relationship with. If I were Leone I would write the scene as Tuco`s brother (who is not a monk) informing him that he is headed towards their father`s funeral and grudgingly invites Tuco to pay his final respect. Tuco, feeling a bit remorseful and embarrassed considers the offer but reflects upon the possibility of Blondie escaping and the lost chance of getting gold, makes an excuse and declines. It would be less than 2 minutes long. But it isn’t too off putting and that is why to this day it's still my favorite movie of all time.

Can you provide some examples of average actors delivering great performances due to well-written characters? Let's be frank. Samuel L. Jackson is a one trick pony. But gosh darn it that sure is one hell of a trick that motherf****n pony does. All jokes aside I find it hard to think of Quintin Tarantino writing the character Jules without envisioning Samuel L. Jackson in mind for the role in Pulp Fiction. It is truly the role Jackson was born to play. It is the role that took Jackson into stardom and to this day Jules’ intimidating obscenity ridden threats, interrogation, debates on burgers and pork, not to mention his love of quoting Ezekiel 25:17 is constantly memed, quoted and parodied. But I wouldn't consider Jackson a great actor. He may sit more comfortable with his tough guy roles but he isn't anywhere near the range of other legendary tough guy actors like Denzel Washington, Clint Eastwood and James Cagney. If you know Jackson is going to be in a movie you are certain that he isn't going to be a bespectacled data programmer hunched behind a computer or a main love interest. He is probably the most famous typecast of Hollywood film history since John Wayne. It's a bit unfortunate because when he attempts more vulnerable or intellectual characters it comes across as forgettable at best and eerie at worst in my honest opinion (Tarzan, RoboCop, Star Wars). I don't think Sam may get another role as defining and well written as Jules in Pulp Fiction. I think a large portion of his filmography isn't impressive from an acting standpoint. He may not be a Marlon Brando or a Laurence Olivier but neither of them could've put in the heart and energy into an intricately moulded character such as Jules Winnfield.

What is the common parenting mistake and how can they rectify that? The worst parenting mistake is not showing any genuine love to your children. The most common parenting mistake ironically is to constantly be selflessly giving to them. I see it more as a source of vanity and pride rather than of genuine love. I have three relatives who are from such a household. Their parents are well-off and stable with the mother supplying them an abundance of love and the father an abundance of money whenever the time calls. All three of them are in their 40s and do not live in the same country as their parents. They come to see their parents every Christmas as a tradition. This sounds nice of them, for all three of them to arrange a date to arrive and stay at the family home, plane tickets etc. In reality their parents are the ones who see to that. The parents have been paying for their children to come see them for Christmas for over twenty years. The parents arrange the date, the tickets and additional expenses that their 40 something year old children may accrue during their stay. Some readers may not see a problem with this. If you can afford it, why not treat your kids, especially during the Christmas? My answer to them is that it has nothing to do with money. It has to do with principle. No one should have to pay to see their grown children once a year. If your kids really cared about you they would come on their own volition and expense, not wait for daddy to purchase highly inflated Christmas flights. Not only this but the parents (both in their 70s) are the one to pick them up upon arrival and drop them off for departure. The parents also provide them with a New Year's vacation to a hotel every year and pay all expenses associated with it. The parents cook meals, carry them out for lunch/dinner and arrange all forms of planning and entertainment. To say that their kids are somewhat spoiled would be quite an understatement. To say that their kids were concerned about their parents descent into old age, loss of movement/stamina and increasing loneliness would be a great exaggeration. This arrangement is likely to continue until one of their parents die of which I'm certain the other parent would have to buy their tickets so they can attend the funeral. When you train your kids that they can receive a constant supply of love without them having to reciprocate you are training them to expect love without having to reciprocate. This is almost as damaging as showing no love at all.

When did you think, "this can only be a fake"? While employed as a pizza delivery rider, after the lifting of the COVID lock-down, our company decided to pull a fast one. A memo from the head office was circulated among all restaurant staff at all branches. It basically said that the company was so concerned about our welfare in these trying times that they were willing to keep a percentage of our weekly salary for us as a form of savings. The memo also mentioned that if we agreed to this ‘Pizza Savings’ (my term, not theirs) that we will be getting 0% interest. My delivery co-worker and I had a field day with that memo. We read it several times in disbelief and laughed. The owners could not be serious. It was obvious they wanted to get a loan/invest in something. It was as if they told themselves instead of taking a 16% interest loan from the bank why not simply take it from their uneducated restaurant workers, all they needed was our signatures. I went around some of the co-workers joking about it. Most of us laughed it off but two of them couldn’t understand what was so funny. ‘But we’re getting 0% interest!’ an older woman working the grill said. She seemed to have the idea that this was a good thing. Apparently she had had so many loans in the past that to her the word interest = bad. I explained to her it was a savings and not a loan. That with savings you want the highest interest you could get and the exact opposite when it comes to a loan. ‘But isn’t it good to have a savings?’ one of the teenaged girls working the pizza table said. I explained to her it is a good thing but it makes no sense to save your money with someone giving you 0%. I tried explaining how banks work, about buying shares etc and getting the best rates for your money. Both women looked at me in silence. In the end they both decided to ‘try it out.’ I didn't know what shocked me more. The fact that the restaurant attempted that stunt or the fact that it actually worked on two employees. Edit: Are you ready to invest in your Pizza Savings Fund? 0% interest guaranteed and you can be assured your money is so safe with us that no one can touch it, not even you. Why do movies try to make female characters look strong by making male characters look stupid and weak? Hollywood needs to take a course in studying James Cameron. He is without a doubt one of the greatest character writers of the 20th century. This is especially in regards to women. Every female lead he has written has become iconic. They are neither strong nor weak. What they are good at is adapting to their environment/circumstances, using their wits and keeping focus on goals rather than trying to prove how much stronger they are than the opposite sex. Examples include: Ellen Ripley - Aliens Lindsey Brigman - The Abyss Sarah Connor - Terminator/Terminator 2 Helen Tasker - True Lies Rose DeWitt Bukater - Titanic Take a look at all the photos. Tell me what is common among all the women. If you answered fear, uncertainty, anxiety, instability or anything hinting at crippling emotions you are correct. None of these women were stronger or more brave than their male counterparts in these films. However all of them were loyal, intelligent and selfless. They were multifaceted characters, displaying weaknesses in many scenarios and great strength and determination in others. They were all emotional. They all depended on the men around them and in various instances the men depended on them. The relationship between male and female was symbiotic Ellen Ripley offered her experience and intelligence to a group of macho, shoot first, ask questions later, marines to survive an alien invasion. Lindsey Brigman kept the SEAL team from turning into savages, kept the ego of her ex-husband/team leader in check and demonstrated love and humanity to the alien life-forces they encountered. Sarah Connor went from being a relatively weak and mild mannered waitress fighting to survive to an obsessive, violent mercenary and then to a more stable and grounded maternal figure after reuniting with her long lost son. Helen Tasker transformed from a mousy, timid housewife to the world's sexiest woman in a mission to save her marriage, in doing so she saves her husband's life as well and Rose went from being a passive, poor little rich girl to a tragic romantic figure that extended beyond class and wealth. All of these women had their weaknesses. None of them dared to think about defeating/overcoming an obstacle without male help. They were women and they were proud of what they were. Many times they screwed up and many times they made foolish decisions/actions but they always saw the bigger picture. They always knew when it was time to lead and when it was time to serve. They were all globally cherished and were well written female characters. Unlike the ones below.
