My girlfriend is mad at me for "not standing up for her.” She accidentally spilled her drink on a girl in the club. The other girl threw her drink on my girlfriend and her boyfriend shoved me. I grabbed my girlfriend and we left. What should I do? I love pub stories. I have one to share in a similar context. Years ago my friends from work and I would visit a bar that was pretty much a flashy looking dive bar. There was 6 of us. The biggest guy in the pack was Kurt who would always bring his wife (then girlfriend) with him. Curt is some specimen of human. If Dolph Lundgren discovered he had a secret Trinidadian half brother, I would gladly tell Dolph to come check out Curt. Curt is a bug dude. He’s so strong that once, three us at work in the warehouse wanted to play a prank on him. We wanted to restrain him on his forklift and bound him onto it with shrink wrap; keeping him there until somebody discovered him. The three of us combined could not subdue Curt and our prank failed. Curt has a great sense of humour when it comes to pranks but when it came to his wife's safety, all jokes ended there. So six us were in this bar taking turns shooting pool. Kurt and his wife were sitting on bar stools against the wall while the rest of us were around a pool table. Suddenly a sound of a beer bottle crashing onto the floor could be heard from the opposite pool table. A pudgy little manchild held his pool stick as though ready to fight someone. His drunken girlfriend released a cackling laugh and was making a poor attempt to subdue him. Apparently the pudgy guy was drunk and believed some guys outside the bar were throwing sweet words towards his woman. He broke his beer as a show of machismo towards the men outside and proceeded to hurl threats their direction Curt and his wife were laughing at something else at the moment. Pudgy guy’s eyes narrowed in on them believing them to be mocking him. He took his girlfriend's beer and hurtles it into the air where it lands and splashes beer upon them both when it smashes near their feet on the ground. Everything went silent. My friends and I at the pool table believed that this was going to be a brawl like no other. Pudgy guy had already provoked the men outside who seemed ready to thrash him and now Curt Lundgren was ready to give Pudgy a demonstration. However Curt is a smart individual. He recognized immediately what was going on and calculated the outcome. Three agitated men ready to fight outside the pub, one drunken idiot stirring up more trouble every second that passed and his girlfriend seeing the whole thing as a joke, broken glass everywhere. If Curt engaged in a fight things would get ugly and his wife could get seriously damaged. Instead Curt decides that we should leave. Without a word we headed to our vehicles and went home. Had Curt been alone he would given Pudgy what he deserved. However bar fights do not play off like they do in those 80s action movies. Everyone involved gets hurts and some even get scarred, maimed or killed. The bar has since closed down after the owner got killed in a drive by shooting last year.

Who is the coolest, Robert Mitchum, Paul Newman, James Dean, or Steve McQueen? Steve McQueen was the most ruggedly manly. He was a race car enthusiast, did a lot of his own stunts and was a notorious ladies man. Paul Newman was the most beautifully rugged. When they say someone has a face like a Greek God, Paul Newman's name is usually mentioned. He served in the US Navy and like McQueen was a professional racecar driver. He also created the non-profit Newman's Own brand of products. James Dean is the most mysteriously fascinating. Died at age 24 he would've probably beaten Brando as the greatest method actor of the 20th century. No one portrays poetic angst better than James Dean. And finally. Robert Mitchum. The vagabond who became an actor. There is NO ONE who can do a good Robert Mitchum impersonation. He is just too cool, too unique. He never acted. He simply spoke his lines. Plus he had a calypso album on the charts. As a Trinidadian, no one can beat an actor who can sing your country's genre of music. Therefore for me Robert Mitchum is the coolest.

What is the nastiest thing you've done for revenge? I was at a house party several years ago. Everyone was having a good time except for this one girl, aged anywhere between 18 - 21 years old, who kept moping about and drawing attention to herself about how her relationship was on the rocks because her boyfriend failed to show up. While everyone was dancing, making conversation or just enjoying the atmosphere, she would position herself in the center of everyone and put on a face of gloom and doom. Guys would keep coming to her out of genuine concern to ask if everything was alright and she would use the opportunity to make a dramatic scene, saying stuff like: ‘I’m really not interested.’ or ‘I’m not in the mood to talk right now.’ or ‘Could you just give me some space. Geez.’ Then she would go running off to another location to repeat her narcissistic process. I observed her for quite a while and honestly I found her to be quite irritating. Her overly childish Minnie Mouse hairstyle incensed me even more. It was similar to the photo below but with pink streaks. A friend of hers came up to me and requested that I go cheer her up by asking her to dance. I explained to the friend that I saw several guys come with honest intentions to comfort her and she blew them off spectacularly. I explained I had no interest in having the same done to me. The friend assured me that that wouldn’t happen and to just do it for Minnie Mouse’s sake. That Minnie was really a nice person when she wasn’t in this kind of mood. So I went over to Minnie as she sat broodingly on a couch with her chin on her palm. Because the music was so loud I had to shout for her to hear. ‘WOULD YOU LIKE TO DANCE?’ She barely looked me in the face when she replied. ‘GO AWAY.’ I became overwhelmed with menacing anger. I had no problem with rejection but Minnie Mouse needed a reality check. My mind speedily and efficiently worked up a plan to get poetic justice. I had the perfect plan. I had but one sentence to tell her that I knew would’ve destroyed her I waited for a pause in the music then went up to her again. I then calmly whispered something into her ear. She paid keen attention because my tone of voice was that of a confiding manner. ‘Hey. I’m so happy you said no.’ I then paused to look at her. She didn’t look at me but her body language showed that she was listening. ‘The truth is I really didn’t want to dance with you but your friend begged me to ask you……so yeah, it worked out good for both of us. She stared me in the face and suddenly burst into tears and went into her friend’s car. I thought everyone would’ve come to me with angry questions as to what I said that made her react like that but nobody cared, not even her friend. They all had had enough of her. She played the sympathy card too much and exhausted all of her credit. A heaviness had lifted in the party with her oppressive presence being gone. Was it a nasty thing to do/say? Damned right it was nasty. But it was also the truth and sometimes the truth hurts. Edit 19.01.22. I sure gave that girl a healthy serving of humble pie. She was not the only person safely guided back to Earth with one sentence. This cocky guy also got his ego destroyed at a chic nightclub. Click here to read about it.

Who was the most successful person from your high school? I'm cheating a bit. Mitra was my best friend in Primary (Elementary) school. The best way I could describe him is being intensely loyal to the point of obsession (he would demand that I admit to him that we were best friends), kind, outspoken and a natural leader. He was not all that gifted intellect-wise and there was even a time when he begged me (the top performing student in class) to allow him to beat me in exams so he could get top grades and get the Sega Genesis his parents promised upon achieving such a feat. I was a vain bastard and didn't let that happen for him. Fast forward twenty years later and I'm walking through the streets of San Juan, trying to flag a taxi to get to a job interview for a much needed part time delivery job, I see a sexy electric blue Impreza pull up next to me. The windows slide down and I see it's my old friend Mitra who I hadn't seen in decades. He gives me a heartfelt shake of the hand and with absolutely no trace of conceit he explains to me that he has a thriving car-parts business/garage. Upon looking him up on Facebook I find out that along with his parents' old home in Trinidad he has a house in Hennessy, Oklahoma. Yes. The guy who I wouldn't let beat me in final exams got the last laugh and with dividends to boot. Couldn't happen to a nicer guy though. Feel free to check out his business here.

What's something on an employee's first day that sets off red flags? In my second year at my current job, a lady was hired to replace my senior who had resigned. The job was in a public office and for the most part was quite easy going. Somebody off the streets could learn the essentials in just a few hours. The lady who came had seniority and several years more experience than me working at a different branch. I therefore expected her to have a wealth of knowledge and experience to share with me. 'How does this work again?’ 'Did I do this right?’ 'How about you be the one to do that? You're so good at it.’ 'Can you show me how to do (such-and-such) again?’ The lady transferred from a location that had the exact same type of system and technology as mine yet she had not a clue how to do anything! How was this woman in a senior position? She didn't know anything about the job. Was she dumb? A week of 'training’ had passed and she didn't really learn anything and had to be supervised at all times. Before I could find out how it was that she was so slow she suddenly vanished. She stopped turning up at work and calls to her phone went unanswered. I sent an email to HR explaining that she had gone AWOL. They gave some half-assed reply. A few months later, after she had long been forgotten, I get a frantic letter from HR saying that they have been paying her salary and they've just become aware that she has not been turning up to work. ‘No shit,' I say in my mind. HR investigates and finds out that she had accepted another job elsewhere the entire time and was gladly accepting two salaries. HR demanded that she return the unearned salary. She said she would but she was going through financial distress at the moment. She never returned a cent. HR washed their hands of the matter and kept it hush hush. Turns out she wasn't dumb at all. So my answer to the question 'what sets off red flags on an employee's first day?’ Playing dumb.

What movie felt like you were right there with the actors? United 93 Didn't have the opportunity to see this on the big screen when it premiered back in ‘06. Really wish I did. However I'm certain I would've been emotionally drained afterwards. The film deals with the September 11th terrorist attacks and chronicles the last few hours of the only flight of the four hijacked planes in which the passengers managed to fight off the terrorists and prevent the plane from crashing into its intended target. The film employs the use of shaky, handheld camera which has become the signature style of its director Paul Greengrass (of whom I am of the opinion that he now overdoes this style in practically every movie he makes). The frenzied handheld style coupled with the use of real time, unknown actors, strategic camera positioning and lack of a protagonist makes the viewer feel like a random passenger aboard the flight. All of this is done intentionally by the director of course. It is one of the few movies in which, even though I knew what would be the eventual outcome, I was glued to the screen in nervous anticipation as to what was going to happen next. A very underrated movie in my honest opinion.

What "poverty food" is actually really delicious? Trinidad has many types of delicious poverty meals that stem from colonialism, slavery and East Indian indentureship. Some are despondently looked upon with embarassment while others are now expensive delicacies that tourists pay, 'ah pound and ah crown’ for. Poor poverty meals These are the meals that really represent someone going through hard times. These are the delicacies prepared from the remnants of the pantry and hunger induced experimentation. Rice and butter As the name suggests, boiled rice grains soaked in butter. Actually it's not butter but margarine, as real butter here is more expensive than most meats. Exceedingly unhealthy but much more delicious than you would imagine. Just imagine the taste of mashed potatoes except it's rice. Flour porridge Heat some white flour on a skillet and just before it's about to burn throw in some condensed milk and water. This is a Haitian recipe but used by many older Trinis who want to feel full but can't afford to buy groceries. According to how well you garnish this concoction, it can be a hidden delight. Plain egg rice When you have one egg and a bag of rice and you need to feed an entire family, this is the meal of choice. Basically you heat up some boiled rice and throw in a well beaten egg. You will be astonished at how far one egg can stretch. Green fig (banana) with ‘butter’ and salt A family with a couple of banana trees in the yard could be saved from starvation with this simple, delicious meal. Boil a couple full but unripe bananas (with or without skin) and serve with margarine and salt. A fully developed green fig well soaked in margarine with a dash of salt can beat meals in most 5 star restaurants. Banana fritters Instead of throwing away your near rotted bananas, mash them to a pulp, knead in some flour and deep fry in oil. Even when eaten cold these fritters are a treat. Rich Poverty Meals These were meals made from ingredients the upper class and colonial masters would discard such as chickens’ neck and pig's tail. Now they are culinary delights that tourists flock towards and are quite expensive to make/purchase. Chicken Foot souse Don't run away just yet. This flavor will knock your socks off. This is basically boiled chicken's feet soaked in a zesty broth. You'd be surprised the amount of meat a chicken's foot can give. Geera neck Dont throw away those chicken necks! Season them with cumin roast them on a skillet for a spicy snack. These are popular 'cutters’ or bar foods, made to sober up drunkards. This can be made with chicken gizzards also. Fried chicken livers My mother would carry us to this seedy looking bakery on a Sunday where they served fried chicken livers, mostly to satisfy the patrons of the bar that was situated next to them. You'll spit out its overly pungent flavor at first try but it gets tastier after each bite. Pig tail Pig tail meals are now synonymous with special events such as birthday parties and wedding receptions. Pig tail pelau, as shown above, is made from rice and pig tails cooked in caramelized sugar (stewed) with peas and whatever garnishes desired. There is also pig tail soup. A pig's tail is incredibly meaty, tender and juicy that so much that many people find themselves sucking at the bone upon finishing. Black pudding Thanks to our English rulers of yesteryear who brought this excrement looking sausage, made entirely of pig's blood, to the Caribbean. Our version includes a lot more spices and this dish is quite popular served in bread as a street food. It looks and sounds horrid but it is quite creamy textured and rich in taste. and lastly Cow heel soup Who would've known that a cow's heel would be so gelatinous, meaty and soak up flavour so well. Along with fish broth and corn soup, this is the definitive soup of Trinidad.

What movies do you like but everybody hates, and why? When The Matrix came out, every nerdy boy over 12 sang its praises. Every nerdy boy except me. I liked it (kinda) but I just couldn’t see the big deal about it. The action was good and everyone raved about the whole bullet time camera innovation. The soundtrack was phenomenal and the story and the main characters were intriguing. But I just couldn’t see the big deal. I just thought it was too silly for the movie to try to be deep and philosophical with its sociological commentary and high-brow sci-fi concepts, while at the same time engage in low-brow kung-fu action, psudo-BDSM rave culture, dystopian cyberpunk futurism, all the while having villains that looked like constipated insurance salesmen. I felt like the movie tried to be several things at once and took itself too seriously. I also felt that the movie would’ve been more enjoyable if it accepted how silly its concept was and focus more on its action scenes rather than having practically ever character besides Neo drifting off into some rambling philosophical stoner rant. Whenever I shared these criticisms with my nerd friends, they would turn red as though I demonstrated the most shocking of blasphemies. ‘You don’t get it. The Matrix is too deep for you to understand. Go watch your cartoons.’ That would be their usual response, but years would pass and my assessment would remain the same. THEN CAME THE MATRIX RELOADED I sat and watched it on TV long after its cinema premier. I wasn’t expecting much; some more philosophical sci-fi mumbo jumbo and a few over-rehearsed fight scenes. However, thirty minutes within the film I was finding myself thoroughly entertained. The movie went in the exact direction I wanted the first one to go. From the beginning to end the movie was a feast of God-like explosive superpowers, vast weaponry utilized in slow motion, explosions and swords slicing through speeding vehicles that contain time and space altering kung-fu fighting white rastas who can’t die, even in explosions. The movie relished in its stupidity and made no attempt to continue with the existential brouhaha of the original film. As an acne-riddled 18yo I ate it up like hot chicken soup but practically everyone I knew who worshipped the original, hated Reloaded with a passion. However, as admittedly dumb as it is, I consider it the superior movie. I haven't seen Resurrections yet but seeing that practically everyone loathes it I wouldn't be surprised if it turns out to be the best of the four.

What is one thing that all men hate? Yesterday I was at home. I couldn't attend work because my area had been flooded for the third time in a month. It was both nerve-wracking and boring being stuck in a house surrounded by water and fearful that the rain falls and the water gets higher and enters inside. I get a missed call. It's from a lady at work who is notorious for always wanting something. Practically every encounter I've had with her usually ends up with her saying 'I wanted to ask you about…… ’ Or 'Would it be alright if I…..’ Or 'Next Monday I wanted to……' In other words she wanted a favour from me. This is all fine and dandy but truly I only like to perform favours to people I consider friends. By no stretch of the imagination do I consider her a friend and the sheer volume of favours she's asked me over the years is exponentially greater than the favours every friend of mine has ever asked me combined. I decided to not take the call. Moments later I see that she sends a voice message. I call my girlfriend and discuss whether I should ignore it and she tells me. 'What if the lady just wants to know if you're alright?’ I then feel guilty. Maybe I am being a bit cynical. I decide to listen to the voice message. I play it; 'Hi. Didn't see you in work today. Hope everything is ok….’ In my mind I said my girlfriend was right and I shouldn't be so presumptuous. However, I then hear a sentence that makes me recoil. 'Since you're not here I was wondering if I could use your office to….’ I stopped listening. I didn't reply. I think every single man would agree that we hate when people only seek after us to get favours done.

Who is the most underestimated horror movie villain? Practically every boy who grew up in the 90s watching horror movies on SyFy (then Sci-Fi) knew of this guy. I'm pretty certain he's responsible for a lot of nightmares we had back then. Revok from David Cronenberg’s sci-fi/body-horror cult classic Scanners (1981) puts a capital V in Villain. He's a powerful, ruthless and deranged psychic (scanner) bent on taking over the world with powers that can control minds and inflict severe physical damage on others. Michael Ironside who portrays Revok is nothing short of excellence. He makes Jack Nicholson’s Joker look like Mr. Rogers with his intense facial expressions, sinister grimacing and lip curling as well as his menacingly emotionless voice. No one can forget the famous scene at the beginning of the movie where Revok calmly and sarcastically pretends to be ‘scanned’ by a weaker fellow scanner only to casually cause the man's head to explode within seconds. Few actors can put such a stamp on a performance like Ironside did as he did with Revok. Scanners may be a bit of a forgotten movie by now but no one can ever forget the character Revok and Ironside's performance.

What should every foreigner know about your country in terms of food, tourist destinations, demography, best time to visit, and USP of your country? Trinidad is actually two islands, Trinidad and Tobago. Trinidad is the oil and gas island. Tobago is the tourist island. We have the only ‘pitch lake’ in the entire world. We invented the steel drum/pan. Yes we did. Look it up. Trinidad had the most thriving KFC in the world at one point in time. Also Trinidad has more KFCs per capita than any country in the world. 59 restaurants in an area smaller than Delaware (which has only 13). In many ways we are very similar to Brazil. We once possessed the world’s hottest pepper, the Moruga Scorpion (we still like to believe it’s the world’s hottest). We put ketchup, mustard and pepper sauce on EVERY fast food. Do not open a fast food restaurant here without having copious amounts of these available to the general public. Don’t even get us started on garlic sauce. If you hate rice you will not last a month here. We make some of the finest rums in the world. Yet beer is more widely consumed. Marijuana is sort of legal. Just don’t get caught selling it. We are very liberal yet quite conservative at the same time. We don’t frown that much upon prostitution, once you’re not a transvestite prostitute. Then you might be asking for trouble.

What is the best comeback you used on someone? When I was much younger my first job was at a warehouse that distributed cosmetics, pharmaceuticals and a host of other things. I was an entry level grunt (or 'picker’ as we called it) along with many other young men like myself. This one guy named Dwayne who came from the hood and spoke as though he had a real tough life in the streets (he didn't) became friends with the supervisor and in little time he got promoted to a 'checker’ which gave him authority over me Dwayne and I didn't have the warmest relationship. He would constantly speak condescendingly of me and my 'book sense' and how I was gullible and naive and 'didn't know the life.’ In reality he was simply envious that I got better grades than him in school. This envy became apparent when I registered for college and got accepted as an evening student. I gave Dwayne my timetable for him to acknowledge that I could no longer work overtime on certain days because of my classes. I didn't need his approval I just had to inform him of it. Dwayne eyed my timetable scornfully and replied that he couldn't approve this because it was unfair to the rest of the staff including himself who had to work overtime even harder now with one man down. I replied that I didn't need his approval. It was already approved by the supervisor. Dwayne snarled and said, ‘Maybe I should go and pursue a degree too? Maybe everyone should go and pursue classes and better themselves?…' 'And that's a problem because?’ I replied. Dwayne then adopted a disappointed look. It was the look he gave whenever he had something condescending to say about me. He said solemnly to himself, 'Some people have book sense but no common sense.’ I replied, 'And you have neither.’ I then walked off. With all his supposed loyalty, less than a year later he left the warehouse after getting accepted to a higher paying job.

Which boxer’s style do you find the most aesthetically pleasing? Definitely The Lion Lennox Lewis. ‘The Lion’ is such an apt name because he does have a fighting style similar to a large cat. Lennox is a great tactician who uses his left jab to feint, taunt, displace and sometimes to smother and confuse. His left jab is like a diagnostic tool where he feels for the condition of the opponent and when the timing is right he unleashes powerful combinations. When facing shorter opponents he squats in a crab like posture and and uses his long arms and height advantage to monitor his opponents’ status, peering at them like a feline playing with its meal. If his opponent has some fight left in him and attacks, Lewis retreats in his crab like manner, smothering their offense with his own punches or jabbing them into a clinch. However he does not stick to this style. This style works for his shorter, less rangy opponents. When faced with opponents his own size and strength he's can successfully change styles from outboxer/boxer -puncher to brawler/pressure fighter. This is most evident in his fight with Vitali Klitschko where the bigger brawler’s (Klitschko) style was all wrong for Lewis’ clinical style. What I personally find pleasing about Lewis’ style is that you see the punches when they land, you see the frustration in his opponents face and the calmness in his. What I like about Lewis himself is that his boxing comes from a place of emotional maturity and self control. You see his method and you eventually see the results. His style is effective and shows a peek of the sportsmanship that lies in a sport that has its foundation in crude barbarity. Edit: If I could add the fact that Lewis is a seasoned chess player. I don't want to assume that this is a factor contributing to his typically calm and stoic demeanor, his emotional and ring intelligence. If I could dab in his personal life a bit, the fact that he is one of the few boxers to have relative success in his personal/family life, his ability to hang up his gloves and avoid any possible brain damage (as per his wife's plea) the avoidance of drug abuse, party lifestyle, scandal and controversy makes him (to me) an underrated role model in the world of sports on par with the likes of George Foreman. Just my 2¢.

What's the stupidest thing you've done for love? This wasn't a falling head over heels with the wrong person type of stupid (although that definitely was the case). This was stupid as in a Mr. Bean or Inspector Clouseau level of dimwit. I was an A level student and infatuated with one of my classmates. She didnt have the exact same feelings for me unfortunately. We both were coming to the end of our schooling. We were sent home a couple weeks before our final exams. I would literally beg her to come study with me in the National Library. The library was a brand new building with 3 floors available for the public. I went there a Saturday and was in the adult floor. I called her phone to ask her to come but she never picked up. I told her voice mail that I was in the library if she was interested in meeting me to study. A few moments later I got a voice message from her saying that she's getting ready to leave the house and might meet me. I became totally ecstatic. These were the days before WhatsApp and SMS was the chief source of texting. I sent her a text message 'What time you coming?’ I didn't notice that in my excitement I texted the above message to my own phone number rather than hers. Some seconds later I felt my phone vibrate and saw a message: 'What time you coming?’ This was the message that I accidentally sent to myself. I immediately assumed it was her and hastily replied to message (aka myself) 'I'm already here!’ I was so excited for our potential study date. I envisioned us going out for lunch and planned how it is I would ask her to go visit the zoo with me. I then felt my phone vibrate and saw a message in my inbox, 'I'm already here!’ I almost jumped out of my chair. Wow. That was quick! How did she get here so fast? I called her phone but it went straight to voicemail. I hastily sent her (aka myself) a message 'I’m up on the 2nd floor.' I then quickly went to the entrance of the building to see if I saw her. I looked around like a wild animal but didn't see her. Where was she? Why can't she ever answer her phone? I pulled out my phone to call her when I saw that I received another message: 'I'm up on the 2nd floor.’ What the hell!? I ran back to the second floor and went to the security at the entrance and asked him if he saw such and such girl and gave him her description. He stared at me in a mocking way and replied 'No.’ I went inside and searched through the entire second floor and couldn't find her. I panicked, wondering if she didn't see me and thought I was playing games and left. I replied to her (aka myself) a message, 'I'm not seeing you!!!’ I then called her phone. I was determined that she answered the call. I told myself that I wouldn't stop until she answered. During the second ring I heard a notification sound. I got another message from ‘her’ : 'I'm not seeing you!!!’ Aaargh. 'Well maybe if you pickup the goddamn phone we wouldn't have this problem!' I thought to myself. Part of me felt as though so she was toying with me while another part felt as though this was just a case of bad communication. I rang her phone nonstop until she finally answered in great annoyance. 'What!’ she almost yelled. 'Where are you?’ I almost yelled in return. 'Why is that any of your business?’ she replied in irritation. 'Because I'm looking for you. If you stopped texting me and maybe answered your phone we wouldn't have this communication problem.’ 'What are you talking about I never texted you!’ she replied. 'Come off with the games,' I said in exasperation, 'Which part of the library are you at?’ She then hung up the phone. I grew angry and decided to send her an angry message. I looked at my SMS chat history with her and was confused. Where did all her messages disappear to? I then looked at my sent messages and saw that I had been sending messages to myself all morning. There's never a moment in my life I felt more stupid than that very moment.

Why would I kill a mugger in self-defense? Are my valuables worth more than their life? I’ve been mugged four times. Two of these muggings were violent. In these muggings I had my face punched relentlessly. I had a beer bottle smashed on my head, requiring stitches. I had a gun pointed at my face. I got my pants and underwear torn open and had to walk to the police station afterwards with my junk in my hands. In both muggings I got laughed at by the muggers. I’ll never forget the moment when one of the muggers looked at me sitting defeated on the curb, robbed, bleeding and beaten. I’ll never forget how in the silence that followed he looked me in the eyes and growled ‘That’s how it is.’ In that situation I’m certain that same mugger would’ve killed me if needed. I felt a deep cynical hatred in him; that beating me to a pulp satisfied some inner rage he compartmentalized towards society. No. It wasn’t just about the money for them. They felt the world owed them something that they themselves couldn’t fathom what. What is it that I had that was so valuable to these muggers? In total I lost around $300 TT (43US), a cheap cell phone and wallet with my identification cards which would’ve been no value to them. Someone who so callously and casually engages in theft while inflicting violence upon his victims is someone who has agreed that they do not value your life nor theirs. Why must I pay special consideration to their lives while being beaten senselessly or having a knife or gun pointed at me? Does the small amount of money lost bother me? No. What bothers me is the reality that there are some people out there who saw me like garbage and inflicted a hateful beating while threatening my life, knowing fully well that the loot probably wasn’t worth it. My valuables may not be worth more than a human life but if in self defense I had fatally shot my armed and/or violent mugger, I would not be sending flowers to his family nor showing up at his funeral, nor would I suffer any sleepless nights over it. As the old folks in Trinidad love to say; how you make your bed is how you lie on it.

What is the cringiest name you have seen/heard given to a child? I worked in a school where there was a girl named Supreme Hurst. I asked her how she ended up with such a unique name and she said she hadn’t the faintest clue other than it was the name her dad chose. Out of curiosity I looked up her name to see if there was some kind of meaning behind it. I found out that there is an Oldsmobile car model with that very name. I would’ve loved to have known if it was by coincidence or intentional that her dad named her after such an unimpressive car. When I showed her the car she was quite disappointed it wasn’t a luxury vehicle. She explained that once she got married her name would change so it didn’t bother her that much. Some months later she got into a relationship with a boy named Stark Grimes. I kid you not. He’s not an aspiring rapper. That’s the name on his birth certificate. I was flabbergasted. The girl with the weirdest name I ever heard of was dating the boy with the weirdest name I ever heard of. I told her in jest that if they got married Supreme Grimes seemed far worse than Supreme Hurst. Stark wasn’t a bad chap. He was witty, well behaved and had a YouTube channel that had some pretty well produced Trinidad-oriented comedy. However the relationship didn’t last. Supreme Hurst and Stark Grimes went their separate ways after a few months of dating. Unfortunately I can’t find any of Supreme’s social media profiles. It’s been a decade since I heard from her. I’m assuming she got married and had that long awaited name change. I just hope for her sake she didn’t get married to a guy with the surname Dick.

What is wrong with parents these days that they don’t teach their kids manners & respect? About a year ago a teacher brought a parent to me. The parent was a mother of two of the most atrocious girls in the school. These were girls who got into fights, provoked others into fighting through taunting and accusing on social media, disrespected everyone in positions of authority and had a nasty, defiant attitude in general. The teacher wanted the parent to get an overall view of all the trouble these girls caused and how desperately they were in need of an intervention. As a librarian for the school library I had had a few bad encounters with the girls so seeing that the mother was there waiting patiently for my story (and wearing a T-shirt that showed that she worked for the police service) I was only too glad to give her the details of my experience and my hope for these girls and their future. After about 2 minutes of recounting my experience with them and making impassioned pleas I glanced at the mother's face and noticed that there was not a trace of emotion. There was an awkward silence as I waited for her to say something. 'Is that all?’ she said with an irritated tone. 'Yes' I replied. 'Did they do anything to you personally?’ she added. 'No. It's not about me. It's about the library…..it's about the school.’ There was another pause. 'So are you banning them from your library?’ she said. 'No I never said I was banning them from the library.’ With that said she remained silent and stared at me, waiting for me to dismiss the conversation of which I did. She then left with the teacher to talk to another teacher who had had encounters with them. Later that day I heard that that was the formula she applied in all the conversations. She listened to every teacher's complaint and simply waited to hear if any action was going to be taken against her girls. She was pumped and ready to fight anyone who was going to take action against her girls or deny them their ‘rights.’ She had no solutions in her mind as to the problems the girls caused because in her mind there were no problems. The girls were defiant against the school system because the mother was defiant against the system. The mom's attitude was that the school system and its rules were a big joke; that all kids behaved like her daughters behaved and she was not having her daughters victimised. So my answer to all this is parents don't teach manners and respect to their kids because they don't believe in the system and they think they are entitled to their own set of rules to live by.

What is the luckiest thing that happened to you? Over twenty years ago I was a mere lad of 17 and staying at a cousin's house for the holidays. My aunt was fed up of us staying in the living room all day playing video games and sent us to walk the dogs. The area was a very safe upper middle class location fringed by mountains and a picturesque golf course nearby. My brother, myself and our cousin walked the quiet road calmly discussing our victories in the gaming world when suddenly we heard the ferocious growling and snapping of a giant pitbull which had broken off its owner’s iron chain and was heading towards us in a mad fury, saliva dripping from its mouth. We stood frozen, all three of us knowing fully well that we were going to get mauled. The minute the dog's feet touched the road a speeding pickup came out of nowhere knocked it on the head. The sound of the hit was loud and blood curdling. It literally sounded like a car crash. The force was enough to give instant death to a human yet the dog managed to run back to its house. The driver sped off without even a moment's thought as to what just happened. It was almost as though Jesus Himself was driving that pickup that saved us from getting severely mauled. We stood there petrified, not knowing what to do or say. Should we quickly head back home? Should we query with the owner as to whether the dog was alive? Should we make a report to the police? None of these logical things we did. Instead we had an argument as to whether the dog was alive or not, if it was, whether it was severely concussed or just fine and whether the skull of a pitbull was tougher than that of a human. My cousin, a lover of physics, then made an argument as to whether a pitbull as such, running at 130km an hour could ram into and overturn a small car. I opted out of this argument and took some time reflecting on the poor dog. I'm glad to be unscarred but to this day I hope the bugger didnt suffer too much.

What is your review of The Banshees of Inisherin? Watched this last Saturday with my girlfriend who thought it looked fascinating. Reading the two other reviews I agree with both as they mention that as a film it remains with you. To this hour it is still slowly digesting into my subconscious. I must stress on the word slow though. That is one of the biggest issues I had with the film. There's slow burner, where something is supposed to happen to connect the dots and then there's just slow, where there is little to no point. It's just slow for being slow's sake. That's the case with Banshees imho. The film posits the reason for the slowness being that Inisherin is a remote isle off Ireland and it's the 1920s. There is no electricity and the isle is so dull best friends no longer speaking could make front page news. This is actually the basis of the plot. Colin Farrel's Pádraic and Brendon Gleeson's Colm are no longer on speaking terms. Pádraic wants to continue idle chatting over beers in the pub while Colm wants more in life. This sets the stage for a series of surreal events that's supposed to be a mataphor for Irish Republicanism or something or the other. It is at that point where the film started losing me slowly. The cast is great, particularly Colin Farrell's slow-witted but good natured character who reminds me of George W Bush at times. He hits the nail on the head as a middle-aged, needy, ineffectual drunk. The cinematography is pretty and it does give a genuine sense of a place lost in time exactly one century ago. However both my girlfriend and I felt as though there was really no point. In beating on the head its symbolism and satire the movie missed out on what could've been a truly good period piece. My rating ** out of 4.

In Saving Private Ryan, is Upham the biggest scumbag in movie history? It’s funny how the human psyche works. In that famous scene where the German (Steamboat Willie) that Upham saved from execution is struggling with Private Mellish on the ground, about to drive a knife into him, our hatred is directed to Upham who stands at the stairs, armed to the teeth with ammo and a rifle, but does nothing. Upham knows what is happening but is undergoing some state of shock and paralysis. As the knife is driven into Mellish and Upham remains cowering at the spot it creates one of the most sad and frustrating scenes in cinema history and renders Upham one of the most detested film characters ever to grace the screen. Funny how no one directs a quarter of that hate to the real scumbag Steamboat Willie. Our psyche works in a way in that we accept killing and violence as part of our human condition. However the thing we collectively and subconsciously detest the most as humans is disloyalty and selfishness, especially in times when camaraderie is crucial to the survival of all. The group all had differing values and opinions but they sacrificed their dislikes and disagreements for the sake of completing the mission or at least survival. They were all forced to find some stupid kid named Ryan who got caught/lost and his mama wanted him home. This was just fresh after the horror and trauma of D-Day Normandy. By this point in the Ryan mission most of the group had been killed and remaining few relied heavily on each other’s loyalty and camaraderie to defend one another. Upham, from the very beginning, stuck out like a crusty old sore thumb. Upham demonstrated a more pacifist intellectual side. He did not have a kill count and hoped to avoid bloodshed as much as possible and hopefully stave off some needless killing. His lack of combat experience combined with his unrealistic ideals irritated his fellow men but at the end of the day he provided a valuable service in regards to being a solid translator. Love him or hate him, he did his primary job and he did somewhat redeem himself of the burden of Mellish’s death by killing Steamboat Willie the second time he was captured, finally understanding that you can’t always play by the rules when it comes to war. He is the one of the most frustrating characters but he’s not the biggest scumbag. That award goes to the Ukrainian collaborators particularly the one nicknamed Little Policeman in the Russian WWII film Come and See. Little Policeman is a dwarfish, hideous man that has led the Nazis to several Belarusian villages and jeers at countless throngs of women, children and elderly people being shot and burned alive. Little Policeman has no allegiance with anyone. He is concerned with saving his own skin and as such he relishes in whatever happens at the moment as long as it favors him. The Nazis see him as a clown and as such he portrays himself as a grotesque caricature of one for their delight, with his shrill, unsettling voice, sporting a wooden ‘gun’ and helmet with a crude swastika self painted on its surface. Never before have I witnessed such a scumbag that I felt like destroying my TV in anger whenever he came onto the screen. Even more disgusting is how he and the other collaborators plead for their lives when they are caught by the resistance. They claim to be victims and beg to be allowed to kill the Nazi captives to show their new loyalty. Little Policeman did not kill or hurt or single person in the film but he was detested far more than the actual Nazis themselves because of his sickening treachery and selfishness. His eventual death (along with the rest of collaborators and Nazi captives) is one of the most redeeming moments in film. He makes Upham look like General Patton in comparison.

What are some inaccuracies or criticisms of JD Vance's book "Hillbilly Elegy"? Oh here we go again. So I'm supposed to assume this has nothing to do with the fact that Trump just appointed JD Vance as his running mate for Vice President. No. The person who asked the question is genuinely interested in a review of Vance's book and the question is in no way a negatively leading question. I haven't read the book yet but I saw the movie. I remember the movie was thrashed by critics and Hollywood acted as though Amy Adams should be drawn and quartered for taking part in such political, propagandist rubbish. The criticism was non stop. I almost believed what the media was saying. Then I watched it and was surprised to discover that it was a really good movie. It was just a simple story about a guy who struggled in life with poverty and drugs in his family and managed to make something of himself thanks to the two people who supported him in his life. The performances were excellent, particularly Amy Adams and Glenn Close and there was nothing remotely political or propagandist about the story. There is nothing in the book that merits me investigating the inaccuracies in the book. It is a memoir. Vance doesn't make any fantastic claims. It's not like Catch Me if You Can or My Wicked Wicked Ways. Did he exaggerate? Did his mother really overdose on heroin or was she just taking a nap? Is Vance's wife really of Indian descent or just three quarters Indian? Did Vance really drive all night to a job interview right after wrestling a heroin needle from his mother or did he just have a stern argument with her, took a nap and a plane the next morning? Does that matter? Are these the ‘inaccuracies’ that should make us condemn the book and Vance? It's astonishing how much the modern left have idealised themselves into believing that they are the final say in regards to everything. That they are never wrong. Any other opinions are stupid, racist or sexist. As a Trinidadian I sometimes argue with such people as to the reality of what goes on on in my country. People who've never even set foot in the country. When will they realize that the more arrogant they behave and the more they tell people what they ought to believe, think, say and feel, the more people will become disenchanted and start doing the opposite of what they suggest. I'm certain Vance's book and the film will see a surge in sales and streaming in the upcoming weeks. I might even come around to reading it, simply because so many critics angrily claim that I shouldn't.

Would Hollywood actor Brad Pitt have made it in old or classic Hollywood back in the day? Very interesting question. For the sake of simplification let's just assume that by Classic Hollywood you mean the Hays Code era of Hollywood whereas sex, nudity, graphic violence, rape etc could not be demonstrated in Hollywood films. (1934 — 1968) 1930s — 1940s Hollywood Hollywood in the aftermath of the Great Depression and the outbreak of the Second World War. This is the age of the Go-Getter and although silent movies are now obsolete, it's exaggerative stage acting style is still rampant. Audiences of this era are favorable towards a certain type of male screen presence. Popular actors of the era are mostly an embodiment of what were considered desirable, manly traits. This is the era of Clark Gable, Cary Grant, Gary Cooper, James Stewart, Errol Flynn, John Wayne and Henry Fonda. The archetypal male film star was usually tall (over 6 feet), athletic, handsome, possessing a rich and resonant voice and possessing a certain self assured alpha male quality. The kind of man who would've made a great career as a top salesman or workforce motivator. The nation was wounded after two World Wars and these idealistic tropes were coveted by men and women alike. It was an age that was obsessively preoccupied with courage, persistence and survival. It was the era of sucking in your emotions and holding your chin high. Unless in possession of exemplary acting skills or song and dance expertise, actors who lacked several of these traits were relegated to minor supporting roles, comic relief roles, extras, stunt work or failed to make it in the film industry at all. Despite being ruggedly handsome, Brad Pitt would've had a hard time getting work in Hollywood during this era. He did not fit the height requirement, his voice would not be considered rich and animated and his brooding, sombre presence would've been a turn off for a national audience hungry for the next cocky, high shouldered, go-getting macho man. 1950s Hollywood The ideal aforementioned leading man is still prevalent with Charlton Heston, Gregory Peck, Burt Lancaster, and Rock Hudson maintaining the status quo. However standards are less rigid as actors like William Holden, Frank Sinatra, Kirk Douglas, Yul Brynner and Tony Curtis, who have the macho appeal but lack the height, are some of the top stars. A growing interest in brooding more sensitive type 'method' acting is gaining ground with the likes of James Dean, Marlon Brando and Paul Newman. Brad Pitt would've been better able to find work in such type roles but the competition would be fierce and only those with extensive stage experience and schooled in New York at the Actor's Studio would get top priority over some quiet, good looking guy from Missouri. 1960s Hollywood The growing counterculture revolution is finally making an impact on Hollywood. While the war scarred older generation is fading to make way for the Baby Boomers, the conservative values and ideal macho leading man is no longer as appealing for those hungry for emotional catharsis. The audience is yearning for a leading man who they could relate to, who shares their flaws and can demonstrate vulnerability. Even the more macho type actors are expected to demonstate weakness and more sensitivity. These would include Clint Eastwood, Sean Connery, Charles Bronson, Steve McQueen, Robert Redford, George Kennedy and Rod Steiger. Slurred speaking (Marlon Brando), meek voiced (Eastwood) overweight (Steiger) and short stature (Bronson) are traits no longer shunned by Hollywood elite. Brad Pitt would've found the greatest chance of obtaining prominent roles during this era. Who knows he might've even replaced Robert Redford in Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid.

What one thing did your father do that left your mother sobbing? Wasn't my biological father but my stepfather. Calling him 'stepfather’ is a bit of a compliment. He basically lived off my mom, was unemployed more often than not and barely provided anything for the rent free roof that lay above his head. Yet my mother persevered. She got involved with my biological father at a tender age and that relationship was traumatic due to his bipolar disorder. She was intent on having a proper family with my stepfather, especially after she bore him two daughters. As mentioned before he was more often unemployed and when when he did find a job it was temporary as he worked in construction. However, in the early 2000s he found some measure of success in the field and started getting established as a professional foreman. He got high paying, big contract jobs and had the power to hire and fire. Soon most of the guys in the street were given jobs by my stepfather and some of the neighborhood women sent love letters in the mailbox to my mother's ire. My stepfather would laugh it off. However as the months turned into years my mother calculated that with the amount of money my stepfather made, it wasn't reflected in the household. We were still broke, had almost no furniture, bills still piled up and the money he gave her was not any significant improvement to when he was roughing it. Things got worse when my stepfather would constantly disappear for the fortnight weekend, especially when he got his salary. When he gave my mother what scanty money remained in his wallet it led to ugly arguments. Everyone told my mother that my stepfather had to be seeing another woman. My mother refused to believe it. Instead she tried to nag, quarrel and harrass him into doing what was right and it just created more nasty arguments. She then resolved that he could no longer live with us but could see his daughters on the weekend. She believed this would change his ways. He readily agreed to this. One fateful Friday evening I was home and the phone rang. I answered it. I heard my stepfather's voice asking for 'Tracey.’ Tracey was the name of our neighbor's daughter. She was 24 years old and had a reputation. I said Tracey didn't live here. When my stepfather recognized my voice he immediately hung up the phone. My mother came and asked me who called. 'It's just S****n.’ 'What does he want?’ my mother said irritably. 'I dunno,' I replied, 'He just asked to talk to Tracey….I think he dialled the wrong number.’ At 16 years old I was a bit naive to comprehend what all this meant. However I'd never forget seeing my mother's face drop like she saw death materialize in front of her and later tears formed in her eyes. My stepfather was getting involved with our neighbor's daughter right across the street. That's where his money went. That meant everyone knew about it except her. That meant she was a fool. They parted ways permanently afterwards. My stepfather would demand that I say that I was mistaken. That it wasn't him who called. He's 68 now and his daughters want nothing to do with him. It really affected my mother as she became more withdrawn and a bit of a recluse and a hoarder. They both are barely on speaking terms. Sometimes I feel as though I should've had more common sense and just kept my mouth shut.

What screams "I'm pretending to be upper class"? My cousin David lived for two years in Trinidad after his upper-middle class parents decided to return to their homeland to retire. David did his SATs at ISPS (International School of Port of Spain), a school which caters to mostly foreign upper-middle/upper class students. It was there that he befriended Carlos. Carlos was a Venezuelan who had an immense stroke of luck. Carlos came from a very poor family in Venezuela and was said to be adopted on a charitable impulse by a rich Texas oil man. Carlos’ foster father didn't intend to have much of a relationship with him but rather wanted to make a point of turning Carlos' life around. He shipped Carlos off to Trinidad and ISPS and left with him a sizable monthly allowance to finish his SATs and pursue a college degree. It was there that Carlos met my cousin David. David did not like Carlos in the least bit. Carlos was the biggest show-off/braggart at ISPS. His first action upon being set to his own devices was to rent a furnished luxury apartment in Goodwood Park (the Beverly Hills of Trinidad). With this apartment he gained fame for hosting weekly parties for his fellow schoolmates laden with weed and alcohol. Like most of Carlos' ‘friends’ David befriended Carlos solely for the opportunity to be invited to these parties. Carlos' attendance at school and his grades soured but he didn't care. He took out a Range Rover and after a drunken night racing along the North Coast he crashed the vehicle and had it wrote off. It was a miracle that he survived and ought to have been an epiphany to change his ways. He didn't. His two years in ISPS were spent indulging, fraternising, boasting, drinking, smoking, chasing girls and maintaining the image of being the most popular student at ISPS. He wasn't the most popular. He was the most infamous. It was hard to find someone who truly liked him. I would include myself in that category. Once when I was in a restaurant with David, Carlos and a few of David's friends, I realized that I had no money for a meal. I made a joke about it. I told everyone that I would be taxing everyone 5% of their meal for charity as I was broke at the moment. Everyone laughed except Carlos who stared at me in horror as though I cursed God and my mother in one sentence. ‘Don’t go anywhere if you don't have any mah-nee!’ Carlos admonished towards me in a stern Venezuelan accent. It was strange how he was so deeply offended by someone near him making a joke about not having money and begging. Everyone stopped laughing. David paid for my meal making sure Carlos didn't notice. Carlos graduated with failing grades and soon found that his funds were depleted. He would guilt trip several of his ‘friends’ for lodging, reminding them of all that he lavished upon them. He reassured them that his foster father was going to send for him to return to the US. This of course was discovered to be a lie, his foster father had washed his hand of an adult Carlos. He found himself broke and homeless. Carlos still lives in Trinidad. He works an ordinary job and rents an unimpressive furniture-less apartment that is above his means. To this day he still brags about his brief period of wealth. His former colleagues take great pains avoiding him whenever they are aware he is around. Otherwise he would stop them in their tracks to entertain lengthy one-sided discussions about the good old days and would inveigle them to grab some drinks in a fancy pub in which they would listen to his ridiculous plans to score big, be constantly reminded of how much he did for their enjoyment at ISPS and then be forced to pay for the bill that he ran up but can't afford with the promise that ‘Drinks are on me next time amigo.’ Such is the life of Carlos. So to answer the question ‘What screams "I'm pretending to be upper class?”’ People like Carlos.

Do you think Europe is more racist than the USA? I haven't been to the whole of Europe and I haven't travelled all the States of the USA. However I've been to Wales and Kentucky recently and I've had two encounters that I think could be used as data towards answering the above question. Aberystwyth, Wales. I was a student on a scholar for a Masters degree along with a few fellow Trinidadians. When we went out shopping, our favourite store by far was Poundland. We patronized Poundland almost on a daily basis buying chocolates, sweets and various goodies for a pound each to our hearts’ delight. Despite the noticeable frigidity of many people in the area we saw, most were helpful and polite. One day at Poundland I was informed that there were rewards to anyone with purchases of over £25 pounds and up. The more you spent the better the reward. After shopping I checked my receipt and saw that I qualified to redeem a cool digital sports watch. I went over to the guy at customer service and showed my receipt. People from Aberystwyth tend to wear a constant smile that fluctuates from smile to smirk according to the mood/situation. This guy's smile changed to a definite smirk when he saw me waving my receipt. ‘What’s that you say?’ he said as though I were speaking Swahili. ‘I want to get the watch.’ I repeated for the third time, ‘I spent over thirty pounds.’ He watched me waving my receipt with a confused expression on his face as though I were a lunatic waving a bill of rights. ‘Come again?’ he said and I knew he was playing stupid and I started to get annoyed. I notice that he's glancing towards the back of the store as if to communicate to the others that he wanted someone else to come over. Suddenly an older man came towards us and asked what was the problem. I explained that I wanted to redeem my points for the sports watch. I showed him the receipt but he stares at me up and down instead. ‘You’re not from the UK I would guess,’ he says. I said no, that I was here on studies. He hemmed and hawed and then said that the prizes are meant for UK citizens. I told him that there was no mention of that in the advertisement hanging on the wall next to him. He hemmed and hawed again and said that it may not be written in the ad but the promotion is to encourage locals to shop at Poundland more. I asked to speak to the manager and with a smirk he said, ‘Nice to meet you. I'm the manager Steve.’ Him and the other worker then proceeded to stare at me, brandishing their wide smile-smirks. Deciding not to make a ruckus I left the matter at that. Georgetown, Kentucky I visited my girlfriend and we stopped at the police station at the above location for her to deal with a matter. While I was waiting for her in the car I grew bored after 30 minutes. There was a swarm of bees that surrounded the area and as they left I went out to take a video of them as the swarmed off. A police car rolls up about 20 feet away from me and the driver's window rolls down. A latino officer then smiles at me and says ‘Hey.’ I said Hi. He says something else but I couldn't hear him so I went closer to his vehicle. He asks me what I was doing there in the car park and I explained that I was waiting for a friend inside the station. He asked me where I was from and I explained that I was from the Caribbean. Suddenly another police car comes speedily from the opposite direction and parks in an aggressive manner as if to cut me off from running away. A tall stocky Caucasian officer exits the vehicle and comes towards me and demands that I keep my hands away from my pockets. He proceeds to search me and discovers me unarmed. He explains that someone reported me as a suspicious individual hanging around the police station parking lot. I explained that I was just a tourist from the Caribbean. They explained that loitering about a police station is seen as suspicious in the State of Kentucky and that I should remain in my vehicle if I waited on my friend here. Tall stocky guy stares at me and asks if I have any questions myself. I said no but I said I appreciated how alert they were and if only Trinidad had such dedicated officers we would have less crime. They both laugh awkwardly and stocky guy pats me on my shoulder like a schoolkid. They both leave without another word. In conclusion I would honestly say that my experience in Wales seemed to border more on seething racism rather my experience in Kentucky. I believe the officers in Georgetown were doing their job whilst the staff at Poundland at Aberystwyth were discriminating in a subtle manner. There was a certain deep seated resentment I felt in Wales whilst in Kentucky it was more of a passive wariness. I felt as though I could've communicated to the officers and reach a certain compromise whilst with the Poundland staff I felt like a brick wall was between us. I also felt like that with the locals of Kentucky, a friendly warmth while in Aberystwyth it was an air of cold professionalism for the most part. In rural Kentucky, places like Kuttawa and Paducah I got no strange looks and witnessed black people working alongside whites in seeming normalcy whereas in Aberystwyth the one black person I witnessed was a homeless man and the one mixed race person was young man working in a thrift shop. So in my honest and ignorant opinion I would think that racism would be more prevalent in a subtle, passive aggressive manner in Europe whilst in the US it can happen due to wariness of strangers rather than due to race. Edit: There is one commenter who continuously alleges that I’ve fabricated my story about my visit to Wales and Aberystwyth. Every time I reply with evidence to him it somehow disappears so I’ve decided to put the evidence where it can’t be removed here in the answer.

Have you ever dated anyone who was married? If so, how did the relationship go? My ex, the mother of my child, was still legally married when we started dating. I am not one to go after married women but she claimed when I first met her that she was entering divorce proceedings. That, along with several other promises, was never fulfilled. The relationship was the textbook whirlwind romance. Things took off like lightning and then thunder crashed and a heavy rain fell on me for several years. My advice is to avoid dating anyone married but doesn't have the decency to follow through with a proper divorce yet wants to enter into the world of dating. They made a vow to their spouse to be with them for better, for worse, for richer, for poorer, in sickness and in health. If they don't have the decency to get a divorce, what makes you think they will be loyal to you? I guarantee they will make you worse, poorer and sick all at once.
