What 1980s movies were huge at the time but are now almost forgotten? The Abyss (1989) As a child of the 90s this movie was THE epic sci-fi fantasy movie while growing up in that era. It would show practically every summer on our local TV and even with a runtime of three hours long (with advertisements) my brother and I devoured it with a passion that we were never to experience again. I read critics joke that director James Cameron was: Therefore The Abyss was the product of those desires as it is sometimes condescendingly referred to as Close Encounters of the Third Kind…….Underwater. Regardless of the comparison after recently rewatching both movies I consider, by a thin margin, The Abyss to be the superior movie (because Richard Dreyfuss' character in Encounters is an annoying twat.) In the film, a team of divers, scientists, Navy SEALS and the like is sent to recover a sunken submarine and in the process encounter some strange activity. Unlike Encounters I love all the characters in The Abyss and find them all believable and likable. There are so many plotholes in Encounters that anybody with at least a high school education would find several scenes questionable. (So the Government has made so much effort to hide a top secret alien meeting mission from the public yet some crazy, deadbeat dad manages to evade helicopters, highly trained defense force operatives and scale a mountain with a grieving, frantic mom on tow so he could jump aboard a spacecraft of intergalactic kidnappers whose sole intention are to breed hideous human-alien hybrid children…….all so he doesn't have to pay child support.) Jokes aside, I think in retrospect Spielberg bit off far too much than he could chew. He never worked in top secret Government operatives so the story is a bit far fetched. Cameron on the other hand is a professional deep sea explorer so the movie doesn't go too far off the suspension of disbelief scale into ludicrousness. Both movies have stunning finales but I would personally go with The Abyss in terms of scale and wonder whereas Encounters is more impressive in terms of special effects. Sadly The Abyss is hardly ever mentioned and is on the road to becoming a lost classic. At least in my book.

What is the biggest problem caused by an inheritance or a will that you ever saw or heard about? Some years ago, when I was hunting for a house I found a property that seemingly had my name stamped on it. It was a neat little hillside property with two bedrooms that was built sturdily and with class. It was one of those good old-fashioned houses that was built in the 70s/80s with a cute porch and terrazzo flooring. The best part was it was within the mortgage the bank offered me. I called the owner and arranged for a proper tour. I brought my ex with me (who like most women, observed things men wouldn't notice) and we climbed the hill and waited in the yard for the owner to arrive. She then motioned to me that in the yard (just a few feet from one of the bedrooms) was this awful looking makeshift shack that looked to be someone's home. What we in Trinidad refer to as a 'Piper Shack.’ She told me that somebody was squatting on the property. I was really looking forward to getting the house and said the shack was probably just a storage shed. She then pointed to a DirectTV satellite on the roof and some crude plumbing that sent filthy water towards the main house. While contemplating all of this, a wild-looking man appeared out of nowhere and loudly greeted us. He told us the house we were interested is a great house and that so many people are interested in it. We then watched him as he entered the shack. I was completely disheartened but I said that this must be some guy hired to maintain the house temporarily. My ex called me a fool. That he was most obviously a squatter. Two men arrived and introduced themselves as the owners. They were pleasant and they spoke with warm conviction of how great the house was and how it was a shame that they were selling it for so low a price. They explained that they were cousins and the house was willed to them by their uncle who died recently. The uncle had no children of his own and left everything to his closest kin. The cousins, who had homes of their own decided to sell the house and split the money. The younger cousin then went on a tangent reminiscing about how nice their old uncle was and how much work he did on the house. 'And who's that man living in the back there,' my ex bluntly interjected. I could see disappointment swell up on the man's face. He obviously wanted to avoid the subject. He explained that his uncle had no one in his old age. He was unmarried and the nephews were grown and living their lives with their families. The uncle befriended a wandering drug addict (‘piper’ in Trinidad terms) and allowed for the man to build his shack in the yard, use his electricity and water and even included in the will that the man have rights to live there as long as he wants. 'But he's a real nice man when you get to know him!' the other cousin chimed in, 'He's very helpful with manual labor. He could watch after your house for you when you're away!’ It was such a sad sight to see them trying to pitch the idea that having a drug addicted, mentally unstable man living in your yard and with legal rights could actually be a good thing. They said that once we saw inside the house we'd see how great of a deal we were getting. In the end we decided that it wasn't worth our while and politely declined.

Do you feel uncomfortable at work around certain co-workers? If so, why? There’s a running joke on online chat-rooms and forums about people who look like created players. If you are/were an avid gamer you would get the joke instantly. If you aren’t then a created player is when gamers have the option of creating their own customized player i.e. choosing their skin colour, height, hairstyle, weight, clothes etc. Many gamers attempt to make the most random or disturbing looking player possible just for kicks e.g huge head, clown hair, wide apart eyes, inhuman skin tone etc. In the real world, it’s hardly likely you would come across anyone looking like these guys anytime soon but on the rare occasion that you do, you tell yourself, ‘Hey! That guy looks like a created player!’ Frivolity out of the way, there’s a man in my workplace who is like a created player. He’s not eerie looking but he is eerie in that no one can could put a finger on his personality without using the word ‘random.’ One day he would swagger to work looking as though he stepped off the set of a poor man’s Western movie, complete with snakeskin cowboy boots, cowboy hat, shirt opened up at the chest and RayBan shades (we work in a school by the way). Another day he would come dressed overly modest as though he spent the summer with monks in Tibet with a head shaved bald, large flowing shirt and giving an aura of calm resolve. Then another day would be a day of espionage as he would be dressed incognito and would spend the day peeping from behind a newspaper at God knows what. If you try to talk to him, you leave with a feeling of discomforting bewilderment. You would ask him a basic, ‘How did you spend your weekend?’ and he would start talking about why every teenager nearing adulthood should practice Feng Shui. Or He would come to you with an angry rant about why he will not teach any unvaccinated students while he himself isn’t vaccinated and hardly wears his masks. Or He would speak ill of teachers who come late to school while he himself has an abysmal regularity and punctuality rate. Everything about him is just random and contradictory. No one knows what he’s up to where he came from and where he’s going. But for me, though it’s uncomfortable to communicate with him, it’s fun to see the ultimate, living breathing created player.

What's the worst experience you've had with telling someone you had feelings for them? While at University I observed that any course that had the word 'Management’ within its name was bound to be laden with beautiful women. When I did Management Accounting I was introduced by Lorna, a good female friend of mine, to this tall, shapely and somewhat quirky young lady with thick black curls, full lips and a shapely body. The only flaw that I observed was she had a slight paunch. Her name was Gabrielle or Gabby as she preferred to be called. She had an outspoken yet aloof disposition whereby she could say the most unfiltered thing and it would never come across offensive, well to me at least. I recall while walking with her and Lorna, Gabby randomly blurted out that my fantasy would be for her and Lorna to carry me to some secret location for a lapdance and ménage à trois. Lorna went red, either in anger, embarassment or a combination of the two. I soon discovered that Gabby's sister attended the school where I worked. I was never able to procure Gabby's phone number as I never got another chance encounter (she was very delinquent in class attendance) and Lorna didn't have it either. I then came up with what I considered a fool proof idea. I would write an old fashioned love letter, explaining my feelings for her and sealed with a kiss I would carry it to her sister to have it delivered to Gabby. All my feelings just flowed out of me as I wrote that long letter. I put a sticker of a rose and then neatly folded it into a red envelope. When I came upon the sister (12 years old at the time) I explained to her my feelings for Gabby and my intention for her to deliver this letter of love to her. I was expecting the sister to gush and swoon (as girls her age are prone to do regarding such romance) but instead she gave me an odd look of confusion and disbelief. 'Are you sure?’ Was all she could reply. 'Yeah,' I said flatly, 'Your sister made such an impression on me. I can't stop thinking of her.’ 'Why don't you just tell her yourself?’ the sister replied in that off-putting, emotionless tone quite strange for a girl her age. 'I don't have her phone number,' I replied and after a brief silence where I'm sure the sister sized me up and decided not to give me Gabby's number, she acquiesced to delivering the letter. The following day, I went up to the sister anxious to hear of what was Gabby's response or better yet collect a letter of my own. 'Did you give her the letter? I asked excitedly. The sister avoided my glances. 'Yeah.' I waited for her response. 'And what happened?’ I said, detecting a faint feeling that this wasn't going to work out well. 'She just looked at it and asked who it was from.’ Another silence. 'And what happened after?’ I said with an underlying sense of dread. 'She asked me what it was you wanted. I told her that you liked her…..she looked at the letter and then put it on her dresser.’ I felt my stomach tighten. 'Didnt she read the letter?’ 'No,' the sister flatly replied, 'She still hasn't opened it.’ There was an awkward silence and the sister then uttered, 'Sir I have to go.’ I felt like the world's biggest clown. I half imagined the sister running to tell a her classmates what a loser Mr. Williamson was and then describing the story. Fast forward four months later and I'm shopping around for car insurance. I head into this big building and none other than Gabby is sitting at the reception office, heavily pregnant. She engages me in delightful quirky conversation as normal almost as though the whole love letter incident was a figment of my imagination. I bid her adieu and immediately called Lorna to tell her what happened to her friend. 'My friend!’ Lorna said shocked, 'She wasn't my friend. She's just a girl from my class. I thought she was your friend! Didn't you realize she was pregnant?’ I replied no and then explained my prior feelings for Gabby and the whole love letter fiasco. 'You sent Gabby a love letter!’ Lorna cried in great shock, 'But she's pregnant….and she's engaged. Didn't you see the ring on her finger?’ Suddenly I just felt like a massive brick landed on my head. Soon the pieces started to fit together.

Was Shelley Duvall considered attractive? When I was a boy growing up, this character was the epitome of ‘attractive’ among boys my age: This was the exact opposite: Now that I'm a full grown adult I find it odd that my attraction has reversed. Nowadays I would consider prime Shelley Duvall far more attractive than prime Pamela Anderson. I'm not saying this as a form of virtue signalling due to her sad passing. I've observed photos from her in the past and discovered that she possessed a very unique beauty. This beauty was exploited quite often in her roles and modeling in the 1970s. Sadly she was only given frumpy housewife and plain Jane supporting roles into the 80s and 90s and all but disappeared at the turn of the millenium, only resurfacing for that infamous Dr. Phil interview in 2016. Despite being tall and thin, with big ears and eyes and crooked teeth Shelley Duvall’s looks were all natural. This might be my personal opinion but she seemed to possess a certain humility about her; the kind of person who wouldn't put on airs about herself and be friendly to almost anyone. Pamela Anderson’s beauty involved a lot of plastic surgery, hair dye and excessive makeup. To each his own but in a hypothetical party full of people I'd make a bee line to be the first to offer a drink to Shelley Duvall. Then we'd talk, sit and laugh at all the hopelessly shallow guys flocking around Pamela Anderson at the other end of the room. RIP

What is an example of an album that, in your opinion, was ruined by the producer and/or the production? It always blows my mind why no one mentions how awfully inconsistent the sound is in Jimi Hendrix's legendary Are You Experienced album. Not saying that it's a bad album, it's one of the greatest albums on Earth. However I can't help but shudder when I hear sound inconsistencies and downright amateurish recording. It's so sad that someone like Hendrix who was possibly the greatest guitarist of the 20th century had his masterpiece recorded in mono. His complex arrangements condescended to just a flat block of sound. Worse yet, because of financial burden, Chas Chandler, the producer and member of The Animals, had the album recorded in 16 different sessions at 3 different locations. When you go from track to track you can hear the chaos behind the production. Songs like Manic Depression, Stone Free and May This Be Love sound hollow as though recorded in someone's basement whilst Fire, Purple Haze and Hey Joe are treated with tender loving care. Love or Confusion sounds as though Chandler was tripping acid while recording and simply toying with the mix as within a few seconds the volume suddenly increases in itself erratically and from then on it's a brawl between guitar, bass and drums. In many instances the Hendrix's voice and guitar overwhelms Mitch Mitchell's drums and Noel Reddings bass. As much as I love Hendrix and his guitar prowess, he wasn't the greatest of vocalists and some tracks could of benefitted with greater accentuation of his talented bandmates. All in all, the chaotic production behind Are You Experienced makes it feel more like a collection of B sides (exceptional B sides) rather than a work of art. Each track takes me to a different place, but not in a good way. I'm sure this wasn't the ‘Experience’ Hendrix wanted the world to have, but say what, it's still an excellent album.

Why do people think Midsommar is a good horror movie? When I'm watching the movie, I didn't think it's scared even a bit. If you go to watch Midsommar simply to get 'scared’ then you are in for a disappointment. It may not scare you in the sense that a knife wielding, mask wearing stalker/killer may or an evil, spectral entity that comes after you through your television but it may build feelings ranging from discomfort to dread to shock. It does not rely on fantastic and nightmarish tropes: ghouls, monsters and masked murderers etc. It doesn't condescend to our primitive childhood fears of a single creature/person out to get us (typically in the darkness of night). Most generic horrors play to our primitive childish fears: unwholesome locations, darkness, ugliness, being alone, unexplainable phenomena, pain, danger, the unknown etc. Midsommar does the opposite we are treated to a sunny, picturesque location full of wide open fields, brightly painted buildings and smiling beautiful people. Midsommar is not traditionally ‘scary’ because none of the characters are villains/monsters. None of the acts commited are evil when viewed in a purely cultural context. The film allows you to ponder on the cruelty and barbarism of several centuries past and at the same time offers a critique as to whether the self-centred, indifference that is characteric of our modern times is any better. Midsommar is a slow burning, psychological horror. It is one of the most disturbing movies I've seen in a long time, let alone one of the best. Ari Aster's directing style had been compared to Stanley Kubrick and I can really see the influence from The Shining, another slow burn, psychological horror. The story involves a young woman who recently suffers from a personal tragedy going to rural Sweden with her boyfriend and his college friends and witness/partake in the pagan Midsommar festival held once every 90 years. Little to their knowledge the participants take the festival a little more seriously than to their liking. I consider Midsommar more resonating and effective than 99% of the horror movies out there. If it doesn't scare you then too bad. There's a whole bunch ghouls and psycho killer movies out there for your liking.

What is the worst excuse you've heard someone give for not having money? Many moons ago I encountered a guy named Moses. Moses was short, squat and effeminate. He declared himself a staunch Catholic and whenever conversation among his male co workers included discussing even the most minor of obscenities, Moses would take offense and leave. He also was also the most despised among all of us guys working at the warehouse. Not because of his above mentioned traits but because of his notoriety of being a cheapskate. 'Hey Moses we're collecting $20 from everyone to buy Erica a gift for her birthday this Friday.’ Moses: 'Sorry but I already bought tickets for a cruise my church is having on Saturday.’ 'Hey Moses Petra is trying to raise funds for her mother's operation by selling BBQ tickets. It's $50 a ticket.’ Moses: 'Tell Petra I'm sorry but I already ate BBQ twice this month but I'll tell everyone at church to pray for her mother.’ These were the typical type of responses you'd get from Moses whenever money was involved. However the worst excuse he ever gave happened when a bunch of us went to a bar to hang out. We had just gotten paid. It was a gruelling month where we worked overtime every day and on the weekends. We all had some extra money and wanted to unwind with some beers, food and pool. We would all take turns and buy rounds of beers and after some time someone would offer to buy food. Everything was going fine and dandy. Practically the whole warehouse staff was there with the exception of older workers, those with family commitments etc and Moses. However, somewhere between the 3rd and 5th round Moses suddenly appeared in the bar and took a seat among us. By then we were all quite intoxicated and in great spirits. We cheered his arrival and patted him on the back. 'What do you want to drink Moses?’ Moses: 'I'm not a big drinker so a Carib Pilsner (Lite) beer is good for me.’ We all cheered Moses for not being such a tightwad and hanging out with us. A few rounds passed and food was bought and shared among us. Moses made himself at home with food, drink and hospitality. While eating we began to sober up and we became less vocal. Moses decided to use this opportunity to discuss his views on the Bible, his contributions to his church and the events it had in store for the weekend. This sobered us up even more. We then realized that the bastard never bought a single round for us. All he did was eat, drink, brag and preach to our credit. One of us diplomatically asked him when it is he was going to contribute to us by paying for a round of drinks. It was then that Moses uttered the most disgusting excuse for not spending money that I have ever heard: Moses: 'I try not to encourage anyone into a life of vice (alcoholism).’ There was a silence and chuckles from the few who thought Moses was making a joke.’ He had to be making a joke. He just sat and happily drank three beers with us. This fact was mentioned to him and he had an immediate response: Moses: 'I never asked for the beers. I came here to save souls.’ The little bugger wasn't joking. He said that he came with the intention to invite us to a shindig his church was having and only accepted the beers and food from us as a nice gesture. He honestly believed the bullshit that was coming out of his mouth. Before anyone could say anything else, Moses rose majestically from the centre of table like it was the Last Supper. He stoically announced that he had to leave and he hoped that we understood his message clear. He then walked unsteadily towards the exit; possibly a bit intoxicated but undoubtedly cheap, conceited and hypocritical. Needless to say the irritation we had for Moses developed into an intense dislike. He didn't last long in the warehouse though. Some time later he had missed several days of work. When he returned he had the excuse that he developed a hernia and had an operation. This was said with no medical records to his claim. Had he not been such a conniving, cheap bastard, our supervisor would've fought for him to keep his job. But in the end everyone was happy to see him go. Last I saw him, he worked as a merchandiser for an instant coffee distributor. I asked about his hernia. Moses: 'What hernia?’ Edit: Moses was a cheap bastard. There was a time when I tried to be the cheap in the bar with my friends and it led to painful results. Literally. Read it here.

Have you ever been on a date that was going so badly you walked out and left? When I was 18, an A-Level student in school, I took the bus and made friends with a quiet and pretty 12 year old girl. Nothing romantic happened. I acted like an older brother to her as I had sisters around that age. I made some silly jokes played some of my awful harmonica music and carried her to the public library for an hour or so and watched magazines. We didn't exchange numbers. It was just a harmless, spontaneous thing. Fast forward seven years later. I bump into her near the University. I'm 25 and she's 19. She gained a few pounds and is a bit more loud and outspoken than I remembered. However the flash back of our good time motivates me to ask her out to a movie the upcoming Saturday night. She agrees. On that day while waiting for her near the cinema I get a call. ‘We’re on our way.’ I wondered what she meant by ‘we’re.’ We agreed it was just her and I. I queried what she meant but she began to burst out in laughter to something somebody was saying. ‘Don’t worry it's another girl,’ she continued, ‘You’re getting to carry out two girls!’ I could hear the friend feeding her every word to say to me. She would then break out in laughter. I got highly irritated with their school girl shenanigans. Something told me to just hang up the phone and head back home. Another part of me said that that would be really bad of me to to do that. She is still just a teenager after all and who could blame her if maybe she felt more comfortable bringing a friend on a date with a guy she doesn't really know that well. I chose to go along with it. Wrong choice. When she and her friend came they came they acted like a pair of spoilt teenaged twats, mentally stuck at age 13. There was no proper introduction to one another. Everything was a joke and a giggle and the only time I seemed to exist was when we passed a fancy restaurant/bar and they wanted get some food and drinks (but couldn't afford it of course). Mentally I agreed to ditch them at the restaurant. I was not going to shell out a bunch of money for these clowns. I bought them their drinks and said I had to to go the washroom. While heading towards the restroom I was having second thoughts about whether this was the right thing to do. I was a wild and careless teenager once. I felt as though it was bad manners and etiquette to ditch my friend who was such a nice girl seven years ago. However I overhead them trying to get people's attention by practically shouting ‘You’re a bitch.’ ‘Oh my gosh no you're a bitch.’ ‘You're the biggest bitch on the planet.’ Etc etc and then bursting out in laughter. I told myself that they clearly didn't give a crap about manners and etiquette themselves. Returning from the washroom I slipped past them and out the building into the streets. I sent a hastily written text message saying that I had an emergency and needed to leave as soon as possible. I then jumped into a taxi and made my way home. I felt a pang of grief for my friend and how she changed for the worse but there was no way I was paying over $300 of my hard earned money to carry two rude and inconsiderate teenaged girls to go see a movie. At least they both got a drink out of it.

Have you actually ever heard someone say 'Do you know who I am?' indignantly? I was working pizza delivery when I took a call for an order. The person on the other end of the line was a guy called Kerron. He was a local media personality/comedian who went by the name Sunny Bling. He had ordered once before and that time he was quite pleasant and unassuming. Back then, he had referred to himself by his actual name Kerron and had no airs about himself. This time however he was Sunny Bling. He had just gotten his own evening talk show (Sunny @ Sundown) and his ego was now working overtime. 'You know who I am right?’ I said yes. He said that he didn't like how long his pizza took the last time he ordered and if he gets bad service he'd 'light us up’ on his show. I went to the manager and told her about his threat. She made me ignore several other customers who placed their orders before him so he could get a speedy delivery. When I reached his house, he was happy to get his order quickly and acted as though nothing happened. He didn't realize I was the guy who took the phone call as he probably assumed delivery guys didn't answer the phone. 'So are you still gonna “light us up" on your show?’ I said sombrely. He gave an awkward laugh and said no. His show has long been taken off the air. I honestly never met anyone who actually watched it.

My next door neighbours on the other hand aren't exactly good Samaritans to say the least: They DON'T socialize with anyone. No one even knows their names. They have one of the biggest houses in the street and they stick up in that house as though the minute they set foot on the road, like vicious cannibals the rest of the street would tear them to pieces. The never give anyone a ride. They've never invited anyone over for a beer or even glass of water. They don't hire anyone from the area for odd jobs. Have you ever walked out of an interview? I didn’t walk out but I sure pissed the hell out of them and made it as awkward as possible. A cable company was looking for part time sales reps for their dishes. I already had a full time job but was looking for a sideline. They arranged for the interview to be at 9am. I came an hour early to their main office. The security had a sour look in his face and asked me what it is I wanted. I told him my name and that I had an interview for 9am. He looked at me as though I was talking jibberish and simply muttered that he didn’t know anything about that and directed me to the payments/customer service area to ask one of the people there where to go. I ignored the queue and walked directly towards the agents and the guard comes frantically running to me like a mama bird protecting its nest. ‘Follow instructions,’ he grunted loudly, ‘I told you to join the line.’ I wanted to bark at him that he never told me that and that he had to be the worse security guard I’ve ever encountered in my life, but of course that wouldn’t bear well for my interview. Suddenly a short pretty young lady passing by looked at me and said, ‘You’re Mr. Williamson?’ I said yes and she told me to follow her to the waiting area. She was professional but I found her a tad too detached. She didn’t ask me about my trip here or apologize for the confusion or anything. She led me to a corridor and and told me to sit by a row of chairs and that the sales supervisor would see me in a moment. She went into a room and came out with a tall, attractive lady with curly hair who looked no older than 24. They passed me without a glance and I assumed that they were both sales people. While sitting there a bunch of people kept passing and no one seemed to recognize my existence. They were all salespeople and mostly men. They came in to use the company phones to try and close sales and make a bunch of noise laughing and hooting afterwards with one another. Something about the vibe of the place just didn’t sit well with me. Around 9:45am the two young ladies passed by me again and without a word went back into the room they had left prior. A few minutes later the shorter one came out and called me in. She said the supervisor was ready to see me. I came in and saw a simple table in front of me where the tall girl sat with her fingers clasped staring at me. The shorter one sat to the side of her and they beckoned me to sit. Just looking at them I could sense that they were ladies who treated themselves well. Their clothes looked expensive, hair, nails and skin well treated, designer handbags etc. They were both very attractive and they knew it. The taller one proceeded to talk about sales and asked what the word ‘sale’ means to me. I kept mentioning how I prefer customer satisfaction rather than soliciting a sale and each time I did that she paused and reverted back to talking about how this job is concerned with hard selling and customer satisfaction can’t come if you don’t have customers. ‘We focus on sales only’ the shorter one chimed in. In my mind I sarcastically said to myself, ‘That’s a shocker.’ They then started discussing targets. They showed me a list of all the packages they were selling. They wanted to get the most expensive packages sold because they believe that people weren’t aware of how much better these were. They wanted to know if I had a problem focusing on selling only the expensive packages this month. They wanted me to lie and say basic packages were unavailable at the moment and that the next month I can sell basic like normal. I was starting to find them and this whole place tiresome. They clearly had values different from mine and I could see myself having spats with them in no time. I decided that I wanted out. However I wasn’t one to walk out on interviews as word gets around in this tiny country. I started asking about pay. ‘Commissions’ the taller one said. ‘Aren’t there any paying jobs,’ I replied, ‘With like a salary.’ They both looked at each other and the taller one replied that there were but that was a different division. I started telling them how I bought a dish from this company some years ago and how I thought it was garbage. I then said that my skills were so good that I could sell thousands of those garbage dishes to people who didn’t even have televisions. They both remained silent. I then said that I only worked on weekends and I don’t answer calls between 8 - 4 pm. They both looked at each other. ‘So Mr. Williamson’ the taller one said with a smile, ‘That’s the end of our interview. Thank you for your time and we’ll be contacting you before the end of the week.’ Without bothering to shake hands I headed out of the room like a man with a bladder control problem. Regardless to say I got a formal email from them a week later civilly explaining that I was unsuccessful with the interview.

What is the most obnoxious thing you have seen someone do at the grocery store? Our local version of Costco is called PriceSmart. Isn't that a clever name? A lady in front of me, at the queue to cash, decided she was cleverer than me and all the fine people employed at PriceSmart. To shop at PriceSmart you have to be a member. You do this by purchasing a membership subscription card which allows you a year of membership. For the average Joe it's a tad costly ($265 TT) but the savings you get shopping at PriceSmart, more than makes up for it. I'm a very economical shopper and I tend to purchase only the bare necessities and would treat myself to something nice only once in a blue moon. This lady in front of me had a cart piled with groceries and also several treats ranging from frozen salmon burgers, Lindt, Toblerone and Mars chocolates, smoked almonds and ribs. Clearly she was not a poor lady. When we neared the cashier she suddenly turned around to stare me in the eyes. This is the conversation that followed. Lady: You don't mind if I use your card right? Me: For what? Lady: To cash. Me: You don't have a card? Lady: No. Can't afford it. I then stared at her pile of groceries tethering at the edge of her trolley. Her bottle of Grey Goose Vodka was almost $300TT but she ‘couldn't afford' a $200TT (at that time) membership. Me: It's only $200 for the membership and it takes just a minute. I saw her face suddenly transform into a look of complete irritation. It was as if I was asking her for the favour. Lady: I don't have the money right now. I just told you. People need to help each other. Me: Well I can't lend you my card. Lady: Why? Me: Because I don't know you. Lady: You need to know me to help me? At that point I remained silent. I didn't want to call her out for attempting to use random strangers for her financial convenience. I didn't want to argue that I spent my hard earned money on this membership and she ought to make that sacrifice also rather than gorge on her four rotisserie chickens as it was not my place to say. Instead she went to the man in front of her, giving him a sad story of how she just lost her card and this stuff is for her mother. The guy took the bait and lent her his card. She then stared at me as if to say, 'Got anything to say now?’ Clearly this wasn't the first time she did this and it definitely wasn't going to be the last. Some people may not see the big deal of what happened there but to me she is trash: a selfish and cheap opportunist. She is a leech on PriceSmart (who generates a profit from membership fees) and on the good people around her who make the necessary sacrifices for the greater good. Edit 24.11.21 Whoa. 5K upvotes. I always thought venting anger never got people anywhere. Was wise enough to avoid that lady's scheme. Was not so wise as a teenager when I fell for a bootlegger's silly scam. Click here to read all about it.

What was your cringiest moment with a boss? Ms. B was a former supervisor of mine in a Government building I worked. She was a lady in her early 50’s. She was a nice person but was an eccentric and an introvert to the core. When things were slow she would stay isolated in her office, playing chess online or taking a nap. When she came out of her office her only conversation would usually be short, irritable grumbles about random stuff that annoyed her about the job and the typical ‘can’t wait for the weekend/payday’ talk. Then she would return to her idle privacy. Mary, a co-worker of mine, observing that our supervisor had so much free time on her hands, decided to enroll in an online course. Mary thought it fair she perform her duties during the morning and after lunch work on her online studies. Ms. B began observing this and one day, while stepping out to grab lunch, made a snide comment towards Mary’s direction: ‘Lunch break is just an hour. I don’t want to report people who like to come to work and do their own thing.’ Ms. B’s grumble was directed towards Mary but in a most blunt and condescending manner. Mary, being a woman of passion, could not take such a hypocritical statement without taking some kind of action. For days, she plotted on how she would give Ms. B a piece of her mind; how dare she? Ms. B who does practically nothing, making accusations of others doing as such. They say it’s only thieves who are always paranoid that everyone wants to steal from them. Such and such was the rantings of Mary for that evening. The day Mary decided she was going to confront Ms. B about the statement, something strange happened. Ms. B, in a seemingly good mood, had come out of her office and was helping visitors and getting involved in the day to day operations of junior staff like myself and Mary. Then Mary observed something that made a Cheshire grin spread across her face. ‘Elijah,’ she said, ‘Look at Ms. B’s pants.’ I looked. Ms. B was wearing a beige colored work-pants. Nothing seemed out of the ordinary until I observed that there was a wet, red spot observable from the back, around the crotch area. I stared aghast. Ms. B didn’t seem to notice her period came down on her and clearly had no protection against such an event. She must’ve assumed that her menopause came to an end and periods were now a thing of the past for her. Some of the people she was dealing with seemed to have observed her predicament also but looked as though they felt too awkward to say anything about it. I looked at Mary and said, ‘We should tell her about it.’ ‘No,’ Mary replied, ‘Not right now.’ Mary waited until the very last visitor left the building and the usual evening lull began. Ms. B went into her office and closed the door. I watched as Mary went up to the door, knocked and entered. ~~~~~~~~~~~ Ten minutes later Ms. B, with all her belongings on her, sped past me while uttering, ‘I have to deal with a matter.’ She hastily left the building. Mary told me that when she explained the situation to Ms. B, the look that came upon Ms. B’s face was nothing short of the deepest dread and horror. That for a second she wore the facial expression of a convict at the gallows. I could not help but empathize with the level of cringe Ms. B must've felt on her way back home. Mary got her poetic justice. If she were really mean she could’ve spread the word about the incident through the entire building but the slight torture was enough. Mary and Ms. B began to develop a meaningful relationship after the incident. In other words they started to scratch each other’s back. Maybe it was some sort of neurotic subconscious agreement they both made, as in reminding each other ‘You got me covered right?’ Maybe the situation gave Ms. B a slice of humble pie? I don’t know. What I do know is that to this day I don’t understand women.

Do biracial people ever pick their white side and identify as white? Sigh The above photo shows five mixed raced men of varying ethnic makeup, myself included. Which one do you think would be the most likely to identify as ‘white?’ If you chose the guy on the far left, congratulations, you have a talent to point out the obvious. That's my cousin. We all are. He is mixed race but looks ‘white.’ Growing up he never picked his white side, society picked it for him. Trinidad has a very small ‘Caucasian’ minority and as such he has been identified as one by the public and has grown to accept and embrace that identification. In the real world nobody wants to hear what you identify yourself as. You don't pick whether you are white or black, society does. If you try to challenge society’s label and argue that you are white when you look black or that you are black when you look white, you end up losing a lot of time, wasting a lot of energy and not to mention, irritating a lot of people with a topic that is intrinsically pointless. So whether you identify as white, black, male, female, young, old, binary, non-binary, here's some news for you: No one cares. No one is really listening. Nothing has changed.

What type of women should you never date? An acquaintance of an acquaintance of mine was a moderately attractive girl. We all attended the University of the West Indies as Evening students and shared the same course in Management Accounting. I'll refer to her as Sarah. Sarah wasn't the brightest bulb but she had a seemingly friendly disposition and was good with people….well, she was good with just males to be honest. Because she enjoyed a lifestyle of getting into the best parties as a 'promo girl’ (attractive girls dressed in skimpy clothing hired to sell/give away alcoholic beverages) her studies suffered. The night before the final exam she approached me in desperation explaining that she did poorly in her midterm and wasn't ready for this exam. She asked that I come over to her place and we both do an 'all-nighter.’ Being as clever as she was with the opposite sex, she made sure to sumptuously stress on and repeat the word 'all-nighter’ as she was aware it sent erotic images into my mind. Despite originally planning to get some good sleep that night I went over to her apartment. She then served me hot chocolate and cookies whilst moving around in a rather eye popping nightgown. I sat and calmly explained accounting stuff but when 3am reached and I realized that she couldn't get the grasp of the first two chapters, I knew this was going to be a lost cause. I was ready to go home and sleep. However, she rubbed my legs tenderly and gave me puppy dog eyes, explaining how desperate she was to pass this exam. I've always been something of a nice-guy and taking advantage of women in desperation has never been my thing. I asked that she buy lunch after the exam in exchange for staying up all night. We continued and as the wee hours of morning started to break the stillness of the dark, she started getting rather irritable and I condescended to teaching her how to do up legit looking accounting tables and fill them with stuff that's supposed to be there. In my heart I knew she was going to fail. When 8am arrived we were both exhausted. I went home to have a bath and change clothes to ready myself for the exam at 11am. I sat the exam and found it a tad challenging but manageable. However when I glanced back at Sarah her face looked as though she was trying to solve the meaning of life. After the exam ended and everyone filed out the building I headed towards Sarah who bore a disturbed countenance and seemed to be trying to avoid me. I inquired as to her exam experience and she said that it was very difficult and that she didn't even finish half the paper and was certain to fail. I pretended that this wasn't the case. Pondering about the lunch she promised I asked, 'So what's for lunch?’ 'I'm so tired,' she said, 'I need some sleep. See you later.’ She then pulled out her phone as though she just got a phone call and walks the opposite direction from me. Instinctively I know that she is pretending to talk on the phone as a means to get away from me and the topic of her promise to by me lunch. I realize I've been shafted but I tell myself that failing an exam after staying up all night can bring the worst out in anybody. The following semester I'm in the library doing an assignment for marks towards my Statistics midterm. I get a call. I answer it and it's Sarah. I had never even given her my number before. In her typical sugary tones she questions as to how I'm doing and how she doesn't see me around anymore and how I'm so smart she thought I had already finished University with first class honours and yadee yadee yaa. I listen with patience to her insincere flattery knowing fully well that she's looking for some kind of favour. 'Are you doing the Stats course this semester?’ 'Yes,' I stoically replied. I listen as she pretends that this is news to her. She gushes about how it is such a wonderful coincidence and that she is also doing the same course. I already knew this because in the class I had already seen her name signed in the role even though I never witnessed her attending a single class. Clearly she got some naive manchild to sign for her attendance. 'I'm having problems with the stats assignment….you know the one that is due tomorrow. Can I meet you somewhere? I remember how much you helped me for Accounts. I really wish I had a decent, smart guy like you in my life…’ It dawns on me that all the time she really was a deceitful opportunist. I smile as a great idea pops into my head. ‘Are you anywhere near the library?’ 'Yeah,' she replied, 'I'm actually right outside.’ Clearly she had plotted her little scheme very efficiently to the point where she obtained my phone number and location at an instant. 'I'm in the third floor in the carrel in the south west corner.’ I wasn't actually at the south west carrel. However I go to it and take out a folder page. On this I scribble a note and then I fold it and leave on the desk. 'Okay I'm coming now,' Sarah says in an aggressively determined manner. She is so determined she keeps me on the line to ensure that she doesn't lose me to circumstance. 'I gotta leave in a bit,' I tell Sarah. 'You gotta hurry.’ In reality I'm actually gathering my belongings to leave the library. Sarah explains that she has entered 3rd floor while I'm collecting my book bag outside the library. 'I'm at the carrel!’ Sarah tells me with a hint of exasperation as she sees I'm not there. 'Where are you?’ 'You took too long,' I say trying to hide my laughter, 'But I left the answers in a sheet of paper on the desk. Do you see the paper?’ 'Yes,' she exclaims excitedly, as she is happy that she seemingly got what she wanted without having to give up anything. 'Make sure that's the right paper,’ I say, 'See if it has my name on it.’ 'Okay,' she says solemnly and after a few seconds I hear silence and then she hangs up the phone on me. What she sees is something that looks like this: So in response to the above question. Never date any women remotely similar to the above mentioned Sarah.

What are the best episodes of the original Twilight Zone TV series? I think it's impossible to choose the best episodes of The Twilight Zone, however I can describe one of the most severely underrated. The Incredible World of Horace Ford No it's not scary. It's not spooky. It's barely even eerie. It's a profound reflection of changes of the past, childhood nostalgia and the how our ego manipulates many of us to believe 'things were so much better back then.’ *Spoiler Alert* Horace Ford is a gifted toy designer employed by a commercial toymaker. His talents stem from his ability to delve into the mind of a child and understand what appeals to them. However he's been having a midlife crisis of which, rather than brooding on the acceptance of incoming old age, he instead has mentally reverted back to that of a nine year old. He becomes silly and frivolous, neglects his job and throws tantrums whenever his employer and wife calmly try to reason with him. When he does open up about his problem he feverishly reminisces about the past, his old pals and how much simpler and better life was back then. His wife and boss try to explain to him that he is possibly fatigued and that he just needs to rest so he could get over this silly phase. Angered by their indifference he walks off his job and is magically transported back to his childhood. At first he is thrilled but gradually he is horrified to discover that his childhood was but a collection of poverty, overcrowded and dirty streets and his 'pals’ were mostly thuggish street urchins who bullied him. He is then transported back to the present where he confides to his wife what he saw and she reminds him that his childhood was actually traumatic but his ego manipulated him into believing it was great as a form of coping. He accepts the present and resumes his job, happy to find some closure in his life. Why I think it's great. Everyday we all hear a comment, whether online or in person of how much better things were in whatsoever decade. And so on and so on. Some of these comments are justified but many of them are coping mechanisms in regards to personal failures i.e. 'It's not that my life is a disappoinment. Life for everyone now is a disappoinment and here's the reasons why (refer to list above).’ I myself was guilty at some point of thinking like Horace Ford. That is until I chanced upon some old photos of me during childhood and it suddenly dawned on me things were better in a few aspects, but worse in many others. But no matter how bad things were, for many the ego would always try to romanticize the past and make it seem superior to the present. Baby boomers always talk about how great the 60s were despite the obvious issues of the period and their parents would speak highly of the 30s and 40s despite World War 2. This episode gives so much food for thought towards the question, 'Were things really all that great back then?’

What single moment in a film was an example of some of the greatest acting you've ever seen from an individual or ensemble cast? The Last Picture Show (1971) is, in my honest opinion, the greatest piece of ensemble acting I've ever seen. I would go as far and say that this is one of the rare moments in cinema where a certain magic takes over and the movie takes unexplainable life of its own. It is one of the few movies that can move me to tears even if I were to watch it reading captions on mute. The acting, both vocal and non-vocal, is that good. But before I go on a rant, for those who don't know about the film, it revolves around various characters living in a dusty, dying small town in Texas. Life for practically everyone is uneventful and everyone shares a certain yearning; for the older generation it is of good times gone by and things that could've been, for the younger generation, a deep desire to escape the monotony and perpetual routine of the life of their parents and forefathers. Every major character wants to make some kind of difference in their lives and escape the stagnancy that surrounds them; some in constructive and helpful ways and some through seeking attention and infamy. The rest of the characters just seem to accept their fate and live for the rare special moments of feeling some sort of fleeting joy, a connection or purpose in life. The titular ‘Last Picture Show’ symbolises the only escape for most of these individuals in the form of a crumbling local cinema that is about to be closed down by its benevolent but sickly owner who himself represents the life of the town. As such the film is a meditation on loneliness, yearning, alienation and the desperate desire human beings have to connect with others by whatever means possible, a desire that becomes more intense the more isolated society is from the outside world. I would safely assume that all the actors read either the script (and/or the magnificent book by Larry McMurtry) understood the themes, did the assignment and delivered. Practically every scene is like a masterclass in acting. My personal favourite being the final scene where the teenaged protagonist Sonny returns, dejected and alienated, to the middle aged Ruth Popper. She herself has long suffered such feelings and they both share a moment, finally understanding one another; older and younger generation, with the gentle touch of hands. Around them the wind howls non stop in the background while the strain of the same old country songs, same old ads and same outdated radio shows play on the transistor behind them. This serves to remind them that this is their lives and there is little to nothing they can do to change it. This is a film that I believe anyone who lives (or has lived) in a location forgotten by the rest of the general population can relate to, regardless what part of world it is.

What is the worst thing you have seen a teacher do? In Trinidad we have problems pronouncing our ‘th’s. If you are an English teacher it makes sense to speak the Queen's English eloquently or at least make an effort to pronounce your 'th’ in front of your class. That's not the case for Ms. Bentham. Or as she likes to call herself Ms. Bend-Tom. Ms. Bentham was recently informed that she had to present a video session of how she conducts her class. This was for credit towards her Diploma in Education or Dip-Ed as teachers like to call it here. Only with her Dip-Ed could she be promoted to a Teacher II. As such, Ms. Bentham was very high strung about recording the perfect classroom session. She stayed up all night creating a beautiful PowerPoint presentation full of animations, sound clips and videos. She got some excellent speakers borrowed to capture crisp sound and had another English teacher friend bring a video camera on a tripod to film her. She even went as far as giving the class 10% towards their final grade to simply 'behave themselves’ and ask/answer questions. She was very particular about the event the day filming was to begin. She wore her best wig and her polka dotted dress that revealed her shapely figure. She had a team of teacher friends guarding the door of the classroom to ensure no mischievous child outside sabotages her film by yelling inside or switching off the lights and running. Everything went according to plan. The PowerPoint was well done, the students were well behaved, the video was filmed without a hitch. All went to plan, all except for one thing: Ms. Bentham herself. She forgot that the whole point of English class is for students to speak and comprehend proper English. Something Ms. Bentham never practiced herself in her job and personal life. This was most prevalent in her Slothy the Sloth story, which she read in front the class to demonstrate descriptive writing. Here's how she told it: 'Slutty was a fat, tree hanging slut that lived in Brazil. Like most sluts she had long claws that looked like nails, a round head, long limbs and was covered in fur. She was laziest slut of all the sluts in South America. In fact the reason the word slut is synonymous with idleness is because of…’ Ms. Bentham stopped because some of the students were giggling. She looked up to see her English teacher friends staring at her in comic disbelief. However she didn't understand what was the problem. She barked at the students to keep quiet. One of the teachers gestured and mouthed softly, 'Say SLOTH… SLOTH’ Ms. Bentham thought that was the cue to go ahead. ‘……is because of the renowned laziness of Slutty the slut. Some would say that she had a wide stupid, smile and barely moved so that other animals would wonder if she were dead, but that's how most sluts behave… There was an uproar of laughter and Ms. Bentham again became confused, until finally the best student in her class rose and explained to her, 'Miss, they're laughing because you're pronouncing it wrong. It's SLOTH not SLUT. A sloth is an animal, a slut is a woman who has a lot of promiscuous sex.’ Ms. Bentham then had the crippling realization of the sheer embarrassment of her faux pas. Not only did she use the word ‘slut’ repeatedly in her presentation but she was corrected by her own student, and on film to boot. She felt humiliated and her anger was suddenly directed to the student whom she felt was purposely trying to embarass her. 'Candice, please pick up your belongings and go to the Principal's Office. I will not have you using such obscene language in my class.’ The students and even some of the teachers broke out in laughter. My all time vote for the worse thing I've ever seen a teacher do.

What is the best case of “You just picked a fight with the wrong person” that you've witnessed? Some years ago I worked in a pretty rough school in a pretty rough neighborhood. I worked in the school library which wasn’t really a popular hangout for the dangerous kids. At least that's what I thought. There were these two boys, Jesse and Adrian who would usually remain in the library well after school hours. Jesse (16) came from a nearby projects. He was athletic and strong. He worked construction on weekends to help his family. He was around 6’2 and sinewy. Just imagine a younger Deontay Wilder without the facial hair and you had Jesse. Adrian was 16 also. He was 5’9, stocky and a video game enthusiast. He wore glasses, had a silly smile with a chipped front tooth and a prominent paunch, quite unusual for a boy his age. Just imagine Emmitt Smith with glasses and you had Adrian. Both of them couldn’t be more opposite. Jesse was thoughtful and polite. He didn’t talk much but when he did it was usually of a philosophical nature. He had a lot of ambition and was determined to make it in life. Adrian was aloof and untethered. He talked a lot and when he did it was always a lot of shit. It seemed all he knew in life were action movies, anime and video games. He had zero ambition. He cared nothing for his future, let alone his school work. Jesse came after school to the library to spend quality time with his girlfriend every once in a while. Adrian came to the library every day to play Halo and Quake III on the library computers with his gamer buddies or by himself. Jesse would come and chat with his girl in private. He never bothered anyone and if we saw any handsy-pansy going on we spoke to him about it and he would obey. Adrian would sometimes be a nuisance. Video games were not allowed but we would give the boys a chance after school hours if they behaved themselves and obeyed us. Adrian would usually overdo it and have us shut off the computers and send him home. One particular evening Jesse was alone in the library studying for the upcoming end of term exams. His girlfriend and him were going through some problems that day so he was alone and not in the best of moods. Adrian came solo as well to play video games. We told him no. He then told us he wanted to finish his assignment on the computer. We allowed him but every few minutes we took our eyes off him he would put on his video games. We could not allow this especially as exams drew near. We told him if we caught him one more time he would not only have to leave but be banned for the rest of the term. All of this childishness from Adrian was starting to get on Jesse's nerves. Some minutes after our final warning Jesse observed that Adrian was playing a juvenile video game from a web browser. He had the web page minimized at a corner of the screen to hide it from being seen. Jesse took it upon himself to deal with Adrian. Before we could say anything Jesse grabbed the mouse from Adrian’s hand and flung it aside. He then rolled Adrian and his chair away from the computer and spun it around to face him. Jesse looked as though he was going to pull Adrian off the chair by the collar. It was Jesse's biggest mistake. He severely underestimated how strong Adrian was. Adrian rose from his seat and fired two tremendous hooks, left and right, onto Jesse’s cheek and head. I could feel the power from those punches by just looking at them and I knew that the fight was over before it even began. Jesse struggled to keep to his feet and attempted to wrestle Adrian to the ground. It was no good. The punches had him dazed. Adrian easily shook him off and was about to land some more until he saw myself and my coworker coming to subdue him. Adrian had momentarily transformed from a goofy nerd into Mike Tyson for a few seconds. He left the scene immediately. We had to subdue Jesse who claimed that he was going after Adrian to teach him a lesson for the ‘sucker punch.’ We all knew that was just talk. Jesse didn't want to face that beast again. No one in their right mind would. Jesse didn't report the matter and requested the same of us, clearly due to embarrassment. With his naturally forgiving nature Jesse had no hard feelings and the boys developed a mutual respect after. Jesse graduated from the school with some decent grades and works as a successful salesman and party promoter. Adrian graduated from the school with nothing but a superb left and right hook. I truly hope he used his power to good use.

What is the biggest culture shock you have ever faced? In Aberystwyth, Wales, a group of us Trinidadians went to town for shopping. Trinis are notorious jaywalkers and back home, in most instances, we pay little attention to traffic lights as pedestrians. We were at a traffic light at a rather low-traffic road. One of us observed a store that she wanted to check out. In typical Trini fashion she looked left and right and saw that incoming traffic was several yards away and quickly dashed across the road. She then waited for us to come after her on the other side. An older Welsh man looked at us and said solemnly, ‘You can’t cross until you see the little green man!’ We looked at each other wondering if this was some kind of Welsh humour. I pretended to chuckle at the joke. We then looked left and right and dashed across the road as well. Looking behind us we could see the old man and a group of other pedestrians staring at us in anger and disbelief, murmuring among themselves. I wondered what was up with these people. Why didn’t they cross? The road was clear. What was up with the old guy talking about the ‘little green man?’ It was when I glanced at the traffic light it dawned on me. The ‘WALK’ light had finally come on. Edit: This is not an effort to make fun of UK and/or Welsh culture but rather demonstrate my appreciation for the respect for order and rule-abiding that my friends and I witnessed. However, for all the commenters claiming that the author is lying and then saying 'I'm from the UK and we don't care about/have jaywalking rules’ or 'I visited Aberystwyth and I never saw anyone get upset over jaywalkers’ Please keep your scepticism to yourself. What is the strangest complaint you have received at your job? Some years ago while counting down the last few minutes before my shift ended in a public library, a young woman came to the information desk with an ennraged look on her face. Lady: Can someone please tell me where the Spanish classes are? I've been on all the floors and no one seems to know what I'm talking about. Me: Sorry miss but those aren't Spanish classes. The Spanish Embassy has been having a series of public talks every Wednesday at 5 - 6 pm on the third floor discussing the Latin American economy. We simply allow them to use our conference room on the third floor. Lady: Are you listening to what I'm saying? I left work early to come to these Spanish classes. Where are the people for the Spanish class? Me: I'm sorry miss but we really don't know. We simply give the Embassy access to our conference room. You might want to call the number they left on the advertisement. Lady: So you're saying this is your library, where you work, but you have no idea what's going on? Me: We know all what is going on in regards to our public services but the Embassy's program is something external. Any complaints about the program can be addressed to the Embassy's website. Lady: Typical lazy government worker mentality…So you're saying you have no knowledge of what is going on in your own building? Me: This is actually not our building. Several government departments are housed in this building besides the library. Would you like me to call the Embassy for you? Lady: You've wasted my time already. It's already 5:30pm. I mean does it feel good to you to be getting paid for nothing? What's the point of this library? I want to speak to your manager. I was about to explain to her that we don't have ‘managers’ but librarians when she whips out her cell phone and shows a screenshot of a Facebook post advertising the Embassy's program. Me: Miss. I'm sorry but that post shows that the program ends April 24th, which was two weeks ago… Lady: ……so you….this is so unprofessional…..a big freaking library and you can't call people and tell them that the Spanish class program has finished. I want to speak to the manager. This is unacceptable. It was at this point I decided I that I no longer waste my time with this lady's nonsensical complaint.

What is an unpopular opinion you hold? Self-Help Books Can Actually Ruin Your Life Especially if you come from a developing country. Have you ever sat and pondered as to the staggering amount of self-help authors there are out there? It seems every week someone is recommending to you some brand new, groundbreaking, best selling title that eschews a whole new perspective on how to view the world and live your life. The problem with 99% of the authors: Are they really living their dreams? Or are they making a living selling dreams? Moulding a life of success, solely based on easily digestible tips, hints and formulae is like solving advanced level algebra, whilst riding a roller coaster, using only your knowledge of multiplication tables. The knowledge can help….you probably might get the most simple problems correct……but it would be ridiculous to think that you would be able to solve all your problems in that manner, under those unique circumstances. These are people living in dire poverty in India. What can I do to help them out of this financial rut?….. I know! Think and Grow Rich by Napoleon Hill A lonely, mentally unhinged taxi driver… That's easy. The Road Less Travelled and How to Win Friends and Influence People. A wealthy but socially and emotionally void and suicidal philanthropist. Hmm. That's a tough one….The Alchemist by Paolo Coelho and you can throw in The Prophet by Gibran as well. Nothing cures rich-man depression more than obscure but romanticised Eastern parables and fables. Ok, so it's foolish to try and live according to a self help book, but how can I ruin my life simply by seeking advice? In every job that I've worked, every year there's always that one newly employed guy who is all jacked up from reading a lifetime's supply of self help books. He is always brimming with confidence and eager to pin his obstacles against the ropes and send failure scattering with his 2000 watt grin. He hates to hear no and scorns to see people second guessing themselves. He wants to take on all life's challenges and has a Napoleon Hill or Robert Kiyosaki quote ready for every situation. Then something inexplicable happens. Something gradually builds up, registers in his subconscious and overflows upon his ego. It usually takes the form of this mental conversation. 'Wait a minute. I've done everything the book advised me to. I've followed the instructions to the hilt…….yet I'm not seeing the results.’ He hasn't been promoted by his supervisor, rather his supervisor has been taking credit for his own efforts and is getting the promotion instead. Despite constantly showing support and empathy, his wife is even more nagging and helpless than when he first met her. His dedication to go above and beyond with the customer now has him doing the workload of all the lazy and incompetent coworkers around him, who still draw the same salary. He gets the lion's share of verbal abuse from disgruntled customers who rather voice their issues with him rather than the incompetent coworkers. His small business as a landscaper is suffering because his fair price is being exploited whilst mediocre landscapers are charging abominably overpriced rates and are getting more work than him. What the hell is happening here? He followed some great and timeless advice. He just forget to put in one small factor in his equation. His personal environment. His ever changing, ever complex, personal environment. The variable that if included onto his scientific calculator would produce the answer E or 'Error.’ In developing countries likes Trinidad, using US or English or German translated or Dutch translated or any developed country self help books can cause ruin your life because the environment is so different. In developing countries: These are all factors that contradict with what he read in his books and come only through experience. Had he been all the wiser he would've known that not every bit of advice in his self help books could be applied to his unique situation and environment. To make matters worse nowadays, everybody is a self help author and rather than have synchronized, compatible, time tested advice, we have polarising, wishy-washy, one-size-fits-all concoctions and psudo-psychological, parabolic gibberish. Basically, self help authors write anecdotes that's easy to understand, easy to apply and appealing to the majority. Malcolm Gladwell: You have within you an instinct to know when something 'feels’ like a rip-off. Jay Shetty: Think like a monk. Deepak Chopak: Thinking is like brain chemistry. Steve Harvey: Act like a lady, think like a man Paolo Coelho: The universe…
